fields.advanced_explanation: an action-denoting source verb underlies the form; the annexed-complement reading requires a transitive source verb; the intensive reading requires habitual or defining behaviour, not a single event
fields.beginner_explanation: Introduces the intensive agent templates as a graded strengthening of the plain agent noun, covering habitual, professional and excessive performance, and shows that these forms keep the government properties of the verb they come from.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: assigning a فَعيل-shaped word to the wrong class; reading the taa on the intensive template as feminine
fields.contrast_or_transfer: plain agent noun versus intensive: degree and habituality; intensive versus quality adjective on the shared فَعيل shape
fields.intermediate_explanation: isolate the root; verify that the source verb denotes an action rather than a bare state; select the intensive template
fields.prerequisite_statement: the bare-triliteral agent noun; the quality-adjective templates from the previous lesson; annexation and genitive marking
fields.recognition_cue: doubled middle radical with a long-alif ending in an agentive sense; prefixed mim with kasra plus a long alif, read as a person rather than a tool; a long waw or long ya in the second syllable with an agentive or attributive sense
fields.tutor_destination: strong: degree-scale drills over one root, and forced-choice drills between the intensive and the quality adjective on the shared template

fields.advanced_explanation: the role exists only with a passive verb; the promoted element must be the element that was the direct object; a phrasal filler is available only when there is no patient to promote
fields.beginner_explanation: Turns the previous lesson's morphology into syntax: names the argument that occupies the subject position of a passive verb, fixes its case and its agreement behaviour, and enumerates the categories of expression that can fill that position, including cases where nothing overt fills it. Closes a morphology module with a governance topic.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: leaving the promoted element in the accusative; failing to agree the passive verb with its deputy agent
fields.contrast_or_transfer: active sentence against its passive counterpart, argument by argument; accusative patient against nominative deputy agent
fields.intermediate_explanation: confirm the verb is passive from its melody before assigning any role; locate the nominative nominal and assign it the deputy-agent role; check verb agreement against that nominal
fields.prerequisite_statement: L4.M1.06 passive melodies in both tenses; case marking and its exponents; verb-subject agreement including the non-human plural rule
fields.recognition_cue: a verb carrying a passive melody together with a nominative nominal and no expressed agent; agreement on the passive verb tracking the nominative nominal rather than any following phrase; feminine singular agreement with a non-human plural subject
fields.tutor_destination: strong for conversion drills and for role-identification drills over running text; drills must include intransitive passives with phrasal fillers and covert-pronoun cases, and must not reward reading a prepositional phrase as an agent

fields.advanced_explanation: the sound or broken plural of the head noun must be known lexically and cannot be derived reliably; agreement targets must be identified before any of them can be converted; the case of the whole phrase determines which dual ending is selected
fields.beginner_explanation: Teaches number change as a whole-clause operation rather than a change to one word, requiring the learner to propagate a singular, dual or plural choice through the verb, the pronouns, the adjectives and the demonstratives at once.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: using a plural verb form ahead of a plural subject; interchanging the two dual endings
fields.contrast_or_transfer: nominative dual ending against the accusative and genitive dual ending; human plural agreement against non-human plural agreement
fields.intermediate_explanation: identify the head noun and its intended new number; convert the head noun, choosing the sound or broken plural stored for that lexeme; convert the demonstrative
fields.prerequisite_statement: singular, dual and plural noun morphology; sound and broken plural formation; the pronoun inventory
fields.recognition_cue: read the number off the head noun first, then check each dependent for a matching form; use the dual ending to distinguish nominative from the other two cases; check word order before judging a singular verb with a plural subject to be an error
fields.tutor_destination: high — whole-clause conversion is a strong drill format because a single missed dependent makes the item fail, but the drill must score each dependent separately to be diagnostic

fields.advanced_explanation: the number-agreement suppression holds only while the verb precedes its agent; the taught patterns use past-tense verbs with overt nominal agents; the object rule assumes a transitive verb with an expressed object
fields.beginner_explanation: Introduces the verb-initial sentence as the second sentence type, names its verb and agent constituents, fixes the default constituent order, assigns nominative to the agent and accusative to the object, and states the order-conditioned agreement behaviour of the verb. Ends by contrasting the two sentence types as alternative framings of one situation.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: using a plural verb form before a plural agent in verb-initial order; omitting the feminine exponent on a verb whose agent is feminine
fields.contrast_or_transfer: verb-initial versus noun-initial sentence type; agent (nominative doer) versus object (accusative undergoer)
fields.intermediate_explanation: place the verb first; read the agent's gender and select the verb's gender exponent accordingly; keep the verb singular irrespective of the agent's number while the verb precedes
fields.prerequisite_statement: the noun-initial sentence and its two slots; the case names and their exponents; past-tense verb forms as vocabulary
fields.recognition_cue: the first element is a finite verb; the immediately following nominal is nominative and is the doer; the verb is singular even where the following agent is plural
fields.tutor_destination: very high — the order-conditioned agreement asymmetry is a compact rule with a single high-frequency error, and both correct and incorrect forms are generable mechanically

fields.advanced_explanation: subjunctive assignment holds only for the masdar-forming role; the lightened reading requires a preceding predicate of knowledge or certainty plus one of its following markers; the explanatory reading requires a preceding speech/signalling predicate that is not introducing a direct quotation
fields.beginner_explanation: Trains four-way role disambiguation of the short subordinating particle أنْ, using what precedes it and what follows it as joint evidence, and connects each role to its governance consequence (subjunctive assignment, no assignment, or none at all).
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: Reading the masdar-forming role where the lightened role holds, typically when a negator follows.; Leaving the verb in the indicative after the masdar-forming role.
fields.contrast_or_transfer: masdar-forming (assigns subjunctive, substitutable by a verbal noun) versus lightened (assigns nothing, marker-signalled); masdar-forming (followed by subjunctive) versus explanatory (followed by imperative or prohibition)
fields.intermediate_explanation: Look right first: subjunctive imperfective points to the masdar-forming role; negator/perfective/future/jussive-negator points to the lightened role; imperative points to the explanatory role; a past verb after a temporal head points to the expletive role.; Look left second: volition/attempt/fear verbs, knowledge/certainty verbs, speech/signalling verbs and temporal heads each bias a different role.; Apply the substitution test: replace the particle plus verb by an explicit verbal noun; success confirms the masdar-forming role.
fields.prerequisite_statement: mood marking on the imperfective, including subjunctive marking by ending-letter loss; explicit versus interpreted verbal nouns and their positional case; the heavy emphatic particle and its accusative subject noun
fields.recognition_cue: mood of the following imperfective (subjunctive marking, including loss of the plural/feminine ending letter); presence of a negator, perfective marker, future marker or jussive negator directly after the particle; presence of an imperative or prohibition directly after the particle
fields.tutor_destination: high — a clean four-way forced choice with mechanical left/right evidence, well suited to drills that require the learner to name the evidence and the resulting mood.
fields.unresolved_notice: rival analyses: whether the expletive role is truly meaning-neutral or contributes an aspectual/emphatic nuance is presented both ways within the lesson

fields.advanced_explanation: scansion presupposes a fully determined pronunciation, including whether final vowels are realised; matching presupposes a target meter has been hypothesised; the procedure verifies rather than discovers; variations are licensed only in specific positions, which this lesson names but does not enumerate
fields.beginner_explanation: Introduces the metrical analysis of classical verse: the historical framing of the discipline, the inventory of named meters, the metrical foot as the unit from which a meter is assembled, the mnemonic template convention used to name feet, and a first end-to-end scansion of one long-meter hemistich including a licensed variation.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: using the terms for meter and metrical foot interchangeably; scanning the written form instead of the pronounced form
fields.contrast_or_transfer: meter versus foot: whole-line pattern versus building block; light versus heavy syllable as the two weight values
fields.intermediate_explanation: write only what is pronounced; mark each syllable as light or heavy; group the resulting weight string into the expected feet of the target meter
fields.prerequisite_statement: confident vocalised reading including case and mood endings; awareness that indefinite endings add a nasal consonant in pronunciation; awareness of definite-article assimilation
fields.recognition_cue: a text is verse when its hemistichs realise one repeating foot sequence throughout; a meter is recognised by matching a scanned weight string against the expected foot sequence; a licensed variation is recognised as a local shortening in a permitted position, leaving the surrounding feet intact
fields.tutor_destination: medium — foot-to-meter matching and meter naming are gradable, but any drill built on this lesson's core-foot table would propagate its arithmetic errors; drills should be rebuilt from a verified foot inventory

fields.advanced_explanation: the directive reading requires an authority differential or facts that carry their own authority; the commitment reading requires the absence of possibility-hedging particles; the supplication reading requires the invocation lexeme set and the absence of past-time anchoring
fields.beginner_explanation: Isolates the case where a grammatically assertive clause performs an act, and gives it named subtypes with recognition cues. The pedagogically load-bearing case is perfective-form invocation, where the tense form must not be read as past reference.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: treating every assertive as a pure report; reading a perfective invocation formula as a statement about the past
fields.contrast_or_transfer: assertive form with enacting function versus overtly enacting form; perfective-as-supplication versus perfective-as-report
fields.intermediate_explanation: state the grammatical form, then state the function, then state the speaker's intent as a separate line; run the indicator checklist for each of the four subtypes before defaulting to plain report; for a perfective clause, test for a past-time adverbial before assigning the supplication reading
fields.prerequisite_statement: perfective and imperfective verb morphology; nominal sentence with predicate nominal; L5.M1.01 assertive/enacting partition
fields.recognition_cue: for supplication: perfective verb from the invocation lexeme set, divine name as subject, no past-time adverbial, and a context of illness, death or blessing; for commitment: first-person subject, future or ongoing aspect, absence of hedging particles; for directive: statement of an obstacle or condition, speaker with standing, addressee action as the expected uptake
fields.tutor_destination: high for the invocation subtype, where the cue set is concrete; low for the directive and status subtypes, which need a supplied situation

fields.advanced_explanation: purpose assignment requires knowledge of what the addressee already knows; the warning reading requires a consequence the addressee can act on; the boasting or defence reading requires an implicit challenge to answer
fields.beginner_explanation: Teaches that an assertive utterance is produced for a purpose that need not be the transfer of new information, and supplies a named inventory of such purposes. Trains the learner to ask what the speaker is doing rather than only what the sentence says.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: assuming every assertive is a plain report of fact; conflating the informing purpose with the shared-knowledge purpose
fields.contrast_or_transfer: informing versus signalling shared knowledge; surface proposition versus rhetorical purpose
fields.intermediate_explanation: state the surface proposition, then ask what the speaker gains by uttering it here, then name the purpose from the inventory; separate the informing question (does the addressee know this?) from the purpose question (why say it?)
fields.prerequisite_statement: the assertive/enacting partition from L5.M1.01; nominal sentence structure; comparative adjective formation
fields.recognition_cue: ask whether the addressee could plausibly be ignorant of the content; if not, the purpose is not informing; look for mention of a hazard, a hostile party or an adverse consequence as a cue for a warning reading; look for a comparative or self-referential predicate as a cue for boasting or defence
fields.tutor_destination: medium — purpose-labelling drills are feasible only with a supplied situation, since the sentence alone underdetermines the answer

fields.advanced_explanation: stated for coordination of single nominals of equal rank; the case of the joined-to element is already fixed by its own governor; only case has to match; definiteness, gender and number do not
fields.beginner_explanation: Establishes coordination as a named grammatical relation in which a following element inherits the case of the peer element it is joined to, and separates six frequent connectors by the semantic distinction each carries (plain addition, tight sequence, delayed sequence, alternation, correction, adversative contrast). The aim is production of connected prose, not resolution of ambiguous attachment.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: using the tight-sequence connector in a context that states an interval; using the correction connector for a plain contrast where nothing is cancelled
fields.contrast_or_transfer: tight sequence versus delayed sequence; correction versus adversative contrast
fields.intermediate_explanation: locate the constituent preceding the connector and read its case; assign that same case to the constituent following the connector; when several elements are chained, hold every member in that case
fields.prerequisite_statement: the three cases and their exponents; the notion that a case is assigned by a governor; basic verbal and nominal sentence structure
fields.recognition_cue: a connector standing between two constituents of equal syntactic rank; the second constituent bearing the same case exponent as the first; for the sequencing pair, an interval that is stated or inferable from the surrounding narrative rather than from the connector
fields.tutor_destination: strong for production drills (case-matching fill-ins, forced choice within the sequencing pair and within the adversative pair); weak for analysis drills, because the semantic distinctions rest on world knowledge the drill must itself supply

fields.advanced_explanation: the corrective particle characteristically follows a negation, or upgrades an affirmation; the coordinating negator requires an affirmative first term and single-term conjuncts; the paired construction requires its second member to be present
fields.beginner_explanation: Consolidates coordination as a follower relation and inventories ten coordinating particles sorted by sequencing, alternation, correction versus contrast, negation of the second term only, extreme inclusion, and paired alternation, with case transmitted from the first term to the second throughout.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: using the declarative alternation particle inside an alternative question; reading the coordinating negator as ordinary clause negation
fields.contrast_or_transfer: additive with no sequence versus immediate sequence versus delayed sequence; declarative alternation versus interrogative alternation
fields.intermediate_explanation: identify the first term and read its case and clause role; select the particle from the intended semantic relation; assign the second term the same case
fields.prerequisite_statement: case system; negation particles; question formation
fields.recognition_cue: a particle from the closed set standing between two units that share a case; case identity between the two units, with no independent governor for the second; an interrogative frame, which selects the question-alternation particle
fields.tutor_destination: high for case transmission and for particle selection in clear frames; low for items that turn on disputed membership
fields.unresolved_notice: the size and membership of the coordinator inventory is school-dependent; the coordinator status of the extreme-inclusion particle is disputed

fields.advanced_explanation: the surprise reading requires a preceding prefix and a following nominal; the topic frame is incomplete without the linking prefix; the presentative formulas are fixed collocations rather than free constructions
fields.beginner_explanation: Introduces four discourse-level particles that manage attention, topic structure, presentation and surprise, and shows how each is recognised structurally rather than semantically. Anchors them in formal registers such as petitions, court speech and narrative turning points.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: confusing the attention particle with the homographic negated subordinator; omitting the linking prefix on the comment after the topic particle
fields.contrast_or_transfer: conditional use versus surprise use of the same element, distinguished by position and following category; the attention particle versus the homographic negated subordinator
fields.intermediate_explanation: check whether the element is clause-initial or prefix-attached; check whether the next constituent is nominal or verbal; for the topic frame, verify the linking prefix on the comment
fields.prerequisite_statement: the emphatic nominaliser and its clause structure; conditional clause structure with protasis and apodosis; demonstrative inventory
fields.recognition_cue: a clause-initial alerting particle, often immediately followed by the emphatic nominaliser; a topic particle whose comment carries the linking prefix; the presentative element preceding a pronoun or a definite noun phrase
fields.tutor_destination: strong for the two-reading discrimination task; the presentative formulas suit recognition rather than production drills
fields.unresolved_notice: the syntactic category of the surprise element is a classical dispute among grammarians (adverb of place, adverb of time, or particle); the lesson does not raise it

fields.advanced_explanation: the override applies when the plural head denotes non-humans; definiteness matching is the axis that determines whether the string is a phrase at all; case agreement holds regardless of which governor assigned the case
fields.beginner_explanation: Sets out attributive modification (النعت والمنعوت) as agreement on four simultaneous axes, and shows that mismatching one of them either produces ungrammaticality or reanalyses the string as a predication rather than a phrase.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: modifying a non-human plural head with a plural adjective; treating a definite noun followed by an indefinite adjective as a noun phrase
fields.contrast_or_transfer: definite head with definite adjective versus definite head with indefinite adjective; human plural agreement versus non-human plural agreement
fields.intermediate_explanation: fix the head noun's case from its role in the clause; read the head's gender, number and definiteness; build the adjective on the same four values
fields.prerequisite_statement: the three cases and their exponents; definiteness marking; gender and number marking on nouns
fields.recognition_cue: a noun immediately followed by a descriptive word carrying the same case exponent, the same definiteness marking and matching gender/number; a definite noun followed by an indefinite descriptive word, which signals predication rather than modification; a non-human plural head followed by a feminine singular descriptive word, which is modification and not a mismatch
fields.tutor_destination: drills should vary one axis at a time and include the non-human plural override plus at least one definiteness-mismatch item
fields.unresolved_notice: analysis-dependent: describing the adjective as copying the head's case is one formulation; the follower relation is described differently in traditional terms

fields.advanced_explanation: adjacency with no coordinator intervening; a resumptive clitic is obligatory in the two connected types; in the total type the appositive must itself be able to bear the predication
fields.beginner_explanation: Introduces apposition as the fourth follower: a substitute nominal that carries the syntactic weight of the noun it follows, presented through a four-way typology and a resumptive clitic requirement that holds for exactly two of the four types.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: omitting the clitic in the partitive or inclusion type; assigning a part reading where a quality reading is intended, or the reverse
fields.contrast_or_transfer: total versus partitive versus inclusion versus corrective apposition; apposition versus the descriptive follower
fields.intermediate_explanation: confirm case identity between the two nominals; test whether the second nominal alone would carry the predication; check for a clitic and resolve its antecedent
fields.prerequisite_statement: case system; clitic pronouns; the follower class
fields.recognition_cue: a second nominal immediately after the first, with identical case and no coordinator between them; a clitic on the second nominal that resolves to the first, marking the partitive or inclusion type; referential identity with no clitic, marking the total type
fields.tutor_destination: high for the clitic and case checks; medium for type classification, which needs a semantic judgement the form does not supply
fields.unresolved_notice: several of the lesson's own naming pairs are equally analysable as appositional clarification, a rival label introduced only in the following lesson

fields.advanced_explanation: both nominals share case and, normally, definiteness; the clarifier is a rigid nominal, not a derived descriptive, which is what keeps it apart from the descriptive follower; the deciding criterion is interpretive, resting on which nominal the speaker intends as primary
fields.beginner_explanation: Adds a fifth follower whose form is indistinguishable from total apposition and whose only difference is which of the two nominals carries the primary reference, and equips the learner with a deletion test plus an attributed account of the long-standing disagreement over whether the category is independent at all.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: labelling a clarifying rigid nominal as a descriptive follower; assuming every name-after-title pair is appositional clarification
fields.contrast_or_transfer: clarification versus substitution; clarification versus descriptive modification
fields.intermediate_explanation: delete the second nominal and judge the remainder; delete the first nominal and judge the remainder; assign the label according to which deletion leaves the better sentence
fields.prerequisite_statement: the apposition typology from L4.M2.05; case system; definiteness
fields.recognition_cue: a second rigid nominal, same case, with no coordinator and no clitic; a first nominal that carries independent content, typically a title, a teknonym, or a relational noun; referential identity between the pair, so neither member predicates a property of the other
fields.tutor_destination: low to medium - single-label items are not safely gradable here, because the two analyses are formally identical and the lesson's own test is applied inconsistently
fields.unresolved_notice: the independence of the category from apposition is disputed and the lesson deliberately leaves it open; the attribution of the three positions to particular schools requires verification against primary sources

fields.advanced_explanation: both members must occur inside the same span for either figure to be claimed; the complete subtype demands full vocalisation to be known, not just the consonantal skeleton; the negated subtype demands that both members derive from the same concept, one affirmed and one denied
fields.beginner_explanation: Opens the rhetoric module by locating ornamentation inside the three-branch division of classical balagha, then trains recognition of two figures: the pairing of phonetically near-identical words that diverge in sense, and the deliberate juxtaposition of contraries in one span.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: labelling an antonym pair as the sound-based figure, or a sound-alike pair as the contrariety figure; assuming the sound-based figure requires the two tokens to mean the same thing
fields.contrast_or_transfer: sound axis vs sense axis as the primary separator of the two figures; complete vs incomplete resemblance within the sound-based figure
fields.intermediate_explanation: classify a supplied pair: (1) is there sound resemblance? (2) is there sense opposition? (3) assign the figure by which axis is active; subclassify paronomasia by walking the four comparison dimensions in order: letter count, letter identity, letter order, vocalisation; subclassify antithesis by testing the polarity of each member
fields.prerequisite_statement: fluent reading of fully vocalised classical text; awareness that vowels can distinguish otherwise identical consonant skeletons; recognition of negation operators
fields.recognition_cue: locate two tokens in one span whose consonant skeletons coincide wholly or almost wholly; confirm the two tokens are read in different senses in their respective positions; compare vocalisation as well as letters before assigning the complete subtype
fields.tutor_destination: high for classification drills — a supplied pair plus a small feature set (resemblance present, opposition present, polarity, vocalisation identity) is enough to autograde a subtype answer

fields.advanced_explanation: The corrective connector requires an antecedent statement to act on.; The immediate-sequence connector must remain attached orthographically.; The delayed-sequence connector is appropriate only where a gap — temporal, logical or rhetorical — is actually intended.
fields.beginner_explanation: Teaches the four core discourse connectors as a contrastive system operating above the sentence, so that a reader can reconstruct the logical and temporal skeleton of a paragraph and a writer can choose the connector that matches the intended relation instead of defaulting to the neutral one.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: Choosing the delayed-sequence connector where the action follows immediately.; Using the corrective connector where no contrast or correction exists.
fields.contrast_or_transfer: Immediate versus delayed sequence between the two sequencing connectors.; Neutral addition versus specified consequence.
fields.intermediate_explanation: Identify the relation intended between the current clause and the previous one: addition, immediate consequence, staged progression, or correction.; Select the connector that encodes that relation rather than defaulting to the additive one.; Bind the immediate-sequence connector orthographically to the first word of its clause.
fields.prerequisite_statement: basic coordination and clause juncture; negation of verbal and nominal clauses; narrative tense usage
fields.recognition_cue: Orthographic bonding to the following word identifies the immediate-sequence connector; independence identifies the delayed-sequence one.; A connector counts as corrective only when there is prior material for it to cancel, replace or exceed.; A negated clause immediately before the corrective connector signals the affirm-the-alternative pattern.
fields.tutor_destination: Strong: cloze drills that require the learner to choose the connector matching a described relation, minimal-pair drills on the gap distinction, and rewriting drills that replace over-used additive connectors with the informative alternatives.

fields.advanced_explanation: the repair applies only in connected delivery; the following word must begin with a connective, not a stable, initial hamza; the preceding word must actually end vowelless
fields.beginner_explanation: Teaches the phonotactic ban on two adjacent vowelless consonants and the repair strategies Arabic uses when that configuration arises at a word boundary, together with the distinction between pausal and connected pronunciation that determines whether the configuration arises at all.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: Leaving an imperative's final consonant vowelless before the definite article.; Inserting a repair vowel where no configuration exists.
fields.contrast_or_transfer: connective versus stable initial hamza, only the first triggering the configuration; pausal versus connected delivery
fields.intermediate_explanation: check whether the token ends in a vowelless consonant; check whether the next token begins with a connective hamza rather than a stable one; decide whether the delivery pauses or connects at that point
fields.prerequisite_statement: the two kinds of initial hamza; imperative and jussive formation; case endings and indefinite nunation
fields.recognition_cue: a word ending in a vowelless consonant immediately followed by a word beginning with a connective hamza; imperatives and jussive verbs, which characteristically end in a vowelless consonant; the definite article, the reflexive and n-prefixed and s-t-prefixed derived verbs, base-form imperatives, and a small closed noun list as carriers of the connective hamza
fields.tutor_destination: medium — imperative-plus-article items drill cleanly, but the honest rule needs the non-default repair vowels the lesson omits, so drills built directly on this lesson would teach an overgeneralisation

fields.advanced_explanation: template hints hold only tendentially; the concord rule as stated applies to non-human referents; restructured plurals of rational males take plural concord instead; items whose plural belongs to a fourth template not among the three taught
fields.beginner_explanation: Introduces internally restructured plurals as a template operation rather than an affixation, presents three high-frequency plural templates with their recognition cues, and states that these plurals keep ordinary vowel case marking while taking feminine singular concord when their referent is non-human.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: giving masculine plural concord to a non-human restructured plural; applying one template's vowel skeleton to a base that takes a different one
fields.contrast_or_transfer: restructured against suffixal plurals, both in formation and in case marking; the three templates against one another by vowel signature
fields.intermediate_explanation: identify the root consonants, then read the vowel skeleton against the three template signatures; use the singular's template as a hint, then verify the attested plural in a lexicon; apply ordinary case vowels according to syntactic role and definiteness
fields.prerequisite_statement: root and template analysis; the three-case system and definiteness; both suffixal plurals
fields.recognition_cue: the plural shares the base's consonants but not its vowel skeleton, and no suffix is present; an added opening element with a vowelless second consonant identifies the first template; a doubled short-vowel run followed by a long back vowel identifies the second
fields.tutor_destination: high + template recognition and singular-to-plural recall are both drillable, though generation drills must accept multiple attested plurals

fields.advanced_explanation: object reading requires a verbal host; possessor reading requires a nominal host; genitive-position reading requires a governing particle host
fields.beginner_explanation: Teaches the attached pronoun series and the three host categories that license it, so that a suffix can be read correctly as an object, a possessor, or the complement of a governing particle. It also introduces the conditioned shape changes inside that series.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: attaching the bare first-person suffix directly to a verb without the protective nūn; keeping the back vowel on the h-series after a preceding front vowel
fields.contrast_or_transfer: object suffix versus possessor suffix with identical surface shape; bare first-person suffix versus the shape with protective nūn
fields.intermediate_explanation: segment the word into host plus suffix; classify the host category; assign the suffix's role from that category: complement of a verb, possessor of a noun, or complement of a particle
fields.prerequisite_statement: the free pronoun inventory and its person/gender/number contrasts; annexation and definiteness effects on a noun; the fact that governing particles impose the genitive
fields.recognition_cue: the pronoun has no independent orthographic word boundary and closes out its host; identify the host first: a finite verb, a noun, or a governing particle; a protective nūn immediately before a first-person suffix signals a verbal host
fields.tutor_destination: high — host-to-role mapping and allomorph selection are both mechanically checkable in drills

fields.advanced_explanation: unit extraction requires the feminine-marked form to be attested, not merely constructible; the sound feminine plural applies to the unit noun, not to the collective; agreement optionality is stated for collectives, not for the unit nouns
fields.beginner_explanation: Separates three noun classes that all denote more than one thing: the generic collective from which a single item can be extracted by adding the feminine marker, the unit noun so extracted, and the inherently collective noun that has no such counterpart. Frames the collective as morphologically singular but semantically plural, with the agreement consequences that follow.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: calling a collective the plural of its unit noun; choosing agreement at random between the two available patterns
fields.contrast_or_transfer: generic collective versus unit noun; generic collective versus unit-less collective
fields.intermediate_explanation: test whether the noun refers to many while showing no plural morphology; attempt extraction of a unit by adding the feminine marker and check attestation; if extraction succeeds, classify as generic collective and record the unit noun
fields.prerequisite_statement: the feminine marker; sound feminine plural; broken plurals
fields.recognition_cue: a singular-shaped noun with plural reference and no plural morphology; the same stem plus the feminine marker denoting exactly one individual; a sound feminine plural built on that unit form for small counts
fields.tutor_destination: moderate: class-assignment and unit-extraction drills work well; agreement drills need caution because the lesson's own agreement rows are shaky

fields.advanced_explanation: the attribute reading requires agreement on all four dimensions, not only on case; the specification reading requires the preceding element to be genuinely ambiguous in extent; the cognate accusative requires root identity with its verb
fields.beginner_explanation: Makes the Arabic grammatical metalanguage itself the object of study, on the argument that a reader who cannot decode the labels cannot use any classical commentary. Each label is presented with its ordinary-language sense as a mnemonic for its function, and the assembled set is then shown at work on the way commentaries parse the opening line of a pre-Islamic ode.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: using one English label for both the agent and the topic; letting the case of the first construct term propagate to the second
fields.contrast_or_transfer: agent of a verb versus topic of a verbless clause, both translatable as subject; circumstantial versus attribute, separated by definiteness agreement
fields.intermediate_explanation: for each word ask what governs it and what case that governor assigns; decompose an unfamiliar label into its ordinary sense to recover the function it names; use definiteness agreement as the test that separates an attribute from a circumstantial
fields.prerequisite_statement: the three cases and their exponents; verbless and verbal clause structure; construct chains
fields.recognition_cue: a nominative noun with a verb present in the clause is an agent; the same noun with no verb present is a topic; an indefinite derived accusative added to an already complete clause, describing the state of a definite participant, is a circumstantial; an indefinite accusative after a numeral, a measure, or a comparative is a specification
fields.tutor_destination: very strong - term-to-function matching, label recall from a definition, and the circumstantial-versus-attribute agreement test are all directly drillable with standard examples and need no source text
fields.unresolved_notice: school-dependent: governance theory itself is a framework rather than an observation, and it was contested within the tradition; the tradition is not terminologically uniform; rival schools used different labels for overlapping categories, which the lesson does not mention

fields.advanced_explanation: The heavy adversative form requires a prior statement in the discourse for it to act on.; The prepositional concessive frame requires a nominal complement; a clause is admitted only through the intervening أنّ.; Compound adversative markers require the أنّ they are built on and cannot be reduced to their lexical head alone in this function.
fields.beginner_explanation: Introduces the family of contrastive connectives, separating those that correct or counter a prior assertion from those that concede an obstacle and then override it, and fixes for each connective what kind of complement it takes and what case it assigns.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: Opening a discourse with the heavy adversative particle when nothing precedes for it to correct.; Leaving the noun after the heavy adversative particle in the nominative.
fields.contrast_or_transfer: Correction versus concession as discourse relations.; Heavy versus light adversative form: case-assigning versus non-case-assigning.
fields.intermediate_explanation: Decide first whether the intended relation is correction or concession, since that choice narrows the connective set.; Choose the connective, then supply the complement shape that connective licenses: an accusative nominal plus predicate, an أنّ-clause, or a genitive noun phrase.; Check the case marking on the first element after the connective against what the connective assigns.
fields.prerequisite_statement: the inna family and the case pattern it imposes; the difference between prepositions and subordinating conjunctions; nominal versus verbal sentence structure
fields.recognition_cue: A connective is adversative if removing it leaves two assertions where the second corrects or unexpectedly qualifies the first.; A connective is concessive if the clause it introduces states a reason to expect the opposite of the main clause.; The heavy adversative form is identifiable by accusative marking on the noun immediately after it.
fields.tutor_destination: Strong: minimal-pair drills on heavy versus light adversative form, on forward versus backward concessive, and on complement repair when a learner supplies the wrong shape after a given connective.

fields.advanced_explanation: the list of obligatory environments is presented as closed; restriction readings are stated for fronted objects; case preservation is stated for both fronted objects and fronted subjects
fields.beginner_explanation: Treats linear position as a meaningful choice: which constituents may move forward, which environments force movement, what marking a moved constituent keeps, and what pragmatic effect the movement is said to produce.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: omitting the resumptive pronoun after fronting an object; changing the case of the fronted element to nominative
fields.contrast_or_transfer: default order versus fronted order; optional versus obligatory fronting
fields.intermediate_explanation: restore the default order to identify each constituent role; check that the fronted element still carries the case of that role; look for a resumptive pronoun and match its agreement to the fronted element
fields.prerequisite_statement: default order of verbal and nominal clauses; case marking of objects and predicates; attached pronoun paradigms
fields.recognition_cue: a constituent bearing object case standing before its verb; an attached pronoun on the verb agreeing with a preceding full noun; a prepositional phrase or adverbial preceding the clause it belongs to
fields.tutor_destination: supports rewrite drills between default and fronted order and judgement drills over the obligatory environments; pragmatic-effect items cannot be auto-graded and need free-form marking
fields.unresolved_notice: the lesson excludes nominative marking on a preposed noun resumed by a pronoun, whereas the standard treatment of that configuration admits more than one case assignment under rival analyses; this is a live dispute, not a settled rule

fields.advanced_explanation: the definite article is actually present as a prefix; the classification is applied to the first consonant of the following word
fields.beginner_explanation: Develops the definite article as an invariantly written but variably pronounced clitic: fourteen letters trigger assimilation of its laam, realized as gemination of the following consonant, and fourteen do not. The learner is trained to classify any letter into the two groups and to pronounce accordingly.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: pronouncing the laam before a triggering letter; adding gemination to a non-triggering letter by analogy
fields.contrast_or_transfer: an article-prefixed word with a triggering initial against one with a non-triggering initial; the written form of the article, which never varies, against its spoken form, which does
fields.intermediate_explanation: look up the following word's first letter in the two-way classification, then pronounce the article accordingly; when vocalizing, give the laam the vowellessness mark before a non-triggering letter and instead place the gemination mark on a triggering letter; when speaking, double the triggering consonant rather than merely dropping the laam
fields.prerequisite_statement: the full letter inventory; the gemination and vowellessness marks; nunation and the definiteness contrast
fields.recognition_cue: a gemination mark on the consonant immediately following the article; a vowelless laam followed by an unmarked consonant, which signals the non-assimilating class; classification decided by the first consonant of the following word and by nothing else
fields.tutor_destination: high - a closed twenty-eight-way classification with a deterministic consequence is close to ideal drill material

fields.advanced_explanation: the marker-based test assumes a fully declinable common noun; the enumeration is presented as covering the whole definiteness space; the topic/comment default is stated for the unmarked construction
fields.beginner_explanation: Treats definiteness as a system in its own right: it separates definite from indefinite nominals, enumerates the sources from which definiteness comes, names the surface markers, and connects the distinction back to the default definiteness of the two slots of the noun-initial sentence.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: reading any nunated nominal as indefinite; reading any nominal without the article as indefinite
fields.contrast_or_transfer: specific versus non-specific reference for the same lexeme; article-marked definiteness versus inherited definiteness through annexation
fields.intermediate_explanation: check the nominal against each definiteness source in turn; if none applies, classify the nominal as indefinite; when constructing a noun-initial sentence, select a definite topic and an indefinite comment
fields.prerequisite_statement: the article and nunation as surface elements; pronominal suffixes and their attachment; the two slots of the noun-initial sentence
fields.recognition_cue: presence of the definite article on the nominal; nunation on the ending, in the absence of any other definiteness source; membership in a closed class (pronoun, demonstrative, relative noun)
fields.tutor_destination: high — source attribution is a clean, checkable task, and the nunated proper name is an ideal item for eliciting the lesson's own weakest generalisation

fields.advanced_explanation: a phrase reading requires the definite article on the noun that follows; human plural demonstratives require rational plural referents; dual demonstratives require a dual referent and then vary with case
fields.beginner_explanation: Introduces the demonstrative words as a class organised by proximity, gender and number, and teaches how the definiteness of the following noun decides whether the result is a phrase or a complete sentence.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: omitting the definite article on the noun after a demonstrative when a phrase was intended; pairing a masculine demonstrative with a feminine noun
fields.contrast_or_transfer: near versus far series; masculine versus feminine within each distance
fields.intermediate_explanation: identify the referent's gender, number and rationality; choose near or far according to the intended distance; select the matching demonstrative from the grid
fields.prerequisite_statement: the definite article and its effect on definiteness; gender marking on nouns; verbless sentence structure
fields.recognition_cue: a closed-class pointing word occupying a nominal slot; gender and number of the demonstrative match the referent, so mismatch signals a different target; presence of the definite article on the next word signals a phrase reading; its absence signals a predication
fields.tutor_destination: high — agreement selection and the article switch produce unambiguous right/wrong drill items
fields.unresolved_notice: school-dependent: whether the dual demonstratives are genuinely declinable or invariant with substituted endings; rival analyses: demonstrative as modifier of the following noun versus demonstrative as head with the noun in apposition

fields.advanced_explanation: the undergoer reading presupposes a transitive baseline verb of the same root; the connective hamza elides only when the word is not utterance-initial; the restriction check presupposes that the root has already been identified
fields.beginner_explanation: Introduces the augmented pattern marked by a prefixed اِنْـ, presents it as the undergoer counterpart of a transitive base, and states a hard restriction on which roots may enter it. The restriction, together with the categorical ban on a direct object, is the lesson's distinctive contribution.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: Giving the verb a direct object.; Omitting the nasal in the imperfect.
fields.contrast_or_transfer: agent-subject baseline verb against undergoer-subject stem of the same root; prefixed nasal against infixed ت as competing analyses of the same initial string
fields.intermediate_explanation: strip the prefix and test whether three radicals remain; check the first radical against the barred set before accepting the assignment; when the string begins اِنْتَـ, determine whether the nasal is the prefix or the first radical
fields.prerequisite_statement: the baseline stem and its transitivity; connective versus disjunctive hamza; subject and object marking in a verbal clause
fields.recognition_cue: اِنْـ stands before the first radical in the perfect; the imperfect shows a on the subject prefix followed by a vowelless nasal and i before the final radical; no direct object is present in the clause
fields.tutor_destination: strong for admissibility checks and for the prefix-versus-radical disambiguation of the ambiguous initial sequence; also for the intransitivity constraint as an error-detection drill

fields.advanced_explanation: the pronoun must be in the detached accusative series to occupy pre-verbal position; the pronoun must agree with its referent in person, gender and number; the exclusive reading is supported by contrast or explicit negation of alternatives
fields.beginner_explanation: Teaches pre-posing of an object expressed by a detached accusative pronoun, presenting it as a device that narrows the action to that object alone rather than merely emphasising it, and sets it beside the other means of expressing restriction.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: Reading every pre-posed object as exclusive.; Attempting to place a clitic pronoun in pre-verbal position.
fields.contrast_or_transfer: clitic object in place against detached pronoun pre-posed; emphasis without exclusion against exclusion of alternatives
fields.intermediate_explanation: determine that the object is to be placed before the verb; select the detached accusative pronoun matching the referent in person, gender and number; place it before the verb rather than attaching it
fields.prerequisite_statement: object pre-posing for emphasis; clitic object pronouns and their attachment; accusative marking of objects
fields.recognition_cue: a detached accusative pronoun stands before the verb; the verb has no clitic object of its own filling the same role; an alternative is negated or contrasted in the immediate context
fields.tutor_destination: high - drills can require selecting the correct series member for a referent and converting a clitic object into a pre-posed detached one
fields.unresolved_notice: school-dependent: that pre-posing yields restriction rather than heightened attention is a rhetorical-tradition claim and is not universally held in that strong form

fields.advanced_explanation: the long-vowel template applies only when the base has a long medial vowel or a geminate; the four-slot template applies only to four-consonant stems; hamza deletion applies only to a connecting hamza, not to a root hamza
fields.beginner_explanation: Pushes the diminutive template family past the simple three-consonant base into four-consonant stems, stems carrying a prefixed letter or a feminine ending, stems whose weak radical is invisible in the citation form, and two-element proper names. Pairs that formal machinery with the four pragmatic values (small size, affection, belittlement, nearness in time) that decide why a speaker reaches for the form at all.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: diminutizing a short weak-final noun without restoring the hidden radical and without the feminine ending; applying the three-consonant template to a four-consonant stem
fields.contrast_or_transfer: diminutive template versus the adjectival template of similar shape; diminutive template versus the active-participle template
fields.intermediate_explanation: classify the base by consonant count and by presence of a long medial vowel or gemination; identify affixes on the base: prefixed letter, connecting hamza, feminine ending; strip or preserve each affix according to its class before applying the skeleton
fields.prerequisite_statement: root versus template distinction; four-consonant roots; weak-radical classes
fields.recognition_cue: a noun whose first consonant carries damma and whose second carries fatha, with a glide directly after the second; a glide in the stem that has no counterpart in the lexeme's root; a base lexeme recoverable by stripping the inserted glide and restoring the base vowels
fields.tutor_destination: strong: base-to-diminutive production drills are mechanical and gradeable, and the base-class decision makes a good branching drill

fields.advanced_explanation: the noun must be indefinite for the reduced paradigm to surface; the noun must not be the first term of an annexation; both a semantic and a formal trigger must be identifiable
fields.beginner_explanation: Introduces the class of nouns that decline with a reduced set of case exponents and refuse nunation, and teaches the paired-trigger account that is supposed to decide membership. Organises the class into named subgroups (proper names, toponyms, two adjective templates, one plural template family) so the learner can recognise members on sight.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: attaching nunation to a member of the class; writing kasra on a class member governed in the genitive
fields.contrast_or_transfer: full three-exponent paradigm versus reduced two-exponent paradigm; genitive fatha versus genitive kasra in the same syntactic frame
fields.intermediate_explanation: classify the noun as proper name, adjective, or plural of the extended-plural family; search for one formal trigger of the listed inventory; if a trigger pair is present, assign the reduced two-exponent paradigm
fields.prerequisite_statement: the three-case noun inflection system; nunation as an indefiniteness exponent; annexation basics
fields.recognition_cue: an indefinite noun that carries no nunation; fatha appearing where a preposition or a governing genitive slot would predict kasra; a name shaped like a verb template, ending in the added ان, or carrying a feminine ending
fields.tutor_destination: strong: trigger identification and genitive-exponent selection both generate mechanically from lexeme metadata
fields.unresolved_notice: the classification of one toponym as inherently feminine is disputed among grammarians

fields.advanced_explanation: restoration applies only to the term that is actually definitised; restoration concerns the case vowel, not nunation; the metrical licence is confined to poetry
fields.beginner_explanation: Teaches the conditions under which the reduced-exponent class taught previously is suspended and the noun returns to the ordinary genitive exponent, and separates restoration of the case vowel from restoration of nunation. Adds a four-state summary of how one lexeme behaves across definiteness and annexation configurations.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: keeping the reduced genitive exponent on an article-prefixed class member; keeping the reduced genitive exponent on a class member that governs a genitive complement
fields.contrast_or_transfer: indefinite bare occurrence versus article-prefixed occurrence of the same lexeme; indefinite bare occurrence versus first-term-of-annexation occurrence
fields.intermediate_explanation: decide whether the token carries the definite article; decide whether the token is followed by a genitive complement it governs; if either holds, select the ordinary exponent for the case slot
fields.prerequisite_statement: the reduced-exponent class and its triggers from the preceding lesson; the definite article and definiteness marking; annexation structure and which term takes the genitive
fields.recognition_cue: the definite article prefixed to a lexeme whose template predicts the reduced paradigm; a genitive complement following the candidate, marking it as first term of an annexation; the ordinary genitive vowel appearing on a lexeme that would otherwise show fatha
fields.tutor_destination: strong: minimal-pair drills over one lexeme in four configurations are mechanically generable

fields.advanced_explanation: stated for triliteral bases; the invariability rule is stated for the مِن construction specifically; the feminine counterpart is conditioned on a definite feminine head or on independent nominal use
fields.beginner_explanation: Introduces the elative as a single derived shape that covers both degrees of comparison, and makes the point that degree is decided by the surrounding construction rather than by the word's own form. It supplies the build, the weak- and doubled-root adjustments, the feminine counterpart, and the three constructions that fix the reading.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: confusing the elative shape with the agent-participle shape; attaching a مِن complement to an elative that already carries the definite article or already heads an annexation
fields.contrast_or_transfer: comparative construction against the two superlative constructions; the elative template against the agent-participle template, explicitly compared as look-alikes
fields.intermediate_explanation: certify the three radicals of the base adjective; prefix the hamza and assign fatha to the second radical; merge the final radicals if the base is doubled, or reduce the ending if the base is final-weak
fields.prerequisite_statement: triliteral root extraction; adjective agreement; the definite article and definiteness
fields.recognition_cue: an initial hamza with fatha prefixed to three radicals, with fatha on the second radical; a following مِن complement signals the comparative reading; a definite article on the elative, or a genitive noun immediately after it, signals a superlative reading
fields.tutor_destination: high — formation is deterministic and the three constructions give a clean discrimination drill, though item selection must respect which bases actually admit an elative
fields.unresolved_notice: whether sequence and otherness items belong to the elative class is disputed in the tradition and is asserted here without attribution

fields.advanced_explanation: stated for triliteral bases; the invariability rule is stated for the مِن construction specifically; the feminine counterpart is conditioned on a definite feminine head or on independent nominal use
fields.beginner_explanation: Introduces the elative as a single derived shape that covers both degrees of comparison, and makes the point that degree is decided by the surrounding construction rather than by the word's own form. It supplies the build, the weak- and doubled-root adjustments, the feminine counterpart, and the three constructions that fix the reading.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: confusing the elative shape with the agent-participle shape; attaching a مِن complement to an elative that already carries the definite article or already heads an annexation
fields.contrast_or_transfer: comparative construction against the two superlative constructions; the elative template against the agent-participle template, explicitly compared as look-alikes
fields.intermediate_explanation: certify the three radicals of the base adjective; prefix the hamza and assign fatha to the second radical; merge the final radicals if the base is doubled, or reduce the ending if the base is final-weak
fields.prerequisite_statement: triliteral root extraction; adjective agreement; the definite article and definiteness
fields.recognition_cue: an initial hamza with fatha prefixed to three radicals, with fatha on the second radical; a following مِن complement signals the comparative reading; a definite article on the elative, or a genitive noun immediately after it, signals a superlative reading
fields.tutor_destination: high — formation is deterministic and the three constructions give a clean discrimination drill, though item selection must respect which bases actually admit an elative
fields.unresolved_notice: whether sequence and otherness items belong to the elative class is disputed in the tradition and is asserted here without attribution

fields.advanced_explanation: the emphatic lam is licensed on the predicate of the emphatic particle, not freely on any predicate; the emphatic nun requires the fatḥa-marked stem shape rather than the plain indicative or jussive ending; the confirmation reading of قد is primary with perfective verbs
fields.beginner_explanation: Presents the inventory of devices that strengthen an assertive claim and ties the number of devices used to the addressee's assumed epistemic stance. Trains calibration: matching emphasis to actual resistance rather than applying it uniformly.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: applying emphasis to an addressee who has no doubt; using the emphatic particle and the emphatic-exclusive particle interchangeably
fields.contrast_or_transfer: bare assertion versus one-device versus multi-device emphasis; emphatic particle versus emphatic-plus-exclusive particle
fields.intermediate_explanation: assess the addressee's stance, then select zero, one, or two-plus devices accordingly; to raise emphasis one step, add the emphatic particle; to raise it again, add the emphatic lam to the predicate; to raise it further, prefix an oath; to attach the emphatic nun, place a fatḥa on the verb ending before suffixing the nun
fields.prerequisite_statement: nominal sentence structure and its predicate slot; the emphatic-accusative particle and its case assignment; indicative, subjunctive and jussive verb endings
fields.recognition_cue: count the emphatic devices present in a clause and read off the assumed addressee stance; identify لَـ on the predicate of a nominal clause headed by the emphatic particle; identify قد immediately before a finite verb and check the verb's aspect
fields.tutor_destination: high — device identification and stepwise emphasis-raising are both mechanically checkable; the stance inference is not

fields.advanced_explanation: the contrast is only meaningful where a plain counterpart exists; the three additional heavy letters have no light counterpart and are always heavy; vowel colouring is a phonetic consequence and leaves the orthography unchanged
fields.beginner_explanation: Introduces the phonological contrast between pharyngealised and plain consonants, fixes the membership of the emphatic set and of the wider heavy set, and shows that the contrast carries meaning and colours neighbouring vowels.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: Producing an emphatic consonant as its plain counterpart.; Exaggerating emphasis until the sound is distorted.
fields.contrast_or_transfer: each emphatic against its plain counterpart across four pairings; the emphatic subset against the wider heavy set
fields.intermediate_explanation: place the tongue as for the plain articulation; raise the back of the tongue toward the pharynx; tense the pharynx slightly so the sound is lowered
fields.prerequisite_statement: the alphabet and letter names; short vowel signs; the ability to hear vowel quality differences
fields.recognition_cue: orthographic membership in the four-letter emphatic set; auditory darkening of a vowel adjacent to the consonant; a change of meaning when the plain counterpart is substituted
fields.tutor_destination: medium-high for listening discrimination and production drills on minimal pairs; low for anything requiring parsing

fields.advanced_explanation: the verb must be imperfect or imperative; after the oath particle the verb must be affirmative and future-referring for attachment to be obligatory; the light shape is licensed only outside the dual and feminine plural
fields.beginner_explanation: Teaches the emphatic suffix attached to imperfect verbs and imperatives in its heavy and light shapes, the deletions its attachment forces on person and number markers, and the licensing contexts, chiefly oath formulas, in which it is required or permitted.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: Keeping the masculine plural marker before the suffix.; Keeping the long vowel of the feminine singular before the suffix.
fields.contrast_or_transfer: heavy versus light shape in strength and in distribution; the emphatic suffix versus the feminine plural ending, which differ in the vowel before the nasal
fields.intermediate_explanation: identify the person and number ending of the plain imperfect; delete the segment that would collide with the suffix, following the rule for that ending; preserve the residual vowel as the trace of the deleted marker
fields.prerequisite_statement: imperfect conjugation with all person and number endings; mood marking and the particles that govern it; imperative and prohibition formation
fields.recognition_cue: a verb ending in a geminate nasal preceded by a low vowel, as against a feminine plural ending where the preceding consonant is vowelless; an oath particle followed by a prefixed emphatic lam on the verb; an imperfect verb whose expected plural or feminine marker is missing but whose residual vowel is unexpected for the singular
fields.tutor_destination: high — attachment is fully rule-governed and gradable, and the licensing restriction plus the feminine-plural confusion make two good discriminator items; the affective heavy versus light doctrine must not be drilled as fact
fields.unresolved_notice: analysis-dependent: the collision-avoidance motivation offered for the deletions

fields.advanced_explanation: the subjunctive requires the causal reading and a preceding pure request or negation; the apodosis connective is required only when the apodosis cannot stand as an apocopated verb clause; the coordinating reading requires two coordinated elements of the same syntactic type
fields.beginner_explanation: Presents a single-letter connective proclitic as a five-way ambiguous element, contrasts it with the neutral connective that carries no ordering, and ties one of its readings to a mood change on the verb that follows.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: Leaving the following verb in the indicative after the causal reading.; Treating this connective as interchangeable with the neutral coordinating particle.
fields.contrast_or_transfer: this connective against the neutral coordinating particle; the causal reading with subjunctive against the coordinating reading whose mood is inherited from context
fields.intermediate_explanation: identify what precedes the connective: a clause, a request, a negation, a conditional protasis, or nothing; inspect the mood exponent on any following imperfect verb; if a conditional protasis precedes, test whether the apodosis is of a type that forces the connective
fields.prerequisite_statement: coordination; the three moods of the imperfect and their exponents; conditional particles and apocopated verbs
fields.recognition_cue: two eventive predicates in narrative succession with no gap between them, indicating the coordinating reading; a request-type or negative clause before the connective together with a subjunctive exponent on the following imperfect verb, indicating the causal reading; a conditional protasis before the connective and an apodosis that cannot itself be an apocopated verb clause, indicating the apodosis connective
fields.tutor_destination: high with care + function identification and mood selection drill well, but several of the lesson's own token labels would need correction before use as answer keys

fields.advanced_explanation: the double entendre requires genuine polysemy of one token, not resemblance between two tokens; invented causation requires an actual causal assertion, not merely an evocative image; compatibility judgements presuppose a shared register and are stated as gradient, not binary
fields.beginner_explanation: Completes the ornamentation survey with three further figures: intending the remoter of a word's two senses behind its readier sense, substituting an invented aesthetically pleasing cause for a real one, and choosing words for mutual compatibility across a passage.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: conflating the double entendre with the sound-based figure because both involve multiple meanings; treating invented causation as a kind of metaphor
fields.contrast_or_transfer: one token with two senses vs two tokens that resemble each other; causal explanation vs predicative identification
fields.intermediate_explanation: locate the pivot token, enumerate its senses, rank them by immediacy, then test each against the context to identify the intended one; state the real cause, state the offered cause, and judge whether the offered cause is fictional and aesthetically motivated; survey a passage for word clusters and describe the dimension along which they cohere
fields.prerequisite_statement: the sound-based figure from lesson 1, which is the contrast term for the double entendre; a metaphor/simile vocabulary from the expression branch of rhetoric, presupposed but not taught here; dictionary-level polysemy awareness
fields.recognition_cue: for the double entendre, find a token whose readier sense is contextually thin while a second attested sense fits the context better; confirm that both senses are genuinely available for the token, not invented for the analysis; for invented causation, find an explicit causal claim and compare it against the factual cause of the event
fields.tutor_destination: medium — the token-count and explanation-versus-predication tests are drillable; compatibility judgements are not objectively gradable and should stay in discussion tasks rather than scored items

fields.advanced_explanation: the glide must be single and preceded by kasra for the first class; the alif must be one that cannot bear a short vowel; the exponent behaviour depends jointly on class and definiteness
fields.beginner_explanation: Sorts nouns by the shape of their final segment into three classes (المنقوص, المقصور, الممدود) and derives each class's declension behaviour from whether that final segment can bear a short vowel. Adds the definite and indefinite exponent tables for each class and a recognition test based on the ending.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: keeping the final glide in the indefinite nominative or genitive; writing a visible short vowel on an alif-final noun
fields.contrast_or_transfer: visible versus covert exponents across the three classes; definite versus indefinite behaviour within one class
fields.intermediate_explanation: inspect the final segment of the citation form; assign the class by ending shape; check definiteness
fields.prerequisite_statement: the ordinary three-case exponent table; nunation and definiteness; weak final radicals
fields.recognition_cue: a citation form ending in a glide preceded by kasra; a citation form ending in a non-vocalisable alif, written with either alif shape; a citation form ending in alif followed by hamza
fields.tutor_destination: strong: class assignment and form selection under a definiteness-by-case grid are mechanically generable

fields.advanced_explanation: singular number; annexation to a noun or to a non-first-person clitic; for the possessive member, annexation to an overt noun specifically
fields.beginner_explanation: Presents the small closed set known as الأسماء الخمسة, whose case is exponed by long vowels rather than short vowels once the noun is singular and annexed. Fixes the licensing conditions for the long-vowel exponents and enumerates the environments where the ordinary short exponents return.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: writing a short case vowel where the long-vowel exponent is licensed; freezing one long vowel across all syntactic positions
fields.contrast_or_transfer: long-vowel exponents versus ordinary short exponents for the same lexeme; a set member versus its morphologically regular near-synonym of the other gender
fields.intermediate_explanation: confirm the lexeme belongs to the closed set; confirm the token is singular; confirm the token is annexed
fields.prerequisite_statement: the ordinary three-case exponent table; annexation structure; pronominal clitic inventory and attachment
fields.recognition_cue: a kinship or relational noun immediately followed by a pronominal clitic or a genitive complement; a long vowel standing where a short case vowel would otherwise appear; the long vowel differing systematically across the three case slots
fields.tutor_destination: strong: clitic-by-case grids and licensing-condition drills are directly generable

fields.advanced_explanation: the verb must be prefix-conjugated for the mood dimension to apply at all; the final position must be visibly marked for the exponent to be read; the immediately preceding token must be inspected, not assumed absent
fields.beginner_explanation: Establishes that among Arabic verbs only the prefix-conjugated form carries a variable mood ending, and fixes the indicative as its unmarked state, defined negatively as what survives when no licensed governor stands in front of it. Introduces the two indicative exponents so that a raised ending is read as evidence about the left context rather than as a default guess.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: treating the short final vowel as the universal indicative marker; leaving the indicative vowel in place after a subjunctive governor
fields.contrast_or_transfer: vowel exponent versus retained-letter exponent inside one and the same mood; particles that precede an imperfect and govern it versus particles that precede and do not
fields.intermediate_explanation: scan the left context for a governor before assigning any mood label; classify the verb as vowel-exponed or nun-exponed so the right exponent is looked for; read the exponent from the visible pointing rather than inferring it from the verb's position
fields.prerequisite_statement: imperfect prefix conjugation with person, number and gender marking; the idea that a word ending can vary with syntactic environment; noun-initial sentence structure with a topic and a comment
fields.recognition_cue: the verb is prefix-conjugated and its final position carries a visible short vowel; a dual, masculine-plural or second-person-feminine-singular imperfect ends in a long vowel followed by nun; the token immediately to the left, if any, belongs to the non-governing class rather than to a mood-governing inventory
fields.tutor_destination: supports drills that require the exponent and the reason in the same answer, plus negative-control items where a non-governing pre-verbal marker tempts a wrong mood change
fields.unresolved_notice: the fixedness of the command form is asserted without noting the rival analysis that inflects it as a jussive

fields.advanced_explanation: the fixed reading holds for the enumerated categories only; the case slot is inferred from structure, since no exponent is available; the relative choice is conditioned by the antecedent's humanness, gender and number
fields.beginner_explanation: Separates nouns whose ending varies with syntactic position from those whose ending is fixed, and enumerates the fixed-form categories. Teaches the descriptive convention by which a fixed-form token is still assigned a case slot, so that syntactic function and surface exponent are kept apart.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: adding case exponents or nunation to a fixed-form noun; confusing the fixed interrogative with the near-homograph preposition
fields.contrast_or_transfer: varying-ending versus fixed-ending nouns in the same syntactic frames; surface exponent versus assigned case slot
fields.intermediate_explanation: identify the token as a member of a fixed category; determine the syntactic function from position and governor rather than from the ending; record the invariant final vowel
fields.prerequisite_statement: the ordinary case-exponent system; pronoun inventory and clitic attachment; demonstrative and relative usage from earlier levels
fields.recognition_cue: a token whose shape is identical across nominative, accusative and genitive positions; membership in one of the enumerated categories; a final vowel that never alternates even after a preposition
fields.tutor_destination: strong for inventory recall and category labelling; weaker for productive drills, since the forms do not alternate
fields.unresolved_notice: the status of the dual demonstratives and dual relatives is explicitly reported as disputed among grammarians

fields.advanced_explanation: stated for triliteral Form I bases; the derived-form counterparts are only previewed; the resultant-state reading is presented for states following a completed action; attributive agreement presupposes an overt head noun
fields.beginner_explanation: Introduces the patient-participle template as the argument-role counterpart of the agent participle, establishing a minimal-pair opposition built from a single root. It extends the template across weak, hamzated and doubled root classes and previews the differently shaped counterpart of the second verbal form.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: building a hollow-root patient participle with the full long-u skeleton; swapping the agent and patient participles of a root when translating
fields.contrast_or_transfer: agent template against patient template: the prefix and the vowel skeleton mark opposite argument roles; the Form I patient participle against the second-form counterpart, which differs in prefix vowel and gemination
fields.intermediate_explanation: certify the three radicals; prefix م with fatha and insert the long u before the final radical; substitute the class-specific outcome if the root is hollow, initial-hamza or doubled
fields.prerequisite_statement: the agent participle and its template; triliteral root extraction; the augment inventory, including prefixed م
fields.recognition_cue: an initial م that is not a root letter, followed by three radicals in order; a long u standing between the second and third radicals; the prefix vowel distinguishes the Form I member from the derived-form members that share the م prefix
fields.tutor_destination: high — pair generation from a single root and class-variant formation give deterministic drill items

fields.advanced_explanation: the possessed item stays nominative because it is the subject, not a complement; an indefinite subject is acceptable here only because the predicate has been fronted; the person suffix must be the attached series, since these hosts do not take free pronouns
