fields.beginner_explanation: Shows that Arabic expresses possession without any verb corresponding to 'have', using a fronted adverbial or particle phrase as the predicate with the possessed item as a delayed subject, and distinguishes the available exponents by nuance and register.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: treating the availability and ownership exponents as interchangeable; combining these hosts with a free pronoun instead of an attached one
fields.contrast_or_transfer: availability exponent versus ownership exponent; neutral register versus formal or literary alternant
fields.intermediate_explanation: choose the exponent by whether availability, ownership, accompaniment or formal register is intended; attach the appropriate person suffix to that exponent; place the resulting phrase first
fields.prerequisite_statement: verbless sentence structure with topic and comment; attached pronoun series and host selection; the genitive-governing particles
fields.recognition_cue: there is no verb in the clause, yet a possession relation is asserted; a location or benefactive phrase carrying a person suffix stands first; the item said to be possessed follows and is nominative, commonly indefinite
fields.tutor_destination: high for the frame and its case marking; the nuance contrast needs contextual items rather than isolated sentences, since the split is defeasible
fields.unresolved_notice: classification of the location hosts as particles versus adverbials is analysis-dependent and affects their case treatment; school-dependent: the behaviour of one negating operator over a verbless sentence

fields.advanced_explanation: the genitive assignment holds only for non-initial members of the annexation chain; formula reuse is licensed only for formulas with established interpretation; the tenselessness argument applies to verbal nouns, not to participles used as role terms
fields.beginner_explanation: Takes the most formal register isolated in the previous lesson and dissects its three structural pillars: agent-suppressing passives, inherited formulaic phrases, and long chains of verbal nouns in annexation that replace finite clauses. Explains deliberate redundancy as a precision device and uses a forgery anecdote to show that the register is imitable but that emotional excess betrays the imitation.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: writing an active clause with a named agent where the register requires the passive; using finite verbs where a nominal chain is expected
fields.contrast_or_transfer: agent-bearing active clause versus agent-suppressed passive; finite clause versus equivalent chain of verbal nouns
fields.intermediate_explanation: locate the finite verbs and check whether any agent is expressed; identify frozen formulas and treat them as unanalysed units; parse a nominal chain by finding its head and assigning genitive to every subsequent member
fields.prerequisite_statement: passive formation across the augmented forms; verbal-noun families; annexation and genitive assignment
fields.recognition_cue: passive-vowelled verbs with no expressed agent anywhere in the clause; damma-initial vowelling on augmented forms that begin with a connecting hamza; recurring invariant prepositional formulas at clause boundaries
fields.tutor_destination: strong: active-to-passive conversion, chain-to-clause restoration, and formula recognition all make well-defined drills

fields.advanced_explanation: separation is conditioned on a consonant-initial suffix; merger holds in every other environment, including the bare cell; the two jussive shapes are alternatives within one cell, not different cells
fields.beginner_explanation: Teaches the class whose second and third radicals are the same consonant, and reduces its whole paradigm to one conditioned alternation between a merged geminate and a separated sequence. Introduces a genuinely licensed two-way variation in the jussive, which is the learner's first encounter with more than one correct answer in a conjugation cell.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: keeping the geminate before a consonant-initial suffix; separating the radicals in a cell that should merge
fields.contrast_or_transfer: merged against separated realisations of one stem; the two licensed jussive shapes against the ungrammatical indicative-looking jussive
fields.intermediate_explanation: identify the class from the identity of the last two radicals rather than from any weak letter; read the suffix and decide between merged and separated realisation; recall the lexically stored imperfect middle vowel
fields.prerequisite_statement: root positions and the idea that a citation form may hide a radical; sound-verb paradigms in past and imperfect; mood operators and the jussive
fields.recognition_cue: a shadda on the final consonant of a citation-form verb; a surface where the last two consonants are identical and held apart by a vowel, the first of them vowelless; a geminate word carrying fatha directly after a jussive operator, which is a mood form and not an indicative
fields.tutor_destination: good for suffix-triggered cell production and for a mood drill that accepts either licensed jussive shape while rejecting the indicative; the variant set makes automatic single-answer grading unsafe without a licensing list

fields.advanced_explanation: merger requires adjacency with the first segment vowelless and the second vowelled; the merger is blocked when the ending begins with a consonant, because the required configuration does not arise; assimilation of the reflexive augment is conditioned by the identity or emphatic quality of the first radical
fields.beginner_explanation: Teaches consonant merger as a conditioned, partly obligatory and partly blocked process, and trains the learner to read a gemination mark as evidence about morphology rather than as an unanalysable spelling feature. The register focus is formal legal and religious vocabulary, where merged forms are dense.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: Extending the merger to first- and second-person past forms.; Reading every shadda on the second radical as evidence of a doubling template.
fields.contrast_or_transfer: obligatory versus blocked merger within a single verb's own paradigm; a geminate that belongs to the root versus one produced by a doubling template versus one produced by augment assimilation
fields.intermediate_explanation: identify the two segments that would be adjacent before merger; check whether the first is vowelless and the second vowelled; apply the merger, or block it when the following suffix begins with a consonant
fields.prerequisite_statement: root and template analysis; the derived verb forms, especially the t-infix form; past-tense person suffixes
fields.recognition_cue: a shadda on the final consonant of a short verb stem whose dictionary root repeats that consonant; the same lexeme appearing with a separated two-consonant sequence once a consonant-initial person suffix is attached; a shadda immediately after the first radical in a t-infix derived form
fields.tutor_destination: high — the merged versus separated split is a sharp, mechanically gradable discriminator, and the three-sources-of-shadda decision is a good diagnostic drill
fields.unresolved_notice: school-dependent: cross-boundary and near-identical merger belong to recitation norms rather than to written standard usage; analysis-dependent: the reconstructed pre-merger shape given for a gemination-bearing noun

fields.advanced_explanation: the dots are legible and the text is not defective, damaged, or in a style that suppresses pointing; undotted letters are identified by skeleton alone and have no dot signature to check; three of the letters listed as consonants also serve as long-vowel carriers, a dual role deferred to a later lesson
fields.beginner_explanation: Establishes the graphemic inventory of the writing system before any morphology or syntax is attempted: the learner learns to identify every consonant letter in its standalone citation shape, name it, attach an approximate sound value to it, and separate visually identical skeletons by their dot signatures. It is orientation material for a reader with no prior exposure to the script.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: reading a letter without checking dot count or dot side, so that members of one skeleton family are exchanged for each other; confusing letters that have similar overall silhouettes but belong to different families, such as two hook-shaped letters that face in different directions or two bowl-shaped letters differing only in dot side
fields.contrast_or_transfer: voiced versus voiceless dental fricatives, written with different dot counts on different skeletons; plain versus emphatic counterparts across four pairs
fields.intermediate_explanation: group the inventory into skeleton families before memorising individual letters; store each letter as a bundle of name, skeleton, dot signature, and approximate sound value; verify dot count and placement before committing to a letter identity
fields.prerequisite_statement: literacy in a Latin-script language; no Arabic knowledge assumed
fields.recognition_cue: locate the shared skeleton first, then count dots and register their placement; read hook-shaped letters by the orientation of the hook plus dot presence; distinguish tall vertical strokes by the presence or absence of a base hook
fields.tutor_destination: high for absolute-beginner recognition drills: confusable-pair discrimination and letter naming are closed-set and auto-gradable
fields.unresolved_notice: the plain/emphatic pairing is a teaching convenience; the historical and articulatory status of the emphatic lateral letter is disputed in the literature

fields.advanced_explanation: the state-holder must be definite by proper name, definite article, pronoun, or definite construct; a nominal state clause requires both the state-waw and a linking pronoun; a waw-less verbal state clause requires subject identity with the state-holder
fields.beginner_explanation: Develops the accusative state role from a single-word modifier into a three-way typology of realisations, and specifies the licensing conditions that make a following clause or phrase count as a state descriptor rather than as coordination, an attribute, or an adverbial complement.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: omitting the state-waw before a nominal state clause; using an indefinite nominal as the state-holder
fields.contrast_or_transfer: state descriptor versus attribute (condition versus inherent property); nominal state clause (waw required) versus verbal state clause (waw optional)
fields.intermediate_explanation: locate a definite nominal serving as subject or object; confirm that the following material predicates a condition rather than identifying the nominal; locate the linking pronoun
fields.prerequisite_statement: accusative roles; topic-comment clause structure; definiteness marking
fields.recognition_cue: the material answers 'in what condition' at the time of the main event; a definite nominal whose participant role is already filled is followed by further predication; a waw immediately precedes a topic-comment clause containing a pronoun coreferent with that nominal
fields.tutor_destination: high — holder identification, linking-pronoun identification, and realisation typing are three separable drillable skills with objective answers

fields.advanced_explanation: the precedence rule is stated for hamza standing between two vowelled or vowelless neighbours; the imperative loss is stated for exactly three initial-hamza verbs; the long-alif contraction is stated for the first-person singular imperfect
fields.beginner_explanation: Separates verbs that carry hamza as a root consonant from the weak classes, subclassifies them by the position of the hamza, and adds an orthographic layer on top of the morphology: which carrier letter the hamza is written on. Also isolates a very small set of high-frequency imperatives in which the hamza is lost.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: choosing the wrong carrier for the hamza; keeping the hamza in the three stored imperatives
fields.contrast_or_transfer: hamza-bearing roots against weak roots, stated explicitly as different categories; the three subclasses against one another by position and by consequence
fields.intermediate_explanation: locate the hamza in the root and assign the subclass; conjugate on the ordinary template for the subclass, treating hamza as a consonant; read the vowel on the hamza and the vowel before it, then apply the precedence to choose the carrier
fields.prerequisite_statement: root positions and their names; sound-verb paradigms; the short vowels and the vowelless mark
fields.recognition_cue: a hamza carrier glyph standing in one of the three root positions of an otherwise regular template; a long alif opening a first-person singular imperfect, which points to a root-initial hamza; a two-consonant imperative whose first consonant carries damma, which points back to an initial-hamza root
fields.tutor_destination: well suited to carrier-selection drills that supply the vowel environment and ask for the written form, and to a small recall drill on the stored imperatives; carrier drills must accept the variant spellings that real texts use

fields.advanced_explanation: the surrounding vowels are known, which in practice means the environment is vocalized; the hamza is of the cutting type rather than the connecting word-initial alif; after a long vowel the hamza is seatless even where the strength ranking would otherwise predict a seat
fields.beginner_explanation: Teaches the spelling of the glottal stop: that it is a consonant which usually rides on a seat letter, and that the seat is selected by the hamza's position in the word together with a ranking of the surrounding vowels. It gives separate rules for word-initial, medial and final position and notes several special configurations.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: choosing the seat by guesswork or by which letters happen to be nearby; placing the hamza below the initial alif with a vowel other than the i-vowel
fields.contrast_or_transfer: seated against seatless hamza; hamza-bearing alif against plain carrier alif
fields.intermediate_explanation: classify the hamza's position as initial, medial or final; for initial position, write alif as the seat and place the hamza below it only for the i-vowel, above it otherwise; for medial position, read the vowel on the hamza and the vowel on the preceding letter, rank them, and take the seat associated with the stronger
fields.prerequisite_statement: the short-vowel marks and vowellessness; long vowels and carrier letters; positional letter forms and the dotless yaa skeleton
fields.recognition_cue: a hamza mark above or below an alif at the start of a word; a hamza riding on a wow-letter or on a dotless yaa-shaped seat; a bare hamza sitting on the line after a long vowel or after a vowelless consonant
fields.tutor_destination: high - seat selection is a deterministic procedure over a small input space and is ideal for graded drill

fields.advanced_explanation: the governed verb must be imperfect; the purpose reading requires the goal to be unattained at reference time; the purpose-or-limit particle drops out of subjunctive government when it introduces an attained result
fields.beginner_explanation: Introduces purpose clauses as a governed construction and teaches that a small set of purpose particles places the following imperfect verb in the subjunctive, including the negative purpose compounds. Adds a mood-based contrast for the particle that can express either purpose or attained result.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: leaving the verb after a purpose particle in the indicative; retaining the final nun on a suffixed form after a purpose particle
fields.contrast_or_transfer: purpose reading with subjunctive vs. attained-result reading with indicative or perfect; purpose particle vs. causal particle of similar shape
fields.intermediate_explanation: identify the purpose particle; put the following imperfect verb in the subjunctive; select the exponent by form class: final fatha, or nun deletion for suffixed forms
fields.prerequisite_statement: the three moods and their exponents; the suffixed imperfect set and nun deletion; imperfect conjugation
fields.recognition_cue: a purpose particle stands immediately before an imperfect verb; the verb carries a final fatha where the indicative would carry a damma; a suffixed form appears without its final nun
fields.tutor_destination: moderate — the particle-to-mood mapping is easy to drill, and the purpose versus attained-result contrast is the one genuinely discriminating item; the lesson body is thin compared with its module peers
fields.unresolved_notice: whether the subjunctive is assigned by the surface particle or by a suppressed subordinator under it is a standing school dispute that the lesson does not raise

fields.advanced_explanation: shortening is triggered by a consonant-initial suffix, not by person as such; quality selection needs the underlying pattern vowel, which the surface does not show; the third-mood double shortening presupposes that no vowel-initial suffix follows
fields.beginner_explanation: Defines the hollow class by a weak middle radical and gives the environment that conditions its long medial vowel: retained before vowel-initial suffixes, shortened before consonant-initial ones. Establishes that the quality of the shortened vowel is recovered from the underlying radical and pattern rather than from the surface long vowel, and extends the alternation to the third mood.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: keeping the long medial vowel before a consonant-initial suffix; using the wrong shortened vowel quality for a verb with the second weak radical
fields.contrast_or_transfer: vowel-initial against consonant-initial suffixes as the conditioning environment; the two weak middle radicals as sources of two different shortened vowels
fields.intermediate_explanation: certify the root and locate the weak position; classify the verb as hollow rather than weak-final from that position; identify whether the suffix about to be attached begins with a vowel or a consonant
fields.prerequisite_statement: the three moods and their exponents; root-and-pattern analysis with three radical positions; recognition of weak letters as radicals
fields.recognition_cue: a long medial vowel in the citation form where a root position is expected; alternation of that long vowel with a short one across the paradigm of one lexeme; a consonant-initial suffix directly following the medial position
fields.tutor_destination: supports environment-recognition drills on suffix type, quality-selection drills including the exception subset, and mood-plus-morphology drills where both changes must be applied at once

fields.advanced_explanation: verse register for the licensed reading; the intervening material must fall in a sanctioned class; a metrical, emphatic or rhetorical motive must be identifiable
fields.beginner_explanation: Establishes the adjacency requirement holding between the two members of a construct, then presents the verse tolerance for interposing material between them, together with a routine for recovering a construct whose complement has been delayed.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: Interposing material inside a construct in prose.; Reading an apposition as a separated construct.
fields.contrast_or_transfer: prose adjacency vs verse interposition; separated construct vs apposition
fields.intermediate_explanation: locate a noun in construct shape: no nunation, meaning incomplete; search forward for a genitive noun that would complete it; check whether anything intervenes, and of what class
fields.prerequisite_statement: the construct state and genitive marking; definiteness percolation from complement to head; adjective placement relative to a construct
fields.recognition_cue: a noun without nunation that is semantically incomplete and appears to wait for a complement; an intervening particle or short phrase followed by a genitive noun that completes the head; the genitive noun is not an attributive to, or an apposition with, the intervening material
fields.tutor_destination: medium to high + the recovery routine and the apposition contrast are drillable, but most drill material would have to be authored, since the lesson's separated strings are constructed rather than cited

fields.advanced_explanation: each adjacency must be a genuine construct link; the terminal node fixes the definiteness of the whole phrase; the head's case comes from outside the chain
fields.beginner_explanation: Extends the two-term construct to chains of three or more nouns, showing that each intermediate node carries two roles at once, and fixing the case and definiteness consequences at every position in the chain.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: Placing the definite article on an intermediate node.; Marking a middle node nominative because it looks like a head.
fields.contrast_or_transfer: two-node against three-node against four-node chains; a definite-terminated chain against an indefinite-terminated chain
fields.intermediate_explanation: identify the head, determine its clause role, and assign its case from that role; walk rightwards assigning genitive to every subsequent node; verify that no non-terminal node carries article or tanwin
fields.prerequisite_statement: the two-term construct; genitive exponents; definiteness and the article
fields.recognition_cue: a run of consecutive bare nouns, each genitive after the first; absence of article and tanwin on every node but the last; a terminal node made definite by the article, by being a proper name, or by a pronominal suffix
fields.tutor_destination: high + node-role and case assignment over synthetic chains of increasing depth is a cleanly generable drill

fields.advanced_explanation: stated for noun-plus-noun sequences; the definiteness rule presupposes that the final dependent is itself unambiguously definite or indefinite; the descriptive and material types are noted to take an indefinite dependent typically
fields.beginner_explanation: Introduces annexation as the language's principal way of relating two nouns directly, with no linking particle. It fixes the two roles, the morphological suppressions on the head, the invariant genitive on the dependent, the inheritance of definiteness, and the extension of the construction into chains.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: attaching the definite article to the head of the construction; leaving the dependent in a case other than the genitive
fields.contrast_or_transfer: annexation against attributive modification, discriminated by whether both members may carry the article; definite against indefinite annexation, discriminated by the final member alone
fields.intermediate_explanation: identify the pair of adjacent nouns; strip tanwin from the head and verify it carries no article; assign the genitive to the dependent
fields.prerequisite_statement: case marking and its exponents; definiteness, the article and tanwin; genitive marking after prepositions
fields.recognition_cue: two adjacent nouns with no particle and no article on the first; the first noun carries a bare case vowel with no tanwin; the second noun carries a genitive exponent
fields.tutor_destination: high — exponent suppression, dependent marking and chain construction all give deterministic items, and the ungrammatical article placement is a strong discrimination drill

fields.advanced_explanation: the head must appear bare of article and tanwin as the lesson states the rule; the second term must be genitive in both types; the rephrasing test presupposes that the head can predicate over the second term
fields.beginner_explanation: Splits the genitive construct into a possessive or intrinsic type and a descriptive type whose head is a derived describing word, and supplies a rephrasing test that sorts a given construct into one of the two. The aim is accurate parsing of constructs whose head is an adjective or participle rather than a substantive.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: Treating every construct as an expression of ownership.; Translating both types with the same possessive English frame.
fields.contrast_or_transfer: real against non-real with the same second term; ownership against part-whole inside the real type
fields.intermediate_explanation: segment the construct into head and second term; classify the head's derivational class; attempt the rephrasing into noun plus agreeing adjective
fields.prerequisite_statement: the two-term construct and genitive marking; active and passive participles; the elative pattern
fields.recognition_cue: the head is a substantive naming a thing, a part, or a product, indicating the real type; the head is morphologically a participle, an elative, or a quasi-participial adjective, indicating a candidate non-real type; the construct restates as an entity plus an adjective describing it in one respect, confirming the non-real type
fields.tutor_destination: high + sorting constructs into the two types is a compact drill and substantive-headed constructs supply natural distractors

fields.advanced_explanation: the noun must be accusative in both constructions; the detached pronoun must match the addressee in person, gender and number; the conjunction is required between the detached pronoun and the noun in the characteristic warning pattern
fields.beginner_explanation: Teaches two verbless exhortation patterns, one urging a hearer toward a quality and one warning a hearer away from something, both realised as bare accusative nouns licensed by an unpronounced imperative.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: Leaving the exhorted noun in the nominative.; Omitting the conjunction between the detached pronoun and the noun in the warning pattern.
fields.contrast_or_transfer: encouragement against warning by polarity and by estimated licenser; bare accusative noun against detached pronoun plus conjunction
fields.intermediate_explanation: decide whether the target is to be pursued or avoided; for encouragement, place the quality in the accusative alone, repeated, or paired with a second accusative noun; for warning, either place the danger in the accusative alone or use the detached pronoun matching the addressee, then the conjunction, then the accusative noun
fields.prerequisite_statement: accusative marking of objects; imperative verb forms; the detached accusative pronoun series
fields.recognition_cue: a bare accusative noun stands as a complete utterance with no visible verb; the noun names a quality or a danger rather than an entity in a predication; the noun may be repeated or paired with a second accusative noun
fields.tutor_destination: high - drills can require converting an explicit imperative into the verbless frame and selecting the pronoun for a stated addressee

fields.advanced_explanation: the specifier must be definite in the standard pattern; the specifier must name a group containing the pronoun's referent; the case depends on which of the two patterns is used, accusative in the bare pattern and nominative after the introducing particle
fields.beginner_explanation: Teaches the construction in which a pronoun is narrowed by an accusative noun naming the group it refers to, explains the accusative through an estimated verb of specifying, and shows how the pattern is used to claim collective identity.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: Leaving the specifying noun in the nominative in the bare pattern.; Marking the noun accusative after the introducing particle.
fields.contrast_or_transfer: the bare accusative pattern against the introducing-particle nominative pattern; specification against the vocative
fields.intermediate_explanation: place the independent pronoun first; select the noun naming the group and make it definite; mark it accusative, or introduce it with the vocative-like particle and mark it nominative in that variant
fields.prerequisite_statement: independent pronouns; definiteness by article and by construct annexation; accusative marking and its plural exponents
fields.recognition_cue: an independent pronoun opens the clause; a definite noun in the accusative follows it immediately; that noun names a group of which the pronoun is a member
fields.tutor_destination: high - drills can require switching between the two patterns and repairing case errors in each

fields.advanced_explanation: the verb must belong to the mental-state class; the two elements must be capable of forming a topic-predicate pair on their own; the case pattern must be applied uniformly rather than mixing accusative and nominative across the pair
fields.beginner_explanation: Teaches that a mental-state verb placed after the material it would otherwise govern loses its accusative assignment, so that material stays a nominative sentence with the verb appended as a parenthetical comment.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: Treating cancellation by position and blocking by an intervening particle as one phenomenon.; Marking the preceding elements accusative when the verb comes last.
fields.contrast_or_transfer: verb-initial assignment against verb-final cancellation; cancellation by position against suspension by particle
fields.intermediate_explanation: identify the mental-state verb and its linear position relative to the two complements; if the verb precedes both, apply the double-accusative frame; if the verb stands between them, choose either assignment or cancellation and apply it consistently to both elements
fields.prerequisite_statement: double-accusative mental-state verbs; topic and predicate in nominal sentences; suspension of governance from the previous lesson
fields.recognition_cue: the clause opens with a nominative topic and predicate; a mental-state verb follows that complete clause; the trailing verb carries first-person or other subject inflection of its own
fields.tutor_destination: high - drills can present one propositional content in all three positions and require the matching case pattern for each

fields.advanced_explanation: particle-based recognition holds only when the particle heads its clause; performative readings of first-person verbs require an addressee and a here-and-now utterance situation; directive readings of assertives require an authority or a fact that carries authority
fields.beginner_explanation: Establishes the top-level rhetorical partition between utterances that assert a state of affairs and utterances that enact something by being said, and trains the learner to sort utterance types into that partition even when the surface form points the other way. Serves as the organizing frame for the whole module.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: treating every interrogative shape as a request for information; reading grammatical form as a direct index of function
fields.contrast_or_transfer: assertive versus enacting as the top-level split; request-type versus non-request-type enacting subtypes
fields.intermediate_explanation: apply the truth-value test, then sort the enacting result into request-type versus non-request-type, then name the subtype; for a surface assertive, ask what act the speaker is performing before assigning force; for an oath, identify the swearing particle and treat the following clause as the sworn content
fields.prerequisite_statement: imperative and jussive formation; prohibition with the jussive negator; interrogative particles
fields.recognition_cue: ask whether a true/false verdict fits the content; if it does not, the utterance is enacting; check for a dedicated wish/urging particle at the head of the clause; check for a first-person imperfective verb of the performative lexical class addressed to a hearer
fields.tutor_destination: high — a clean binary sort with a named subtype layer supports graded drills, provided dual-function items are excluded or scored separately

fields.advanced_explanation: the referent must be constant across the break; the break must be unexpected given the pattern established before it; a purpose must be assignable, otherwise the shift is not evidence of the device
fields.beginner_explanation: Treats a deliberate break in the expected continuation of person, number or tense across a stretch of discourse as a licensed stylistic device rather than as an inconsistency to be repaired, and pairs each direction of shift with the effect claimed for it.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: reading the shift as a grammatical error; expecting the device to be rare and therefore missing instances
fields.contrast_or_transfer: person shift versus number shift versus tense shift; deliberate shift versus agreement error
fields.intermediate_explanation: establish what the expected continuation was; locate the break and name the dimension on which it occurs; confirm that the referent did not change, which is what separates the device from ordinary reference tracking
fields.prerequisite_statement: subject agreement affixes across all persons and numbers; independent and attached pronoun series; perfective, imperfective and imperative stems
fields.recognition_cue: a change in subject-agreement person or number across adjacent predicates that share a referent; a switch between a pronoun series for one person and a series for another while the referent stays constant; a switch from perfective narration to imperfective within the same event line
fields.tutor_destination: high — detection over a supplied passage is mechanically checkable given the inflectional features; naming the effect is not checkable and should stay a discussion item
fields.unresolved_notice: school-dependent: narrower classical definitions restrict the device to shifts among speaker, addressee and absent person, while the three-dimension version taught here is the broader formulation

fields.advanced_explanation: the prosthetic alif is added only when the residue would otherwise be unpronounceable at the start of an utterance; the vowel computation reads the stem vowel of the imperfect, not the vowel of the perfect; the derivation is defined for addressee persons
fields.beginner_explanation: Derives the command form from the third-mood stem by removing the person prefix and, where the residue would begin with a vowelless consonant, supplying a prosthetic connecting alif whose vowel is computed from the stem. Separates positive commands from negative ones, which are built on a governed imperfect rather than on the command form.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: putting the wrong vowel on the prosthetic alif; prefixing a prosthetic alif to a fourth-pattern command
fields.contrast_or_transfer: a command form against the governed imperfect it was derived from, differing by the presence of the prefix; a prosthetic connecting alif against a pattern hamza that belongs to the word
fields.intermediate_explanation: put the verb into the third mood; remove the person prefix; test whether the residue begins with a vowelless consonant
fields.prerequisite_statement: the third mood and its exponents; the prohibitive negator and its construction; identification of derived verb patterns, in particular the fourth
fields.recognition_cue: a verb form with no person prefix opening with a plain alif that carries a vowel; the same stem shape as the governed imperfect once the prefix is stripped; a derived-form command opening with a written hamza rather than a plain alif
fields.tutor_destination: supports staged derivation drills where each intermediate step is checked, prosthetic-vowel drills, and polarity drills where the negative form must switch construction rather than shape
fields.unresolved_notice: the inflectional status of the command form is a standing school dispute and is stated here as settled

fields.advanced_explanation: the categorial tests must be applied in order because later tests presuppose earlier exclusions; elision applies only when a word precedes within the same utterance; the vowel rule for the connecting alif is stated for commands of triliteral verbs
fields.beginner_explanation: Splits word-initial alif into two categories according to whether its glottal onset survives inside connected speech, and supplies a category-based decision procedure keyed to word class, verb length and a memorised closed noun list. Closes with a note that in unpointed writing the two categories are not distinguishable from the orthography alone.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: pronouncing a connecting hamza in the middle of an utterance; assigning the same hamza type to commands of triliteral and of derived verbs
fields.contrast_or_transfer: a triliteral command against a fourth-pattern command, differing in hamza type; a member of the closed noun list against an ordinary noun
fields.intermediate_explanation: ask whether the word is the definite article; ask whether it belongs to the closed noun list; for a perfect verb, count the letters of the pattern
fields.prerequisite_statement: command derivation and the prosthetic alif from the preceding lesson; derived verb patterns and their letter counts; the definite article as a prefixed element
fields.recognition_cue: in pointed text, the presence or absence of the hamza mark on the initial alif; membership of the word in one of the listed categories, applied in order; the letter count and derived pattern of a perfect verb
fields.tutor_destination: supports sorting drills over mixed word lists, connected-reading drills where the elision must actually be performed, and closed-list recall drills

fields.advanced_explanation: the emphatic member is licensed only clause-initially; the subordinating member is licensed by a preceding governor that selects a clausal complement; the geminate adversative is licensed only before a nominal or an enclitic pronoun
fields.beginner_explanation: Installs the second abrogator family — particles whose case effect is the exact mirror of the verbal family taught earlier — and differentiates its first three members not by case behaviour, which they share, but by clause position and by the environment that selects each one.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: leaving the first element nominative after a particle of this family; marking the predicate accusative after a particle of this family
fields.contrast_or_transfer: the verbal family against the particle family as mirror images of one another; emphatic against subordinating member, separated by clause position and by the presence of a selecting verb
fields.intermediate_explanation: identify the particle and confirm it belongs to this roster; assign the accusative to the element immediately following and the nominative to the predicate; select the member by environment: clause-initial emphasis, post-cognition-verb subordination, or adversative contrast
fields.prerequisite_statement: the verbal abrogator family and its signature; case exponents and their names; enclitic pronoun forms
fields.recognition_cue: a clause-initial particle of this roster followed immediately by an accusative-marked nominal; a nominative-marked predicate following that nominal, which is the diagnostic that distinguishes this family from the verbal one; the particle carrying an enclitic pronoun, in which case the accusative slot has no independent word
fields.tutor_destination: high — the mirror-image case drill against the verbal family is the sharpest available discrimination exercise for this module

fields.advanced_explanation: the case signature is inherited without modification from the earlier members; the wish member is appropriate where the wished-for state is presented as unrealized or unrealizable; the hope member is appropriate where the outcome is presented as genuinely possible
fields.beginner_explanation: Completes the particle family with three members that share the established case signature exactly and are therefore taught purely as a semantic discrimination task: resemblance, counterfactual wish, and attainable hope. The grammatical content is a restatement; the instructional content is modal choice.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: using the wish member for an outcome that is actually likely; leaving the first governed element nominative after these particles
fields.contrast_or_transfer: unattainable wish against attainable hope, presented as the lesson's central discrimination; the emphatic resemblance particle against the ordinary comparison preposition and comparison noun
fields.intermediate_explanation: identify the particle as a member of the family and apply the established slot assignment unchanged; for production, choose between the wish and hope members according to whether the state of affairs is presented as attainable; reserve the resemblance member for emphatic comparison and use the ordinary comparison devices otherwise
fields.prerequisite_statement: L2.M2.03 case signature and slot labels for this family; enclitic pronoun forms; the notion of a nominal predication
fields.recognition_cue: any of the three particles heading a nominal predication, with the following element accusative; a nominative predicate as the confirmation that the particle family, not the verbal family, is at work; the particle carrying an enclitic pronoun as its governed element
fields.tutor_destination: high — the wish/hope choice is a clean situation-to-particle drill that does not depend on case at all

fields.advanced_explanation: an action-denoting source verb underlies the form; the annexed-complement reading requires a transitive source verb; the intensive reading requires habitual or defining behaviour, not a single event
fields.beginner_explanation: Introduces the intensive agent templates as a graded strengthening of the plain agent noun, covering habitual, professional and excessive performance, and shows that these forms keep the government properties of the verb they come from.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: assigning a فَعيل-shaped word to the wrong class; reading the taa on the intensive template as feminine
fields.contrast_or_transfer: plain agent noun versus intensive: degree and habituality; intensive versus quality adjective on the shared فَعيل shape
fields.intermediate_explanation: isolate the root; verify that the source verb denotes an action rather than a bare state; select the intensive template
fields.prerequisite_statement: the bare-triliteral agent noun; the quality-adjective templates from the previous lesson; annexation and genitive marking
fields.recognition_cue: doubled middle radical with a long-alif ending in an agentive sense; prefixed mim with kasra plus a long alif, read as a person rather than a tool; a long waw or long ya in the second syllable with an agentive or attributive sense
fields.tutor_destination: strong: degree-scale drills over one root, and forced-choice drills between the intensive and the quality adjective on the shared template

fields.advanced_explanation: there must be an overt pronoun on the verb linking back to the pre-posed noun; the verb must be able in principle to take the pre-posed noun as an argument for the accusative reading; nothing in the left periphery may block an accusative opening
fields.beginner_explanation: Teaches the construction in which a noun stands before a verb that already carries an object pronoun coreferential with that noun, and shows the learner how to decide what case the pre-posed noun takes and what is taken to govern it.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: Treating a pre-posed noun with a resumptive pronoun and one without as the same construction with the same analysis.; Selecting a human masculine plural clitic for a non-human plural antecedent.
fields.contrast_or_transfer: bare pre-posing without a pronoun versus pre-posing with a pronoun; canonical verb-first order versus either pre-posed order
fields.intermediate_explanation: locate the noun standing before the verb; locate the clitic pronoun on the verb and confirm it refers back to that noun; ask whether the verb is of a type that could govern the noun directly as an object
fields.prerequisite_statement: direct object and accusative marking; attached object pronouns and their paradigm; topic and predicate in nominal sentences
fields.recognition_cue: a noun precedes a finite verb instead of following it; the verb carries an attached object pronoun; that pronoun has no antecedent other than the pre-posed noun
fields.tutor_destination: high - supports drills on clitic agreement, on case assignment under a left-peripheral particle, and on converting canonical order into the pre-posed form

fields.advanced_explanation: one pole must be genuinely absent, not merely unexpressed by an exponent; the attributed property in the implied type must belong to a different semantic field from the stated subject; the clue must be present, otherwise the sentence is an ordinary statement
fields.beginner_explanation: Extends the comparison frame by deleting one of its two obligatory poles and names the two resulting configurations by which pole survives. Introduces the contextual signal that blocks the literal reading and directs recovery of the deleted pole.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: reading a doubly-omitted comparison as an explicit metaphor because both look like bare nominal predication; labelling an expression as implied metaphor without identifying the clue that recovers the deleted image
fields.contrast_or_transfer: explicit versus implied by which pole survives; metaphor versus the doubly-omitted comparison by pole count
fields.intermediate_explanation: locate the expression that resists a literal reading; ask what is being described and what it is being set against; ask whether the image is named openly
fields.prerequisite_statement: the four comparison slots and the composite type labels; nominal predication; verb-subject semantic selection
fields.recognition_cue: a nominal denoting a category incompatible with its predicate or with the action around it; a predicate or attribute drawn from a semantic field alien to its stated subject; no comparison exponent anywhere in the clause
fields.tutor_destination: high for two-way type discrimination and clue identification; items must be authored because detection depends on world knowledge rather than on form

fields.advanced_explanation: the accusative rule for the excluded item holds only when the clause is affirmative and the set is stated; the appositive option arises only in a negative clause with the set stated; role-driven case applies only when the set is left out
fields.beginner_explanation: Teaches the exclusion construction: its three-part anatomy, the one particle and two nouns that introduce the excluded item, and a case-selection table conditioned on whether the clause is affirmative or negative and whether the set excluded from is stated or left out.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: treating the nominal exclusion words as invariable particles; forcing the accusative on the excluded item when the set is not stated
fields.contrast_or_transfer: affirmative against negative clause behaviour; set stated against set omitted
fields.intermediate_explanation: locate the set, the exclusion word and the excluded item; determine whether the clause is affirmative or negative; determine whether the set is stated or left out
fields.prerequisite_statement: nominative, accusative and genitive marking; annexation and the genitive complement; negation of verbal and nominal clauses
fields.recognition_cue: an exclusion word standing between a set-denoting expression and a following noun; an accusative noun after the exclusion particle in an affirmative clause; a nominative noun after the exclusion particle in a negated clause with no set expressed
fields.tutor_destination: very strong: the case-selection table is small, closed and fully mechanical, so forced-choice and fill-in drills can be generated and graded exactly.
fields.unresolved_notice: school-dependent: the negative-clause alternation is presented as a free choice, whereas the tradition records a preference between the two readings that this lesson does not attribute; the case behaviour of the second nominal exclusion word is stated only through its annexation and not through its own inflectional class, which is itself disputed

fields.advanced_explanation: the licensing decision is made on the opening element of the response, not on the whole clause; the connective attaches at the left edge of the response; a bare imperfect response takes no connective
fields.beginner_explanation: Decomposes the conditional sentence into its two named halves and introduces the licensing question that governs the response half: whether the response must be introduced by the connective فـ. Frames this as a decision driven by what the response opens with, and contrasts it with the bare jussive response taught in the previous lesson.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: prefixing the connective to a response that is already a bare jussive verb; omitting the connective before a response that opens with a future marker
fields.contrast_or_transfer: connective-introduced response vs. bare jussive response; response verb after the connective plus future marker (indicative) vs. response verb with no connective (jussive)
fields.intermediate_explanation: identify the trigger and mark the condition verb as jussive; read the first element of the response clause; classify that element against the licensing list
fields.prerequisite_statement: the conditional trigger inventory and jussive marking; nominal vs. verbal sentence distinction; future markers, negators and their mood requirements
fields.recognition_cue: a conditional trigger opens the sentence and a second clause follows; the response opens with a noun or pronoun rather than a verb; the response opens with a future marker, a negator, a command form, an emphatic particle or a probability particle
fields.tutor_destination: strong — the licensing decision is a clean classification drill over response openers, and the wrong-mood-after-connective error is a good discriminating item
fields.unresolved_notice: the mood status of the imperative is a standing school dispute and the lesson asserts one side; double government of the condition verb by both لم and the conditional trigger is analysis-dependent

fields.advanced_explanation: both verbs are imperfect; the response is a bare verb with no intervening connective or operator; the trigger belongs to the jazm-imposing subset of condition words
fields.beginner_explanation: Establishes the conditional sentence as a two-slot governing frame in which a single trigger word imposes one mood on two separate verbs, and teaches the closed inventory of trigger words that do this. Pairs the syntactic rule with the class-sensitive morphology needed to actually spell the governed forms.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: marking only the condition verb and leaving the response verb with indicative marking; reading the sukun-final conditional trigger as its geminate emphatic homograph
fields.contrast_or_transfer: sukun-final conditional trigger vs. its geminate emphatic homograph, which takes a following noun in the accusative; human-reference vs. non-human-reference condition nouns
fields.intermediate_explanation: locate the trigger word; assign the immediately following verb to the condition slot; assign the consequence verb to the response slot
fields.prerequisite_statement: imperfect conjugation and its indicative marking; weak-root classification into hollow and defective; dual and plural verb suffixes
fields.recognition_cue: a member of the closed trigger list stands at the opening of the clause; the first following imperfect verb lacks the indicative final damma; a second verb later in the same sentence carries a matching reduced ending
fields.tutor_destination: strong — slot identification and indicative-to-jussive conversion are directly drillable, with weak class as the difficulty axis
fields.unresolved_notice: the categorial and positional analysis of the three non-particle condition words is analysis-dependent

fields.advanced_explanation: rational reference conditions the choice between the two who/what interrogatives; the verb-adjacent variant of the what-interrogative is preferred before verbs; the singular accusative counted noun applies to the interrogative quantity use
fields.beginner_explanation: Teaches the two ways Arabic forms questions, separating the particles that request a yes-or-no judgement from the words that request a specific piece of information, and assigns each interrogative word a syntactic slot.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: placing a question particle somewhere other than the front of the clause; using the non-rational interrogative to ask about a person
fields.contrast_or_transfer: polar particle versus information interrogative; rational versus non-rational interrogative
fields.intermediate_explanation: decide whether the question requests a truth judgement or a specific constituent; for polar questions, place the particle at the front and leave the clause otherwise intact; for information questions, choose the interrogative matching the requested category (person, thing, place, time, manner, reason, quantity)
fields.prerequisite_statement: verbless and verbal sentence structure; case labels and positional case; the rational/non-rational distinction used earlier for agreement
fields.recognition_cue: a clause-initial closed-class word with no lexical content of its own signals a question; polar particles are followed by an otherwise complete clause; information interrogatives leave a gap corresponding to the requested constituent
fields.tutor_destination: high — word order and interrogative selection are objectively checkable; the register difference between the two polar particles is not

fields.advanced_explanation: the literal reading must remain coherent; a conventional or contextually inferable chain must connect the literal state to the intended meaning; the audience must share the cultural premise the chain relies on
fields.beginner_explanation: Introduces the third figure of the imagery science, defined not by deletion or by resemblance but by the survival of a coherent literal reading alongside an intended further meaning. Splits it into three subtypes according to what the indirect expression points at, and makes the inference chain from surface to intent explicit.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: classifying an expression as metaphor when its literal reading is perfectly coherent; reading the entity-pointing subtype label as though it named a quality
fields.contrast_or_transfer: this figure versus metaphor decided by whether the literal reading survives; quality-pointing versus entity-pointing subtypes, that is an adjective-like target versus a noun-like target
fields.intermediate_explanation: test whether the literal reading is possible; a possible literal reading keeps the case in this class; state the intended meaning explicitly; classify by whether the target is a quality, an entity, or an attribution via something related
fields.prerequisite_statement: annexation, including an adjective as first term; definite descriptive phrases used referentially; prepositional predication with a locative sense
fields.recognition_cue: an adjective annexed to a body-part or possession noun where the literal reading remains coherent; a definite descriptive phrase standing in the syntactic slot a proper name would occupy; an abstract quality noun predicated as located in or upon something belonging to a person
fields.tutor_destination: high for subtype classification and for chain-reconstruction drills; the chain step-out is unusually well suited to a written free-response drill with a checkable skeleton
fields.unresolved_notice: school-dependent: whether the figure is literal or figurative usage is disputed and the lesson presents one side

fields.advanced_explanation: default mood retention is specific to this negator; the past and future negators require their respective dependent moods on the verb; the prohibitive reading requires the dependent mood associated with commands
fields.beginner_explanation: Teaches the negator that leaves an imperfect verb in its default mood, contrasts it with the other negating operators by tense and by mood effect, and separates it from the identically written prohibitive.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: using the past negator when present-time negation is intended; putting the verb into a dependent mood after this negator
fields.contrast_or_transfer: statement negator versus prohibitive, distinguished only by the verb's mood; this negator versus the past negator versus the future negator, by mood and time reference
fields.intermediate_explanation: decide the time reference and the form of the verb to be negated; select the operator that matches that combination; place the operator immediately before the verb
fields.prerequisite_statement: imperfect verb forms and their default mood endings; the mood labels; person marking on imperfect verbs
fields.recognition_cue: the negator stands immediately before an imperfect verb; the verb keeps its default mood ending, which is the signal that this is the statement negator; a dependent mood ending on the following verb signals the prohibitive reading instead
fields.tutor_destination: high — operator selection and mood outcomes give unambiguous drill items, and the negative/prohibitive minimal pair is a natural discrimination exercise

fields.advanced_explanation: the genitive analysis requires the complement to be a bare noun that can serve as an annexation term; the relative analysis of the suffixed element is required, not optional, when a clause follows; the specification analysis requires accusative marking
fields.beginner_explanation: Teaches the internal composition of the fixed singling-out expression لا سيّما and the case options its complement may take, showing that the complement's definiteness or clausal status selects among a genitive-only reading, a three-way case choice, or a relative reading of its final element.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: Putting a definite complement in the accusative.; Keeping the expletive analysis of the suffixed element when a clause follows.
fields.contrast_or_transfer: definite complement (one licensed case) versus indefinite complement (three licensed cases); nominal complement (suffixed element expletive) versus clausal complement (suffixed element relative)
fields.intermediate_explanation: Check definiteness of the complement: if definite, assign genitive as annexation term (with the nominative variant noted as attested).; If not definite, check whether the complement is a clause: if so, read the suffixed element as a relative noun and the clause as its content.; If the complement is an indefinite noun, choose among three case options and state the analysis matching the chosen case.
fields.prerequisite_statement: genus-negating construction and its subject noun; annexation and genitive assignment; specification as an accusative category
fields.recognition_cue: whether the complement carries the definite article or is a proper name; whether the complement is a bare noun or a full clause containing a verb; the case vowel actually realized on the complement, which selects among competing analyses rather than deciding grammaticality
fields.tutor_destination: medium — drills must accept a set of correct answers for indefinite complements, so a single-answer drill format would mark valid responses wrong.
fields.unresolved_notice: school-dependent: the case options for definite and indefinite complements are attributed differently across grammarians, and the lesson presents one option as classical standard while conceding the other is defensible

fields.advanced_explanation: stated for coordination of single nominals of equal rank; the case of the joined-to element is already fixed by its own governor; only case has to match; definiteness, gender and number do not
fields.beginner_explanation: Establishes coordination as a named grammatical relation in which a following element inherits the case of the peer element it is joined to, and separates six frequent connectors by the semantic distinction each carries (plain addition, tight sequence, delayed sequence, alternation, correction, adversative contrast). The aim is production of connected prose, not resolution of ambiguous attachment.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: using the tight-sequence connector in a context that states an interval; using the correction connector for a plain contrast where nothing is cancelled
fields.contrast_or_transfer: tight sequence versus delayed sequence; correction versus adversative contrast
fields.intermediate_explanation: locate the constituent preceding the connector and read its case; assign that same case to the constituent following the connector; when several elements are chained, hold every member in that case
fields.prerequisite_statement: the three cases and their exponents; the notion that a case is assigned by a governor; basic verbal and nominal sentence structure
fields.recognition_cue: a connector standing between two constituents of equal syntactic rank; the second constituent bearing the same case exponent as the first; for the sequencing pair, an interval that is stated or inferable from the surrounding narrative rather than from the connector
fields.tutor_destination: strong for production drills (case-matching fill-ins, forced choice within the sequencing pair and within the adversative pair); weak for analysis drills, because the semantic distinctions rest on world knowledge the drill must itself supply

fields.advanced_explanation: the regime applies over a nominal (equative) predication, not over a verbal one; the frozen member is presented as confined to present-time reference; the accusative exponent lands on the predicate word itself, whether that word is an adjective, a participle, or a noun
fields.beginner_explanation: Introduces the abrogator class as a functional category of governors that cancel the all-nominative default of a noun-initial predication, and installs its first family through four high-frequency verbal members together with their inflectional behaviour. The lesson's second aim is to make the learner locate two distinct governed slots and state a case reason for each.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: leaving the predicate element in the nominative after a family member; marking the first governed element accusative after a family member
fields.contrast_or_transfer: default equative predication (both elements nominative) against the governed one (predicate accusative); the four members set against one another on an aspectual axis
fields.intermediate_explanation: identify the governor as a member of this family; assign the nominative element to the اسم slot and the accusative element to the خبر slot; verify that the accusative exponent sits on the predicate element and not on the subject
fields.prerequisite_statement: the noun-initial predication and its two nominative roles; the case values and their default exponents; perfective and imperfective inflection for person and number
fields.recognition_cue: an equative predication preceded by a member of the listed verbal roster; a single accusative-marked nominal or adjective after a verb of state where no transitive-object reading is available; a conjugated governor whose subject is realized only as an affix, leaving the accusative complement as the sole independently marked governed element
fields.tutor_destination: high — minimal-pair case drills, member selection by aspect, and negation-route selection are all directly drillable from the lesson's own contrast sets

fields.advanced_explanation: clustering is a memory aid, not a generative rule; the fluctuating members are safer with feminine concord but not exclusively so; unpaired body parts named in the lesson stay masculine
fields.beginner_explanation: Isolates the class of nouns that take feminine concord although nothing in their form shows it, organises that class into semantic clusters to make it memorisable, and drills the concord consequences on adjectives, deictics, pronouns and verbs.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: giving masculine concord to the noun for soul or self; collapsing a marker-feminine noun and a convention-feminine noun into one category
fields.contrast_or_transfer: unmarked feminine versus marked feminine; paired versus unpaired body-part nouns
fields.intermediate_explanation: store gender together with meaning when acquiring any new noun; when an unmarked noun is encountered, check the memorised class before defaulting to masculine; apply feminine concord across all four target types once membership is established
fields.prerequisite_statement: the gender system and its three visible endings; adjective, demonstrative and pronoun concord; past and present verb inflection basics
fields.recognition_cue: the noun shows no feminine affix yet a concord target in the clause is feminine; the noun falls into one of the taught semantic clusters; lexicon entry marks the noun feminine
fields.tutor_destination: high + a closed list with deterministic concord outcomes is ideal flashcard and cloze material, provided fluctuating members are drilled separately
fields.unresolved_notice: whether a given extended-alif noun is marker-feminine or convention-feminine is analysis-dependent and affects how the class boundary is drawn

fields.advanced_explanation: a non-resemblance link must be nameable; the direction of transfer must be determinable from the context; the predicate or governor must be the element that rules out the literal sense
fields.beginner_explanation: Separates non-resemblance figurative transfer from resemblance-based metaphor and supplies a named inventory of the semantic links that license each transfer. Trains the learner to name the licensing link and its direction rather than merely notice that a word is used non-literally.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: classifying a transfer as this figure when the ground of the transfer is actually resemblance; swapping the part-for-whole and whole-for-part labels
fields.contrast_or_transfer: part named versus whole named; place named versus contents named
fields.intermediate_explanation: establish that the literal sense fails in this position; exclude a resemblance basis, which would select metaphor instead; exclude a coherent literal reading, which would select the metonymy class instead
fields.prerequisite_statement: the metaphor class and its resemblance basis; the metonymy class and its literal-possibility criterion; verb argument selection and the notion of a semantic clash
fields.recognition_cue: a token whose literal denotation cannot satisfy the predicate it stands under; an identifiable non-resemblance link between the literal sense and the required sense; body-part nouns standing as arguments of predicates that only whole persons can satisfy
fields.tutor_destination: high for link-naming drills with a direction field; the two internally reversed specimens must be excluded from any item bank until repaired
fields.unresolved_notice: several anchor specimens are classically disputed between figurative transfer and elided annexation, and some schools reject the figurative category for them outright

fields.advanced_explanation: verbal-noun status is a hard precondition; causal reading is a hard precondition; identity of agent and of time between motive and main verb is a hard precondition
fields.beginner_explanation: Presents the accusative verbal noun that states the motive for an action, the three admissibility conditions it must satisfy, the prepositional paraphrase used when those conditions fail, and the test the lesson offers for telling it apart from the reinforcing verbal noun of the previous lesson.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: putting a non-derived ordinary noun in the motive slot; using a definite verbal noun in the bare accusative
fields.contrast_or_transfer: cause accusative versus reinforcing verbal noun — different root and why-question versus same root and how-question; bare accusative versus preposition plus verbal noun
fields.intermediate_explanation: confirm that the candidate is a verbal noun rather than an ordinary noun; confirm that it answers a why-question rather than a how-question; confirm that the one who acts and the one who is motivated are the same, at the same time
fields.prerequisite_statement: verbal nouns and their derivation across verb forms; accusative marking; definiteness marking and annexation
fields.recognition_cue: an indefinite accusative verbal noun that answers a why-question about the main verb; an accusative verbal noun whose root differs from the verb's root; an accusative verbal noun followed by a preposition introducing the thing desired or feared
fields.tutor_destination: strong for condition-checking drills and for forced-choice discrimination between the two verbal-noun accusatives; weaker for production, since motive choice is open-ended.

fields.advanced_explanation: verse register; a metrical or rhyme requirement at the position; the lexeme must have a determinate prose default to deviate from
fields.beginner_explanation: Isolates the two inverse operations on noun-final long endings, dropping the final glottal stop so an extended ending becomes a shortened one and supplying it in the reverse direction, and fixes the principle that the operation touches sound shape only while the parse is computed from the prose form.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: Swapping which term shortens and which extends.; Writing a shortened verse form in prose.
fields.contrast_or_transfer: shortening vs extending as inverse directions; visible vs estimated case marker for the same syntactic role
fields.intermediate_explanation: note whether the attested ending is a bare final alif or alif plus glottal stop; retrieve the prose default form for the lexeme from the lexicon; if the two differ, name the operation by its direction
fields.prerequisite_statement: final-weak and hamzated noun endings; visible vs estimated case markers; the three-case system
fields.recognition_cue: the word sits at a line-final or hemistich-final position, or at any position where the meter fixes the syllable count; the ending is a bare final alif where the lexicon predicts alif plus glottal stop, or the reverse; the lexicon default for the same lexeme differs from the attested shape
fields.tutor_destination: high for direction discrimination and class identification; the transformation drills are unambiguous, though several drill targets are constructed forms rather than cited attestations
fields.unresolved_notice: the acceptability of the extending direction is disputed in the classical literature, and the lesson presents it flatly as accepted

fields.advanced_explanation: both templates presuppose a Form I verb; the manner template additionally presupposes lexical attestation for that root; the vowel discriminator is only available where the text is vowelled or the context is decisive
fields.beginner_explanation: Teaches two verbal-noun sub-types distinguished by a single vowel on the first radical: one counting a single occurrence of the action, the other describing the characteristic manner in which it is performed. Shows how narrative prose exploits the first to freeze a moment and the second to characterise a person.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: swapping the two first-radical vowels; assuming every root offers both members
fields.contrast_or_transfer: occurrence versus manner on one and the same root; fatha versus kasra on the first radical as the whole of the formal difference
fields.intermediate_explanation: confirm the verb is Form I before applying either template; decide whether the intended sense is a count of one event or a description of how the event is performed; vowel the first radical accordingly
fields.prerequisite_statement: verbal nouns of Form I; verbal nouns of derived forms; the feminine ending as a derivational marker
fields.recognition_cue: a short feminine-ended deverbal noun with fatha on the first radical and no vowel on the second; the same shape with kasra on the first radical; co-occurrence with the numeral for one or with a counting context, pointing to the occurrence reading
fields.tutor_destination: strong: the minimal pair is ideal for a forced-choice vowelling drill, and the gaps make good negative items

fields.advanced_explanation: the accusative-governing use of a verbal noun requires an underlying transitive verb; the participle rewrite requires an identifiable agent; the reduced final-weak participle shape applies only in the indefinite nominative and genitive
fields.beginner_explanation: Teaches the learner to rewrite one propositional content three ways using the finite verb, the verbal noun and the active participle from a single root, and to state what each rewrite changes in emphasis and in clause structure.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: using a participle where a single completed event is meant; marking the agent nominative after a verbal noun
fields.contrast_or_transfer: verb against verbal noun against participle for the same content; accusative object retained against prepositional attachment
fields.intermediate_explanation: identify the root and derive the three forms; for a verbal-noun rewrite, demote the subject to genitive and decide whether the object stays accusative or attaches by preposition; for a participle rewrite, make the agent the subject and place the participle in predicate position or under a copular verb
fields.prerequisite_statement: root and pattern derivation; verbal noun families; active participle formation
fields.recognition_cue: a possessive construction whose head is a verbal noun and whose second term denotes the agent; an accusative noun following a verbal-noun possessive construction, marking retained verbal government; a participle in predicate position with the agent as an independent subject
fields.tutor_destination: high — triad completion and clause rewriting are both mechanical enough to score, and the final-weak declension gives a sharp discrimination item

fields.advanced_explanation: distinguishing the class from place nouns requires a vocalized prefix; the modern machine template is register-bound and does not extend to traditional tools; the semantic tendencies are described as tendencies, not licensing conditions
fields.beginner_explanation: Teaches the noun naming the tool with which an action is performed, unifies its three classical templates by the prefix vowel, states openly that the choice among the three is lexical rather than derivable, and adds the modern machine template as a functional extension.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: mixing up the prefix vowels of the instrument and place classes; trying to predict which instrument template a root takes
fields.contrast_or_transfer: instrument noun versus place or time noun, by prefix vowel; classical instrument templates versus the modern machine template
fields.intermediate_explanation: isolate the root; recall the lexicalized template for that root rather than deriving it; confirm the class by the prefix vowel
fields.prerequisite_statement: place and time nouns from the previous lesson, including their prefix vowel; root extraction and separation of affixal from radical letters; broken plural shapes
fields.recognition_cue: prefixed mim carrying kasra over a three-radical stem; a long alif before the last radical, or a taa marbuta ending, or neither; the referent is a manipulable object rather than a location or a person
fields.tutor_destination: strong for recall and for prefix-vowel discrimination; weak for production drills, since the lesson states that the template cannot be predicted

fields.advanced_explanation: scope is strong triliteral verbs; the mood marker is determined by what governs the clause, not by the verb itself; the middle vowel must be known per lexeme before the form can be produced
fields.beginner_explanation: Introduces the imperfect (المضارع) of strong verbs as a circumfixal paradigm: a person-marking prefix plus number/gender endings, and adds a first pass at the three moods signalled on the final position.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: leaving the unmarked final vowel in place after the complementiser; applying the vowel exponent to a nun-bearing form, that is, keeping its nun
fields.contrast_or_transfer: perfect marking by ending only versus imperfect marking by prefix plus ending; indicative versus subjunctive versus jussive final markers
fields.intermediate_explanation: choose the prefix that matches the person; attach it to the imperfect stem carrying the verb's lexically stored middle vowel; add the number/gender ending for the target slot
fields.prerequisite_statement: perfect conjugation and the thirteen-slot inventory; personal pronoun inventory; short vowels and sukun
fields.recognition_cue: an imperfect form opens with one of four short-vowel prefixes; the prefix narrows the candidate slots, and the ending selects among them; a long-vowel-plus-nun ending marks dual, masculine plural or second feminine singular
fields.tutor_destination: drills should pair slot production with a governing environment, and must separately train the syncretic prefix case

fields.advanced_explanation: the governor must stand in the verb's immediate left context with no competing governor between; the verb must be prefix-conjugated; for unwritten government the licensing host must itself be one of the listed items
fields.beginner_explanation: Introduces the closed inventory of particles that pull the imperfect out of its unmarked mood into the subjunctive, pairing each with the semantic contribution that motivates choosing it. Ends by opening the possibility that the licensing particle is not written at all, so that government can be asserted where no governor token is present.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: keeping the unmarked final vowel after the future-denying particle; substituting the jussive exponent after a subjunctive particle, and generally conflating the two similar-looking negators
fields.contrast_or_transfer: لن against لم: different mood, different exponent, different time reference; the complementiser sense against the future-denying and purpose senses inside one inventory
fields.intermediate_explanation: inspect the token immediately preceding the verb; test that token against the closed subjunctive inventory; if no surface governor is found, test whether a listed host licenses an unwritten one before concluding indicative
fields.prerequisite_statement: the unmarked mood and its two exponents from the preceding lesson; the closed nun-bearing imperfect class; prefixed prepositions written fused to the following word
fields.recognition_cue: the token immediately left of the imperfect belongs to the subjunctive governor inventory; the final position shows a fatha where the unmarked mood would show a damma; an expected final nun is absent while the long vowel before it remains
fields.tutor_destination: supports drills whose accepted answer must name the governing particle, plus negative controls contrasting the two look-alike negators and items where the governor is unwritten
