fields.unresolved_notice: government by an unwritten أن versus government by the lam itself is a school dispute that the lesson presents without attribution

fields.advanced_explanation: the licensor must be identified before any mood is reported for a deletion-exponed form; the conditional reading requires both a condition verb and an answer verb; cluster resolution applies only where a following word begins with a connecting alif
fields.beginner_explanation: Consolidates the three moods into a single verb-class by mood matrix and extends the licensors of the third mood beyond negation to conditional structures. Makes explicit that for one inflectional class two moods are surface-identical, so the mood can only be recovered from the licensor.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: putting the subjunctive vowel where the silent ending belongs; keeping the weak final letter under the third mood
fields.contrast_or_transfer: the three moods set side by side with their licensors and exponents; identical surfaces under different licensors within the nun-bearing class
fields.intermediate_explanation: identify the verb class; identify the licensor and the mood it imposes; read the exponent expected for that class in that mood off the matrix
fields.prerequisite_statement: all three mood licensor inventories from the three preceding lessons; the exponent for each class in the first two moods; identification of weak final radicals
fields.recognition_cue: the ending is silent, or an expected nun is missing, or an expected weak letter is missing; a conditional particle or a conditional noun introduces a clause containing two verbs; a nun-less form of the nun-bearing class occurs with a licensor that must be inspected to fix the mood
fields.tutor_destination: supports discrimination drills built on the syncretic pair where the licensor is the only cue, and repair drills where a cluster-resolved kasra must not be relabelled as a different mood

fields.advanced_explanation: the fixed-on-damma types require the noun to be inherently definite by reference; the accusative types require a dependent element or non-specific reference; the intermediary must agree in gender with the addressed noun
fields.beginner_explanation: Introduces direct address as a governed construction and teaches a five-way classification of the addressed noun in which the classification determines whether the noun is fixed on a damma or carries accusative marking. Adds the intermediary construction required when the addressed noun carries the definite article.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: adding nunation to an addressed proper name; placing the definite article directly after the address particle
fields.contrast_or_transfer: specific indefinite (damma, no nunation) vs. non-specific indefinite (accusative with nunation); annexation head vs. resembling-annexation head, distinguished by the case of the second element
fields.intermediate_explanation: confirm the presence of an address particle; ask whether the addressed noun is a single-word proper name; if indefinite, ask whether a specific individual is being addressed
fields.prerequisite_statement: the three cases and their markers; definiteness and nunation; annexation structure
fields.recognition_cue: an address particle stands immediately before a noun; the noun carries a damma with no nunation, signalling one of the two fixed types; the noun carries accusative marking, signalling one of the three accusative types
fields.tutor_destination: strong — the five types form a clean classification drill, and the specific vs. non-specific contrast is a high-value discrimination item
fields.unresolved_notice: the analysis of the element following the intermediary as a modifier versus an appositive is a standing school dispute; the lesson asserts only that it is nominative

fields.advanced_explanation: the base structure must be a nominal sentence with an identifiable subject and predicate; case assignment applies only within the clause the abrogator heads; the mental-state family requires a verb that actually takes two objects rather than one
fields.beginner_explanation: Puts a single nominal sentence through every abrogator family in turn so the learner treats each family as a distinct case-assignment operator rather than as vocabulary, and adds the principle that nested abrogators each govern only their own clause.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: reversing the direction of the case change between the two particle families; carrying one family's rule over to a member of another family
fields.contrast_or_transfer: accusative on the predicate against accusative on the subject as the family diagnostic; one accusative against two accusatives
fields.intermediate_explanation: start from the base nominal sentence and label both components; insert the abrogator and re-derive the case of each component from the family signature; restate the resulting semantic value, since the choice of member encodes stance and not only case
fields.prerequisite_statement: nominal sentence structure with subject and predicate; nominative and accusative marking; attached pronoun inventory
fields.recognition_cue: identify the head element first, then read its family off a membership list; check which of the two components carries accusative marking to confirm the family; when two accusatives follow a mental-state verb, treat them as a former subject-predicate pair rather than as an object plus a modifier
fields.tutor_destination: high — the base-sentence-through-all-families format is directly drillable, and the nesting items give a natural hard tier
fields.unresolved_notice: family membership lists vary across grammatical schools, notably the treatment of certainty verbs against preponderance verbs inside the mental-state family, and the lesson presents one list without attribution

fields.advanced_explanation: the identification step must complete before any case expectation is asserted; each governor's signature applies only to the elements it itself governs; the sense-conditioned members remain gated by sense even inside the synthesis procedure
fields.beginner_explanation: A synthesis lesson that converts three separately learned governance regimes into one ordered identification task: recognize the governor, classify its family, then apply that family's case signature. It also introduces stacking, where several abrogators occupy one sentence and each governs its own pair.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: swapping the assignments of the verbal and particle families; treating the cognition verb's agent as one of the accusatives
fields.contrast_or_transfer: all three signatures presented as one table, which is the lesson's central artefact; the same nominal shown under a verbal governor and under a particle governor to isolate which word changes case
fields.intermediate_explanation: scan for a governor; classify it into one of three families; apply that family's signature to its two governed elements
fields.prerequisite_statement: all three families as taught in L2.M2.01 through L2.M2.05; case exponents and their names; the notion of a governor's scope
fields.recognition_cue: a governor drawn from one of the three consolidated rosters; the governor's word class — inflecting verb against invariant particle — as the first cut; the presence or absence of a separate nominative agent as the cut between the two verbal families
fields.tutor_destination: high — family identification over mixed sentence sets is the drill that actually tests whether the three regimes were learned as a system rather than as three memorized pairs

fields.advanced_explanation: continuative members require a preceding negator or an equivalent licenser to carry the persistence reading; the duration member requires its particle and a following consequent clause; the case signature of the core family carries over unchanged to both subclasses
fields.beginner_explanation: Extends the verbal abrogator family with two subclasses the previous lesson did not reach: continuative members that are licensed only under a preceding negator, and time-anchored members that situate the state within a part of the day. It also widens the inventory of things that may occupy the predicate slot.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: using a continuative member without its licensing negator; confusing the perfective of the night-anchored member with a segmentally similar common noun
fields.contrast_or_transfer: cessation verb bare against cessation verb licensed by negation, which reverses the truth conditions; the negating use of the particle against its subordinating use with the duration member
fields.intermediate_explanation: check whether the candidate governor is a continuative member and, if so, whether a licenser precedes it; read the negator and the cessation verb as a single continuative governor rather than as negation of the sentence; distinguish the negating particle from the homographic subordinating particle by which member follows it
fields.prerequisite_statement: the core family and its case signature; negation particles and their scope; hollow and geminate verb inflection
fields.recognition_cue: a negator immediately followed by a cessation verb, forming one governing unit over a nominal predication; the same governing behaviour as the core family — one nominative element, one accusative element — but with a two-token governor; a time-anchored member whose predicate names a state rather than an event
fields.tutor_destination: high — the licensed/unlicensed minimal pair is an unusually sharp drill because the error inverts the meaning rather than merely damaging the case

fields.advanced_explanation: stated for nominal bases, chiefly place names, people names and abstract nouns; agreement rules presuppose an overt head noun; the permanent-attribute reading is stated in contrast to a locational prepositional phrase
fields.beginner_explanation: Introduces the relational adjective formed by a suffix rather than by an internal template, giving learners a productive way to say that something belongs to or derives from a named entity. It covers base adjustments before suffixation, the feminine and plural agreement forms, and the main semantic domains the derivation serves.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: retaining the base's final feminine marker before attaching the suffix; using the masculine suffix with a feminine head or the feminine form with a masculine head
fields.contrast_or_transfer: masculine suffix against feminine suffix plus marker; relational adjective against a prepositional phrase for the same referent, permanent attribute against current location
fields.intermediate_explanation: take the base noun in its singular form; delete a final feminine marker if present; convert or drop a final long vowel according to the base's shape
fields.prerequisite_statement: adjective agreement in gender, number, case and definiteness; the feminine marker and its behaviour; sound masculine and sound feminine plural tails
fields.recognition_cue: a nominal ending in a geminated yaa preceded by kasra, where the yaa is not part of the root; the stem before the suffix is recoverable as an independent noun, often a place or people name; the feminine counterpart shows the feminine marker stacked after the suffix
fields.tutor_destination: high — base-to-output derivation and gender agreement are deterministic, though items must be chosen so the base adjustment is actually exercised

fields.advanced_explanation: the verb must be prefix-conjugated for the mood dimension to apply at all; the final position must be visibly marked for the exponent to be read; the immediately preceding token must be inspected, not assumed absent
fields.beginner_explanation: Establishes that among Arabic verbs only the prefix-conjugated form carries a variable mood ending, and fixes the indicative as its unmarked state, defined negatively as what survives when no licensed governor stands in front of it. Introduces the two indicative exponents so that a raised ending is read as evidence about the left context rather than as a default guess.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: treating the short final vowel as the universal indicative marker; leaving the indicative vowel in place after a subjunctive governor
fields.contrast_or_transfer: vowel exponent versus retained-letter exponent inside one and the same mood; particles that precede an imperfect and govern it versus particles that precede and do not
fields.intermediate_explanation: scan the left context for a governor before assigning any mood label; classify the verb as vowel-exponed or nun-exponed so the right exponent is looked for; read the exponent from the visible pointing rather than inferring it from the verb's position
fields.prerequisite_statement: imperfect prefix conjugation with person, number and gender marking; the idea that a word ending can vary with syntactic environment; noun-initial sentence structure with a topic and a comment
fields.recognition_cue: the verb is prefix-conjugated and its final position carries a visible short vowel; a dual, masculine-plural or second-person-feminine-singular imperfect ends in a long vowel followed by nun; the token immediately to the left, if any, belongs to the non-governing class rather than to a mood-governing inventory
fields.tutor_destination: supports drills that require the exponent and the reason in the same answer, plus negative-control items where a non-governing pre-verbal marker tempts a wrong mood change
fields.unresolved_notice: the fixedness of the command form is asserted without noting the rival analysis that inflects it as a jussive

fields.advanced_explanation: polarity applies only to the numerals three to ten; the counted noun must be plural and never singular or dual with three to ten; the construct requires the numeral to be bare of article and tanwin
fields.beginner_explanation: Fixes the behaviour of the cardinal numerals from one to ten: ordinary agreement for the first two, inverse gender agreement for three to ten, a construct whose second term is a genitive plural, and the anomalous behaviour of eight with feminine counted nouns.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: Applying ordinary gender agreement to the numerals three to ten.; Using a singular or dual counted noun with three to ten.
fields.contrast_or_transfer: one and two against three to ten in both agreement and position; masculine against feminine counted nouns for the same numeral
fields.intermediate_explanation: identify the singular of the counted noun and determine its gender; select the numeral form of the opposite gender for three to ten, or the agreeing form for one and two; put the counted noun in the plural and mark it genitive
fields.prerequisite_statement: noun gender; sound and broken plural formation; the construct and genitive marking
fields.recognition_cue: a bare numeral immediately followed by a bare plural in the genitive, indicating the construct numeral phrase; presence or absence of the feminine ending on the numeral relative to the gender of the counted singular, confirming polarity; a numeral standing after its noun and agreeing with it, indicating one or two
fields.tutor_destination: very high + the polarity rule is mechanically generable and its dominant failure mode, ordinary agreement, supplies an ideal distractor for every item

fields.advanced_explanation: the verb must be imperfect; the subject must be dual, masculine plural, or a second-person feminine singular addressee; a governing particle must be present for deletion to apply
fields.beginner_explanation: Isolates the five suffixed imperfect conjugations whose indicative is marked by a final nun and teaches that deletion of that nun is the mood exponent for both the subjunctive and the jussive in those forms. Sets the boundary of the class by excluding the feminine plural, whose ending is superficially similar.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: counting the feminine-plural conjugations as members of the five-member set; retaining the nun after a subjunctive or jussive particle
fields.contrast_or_transfer: indicative with nun vs. subjunctive and jussive without it; the indicative nun vs. the feminine-plural nun, which is not a mood exponent
fields.intermediate_explanation: determine the person, number and gender of the subject; decide whether the conjugation belongs to the five-member set; check for a preceding governing particle and identify the mood it assigns
fields.prerequisite_statement: imperfect conjugation across person, number and gender; dual and plural formation; the three moods and their unsuffixed exponents
fields.recognition_cue: the imperfect verb ends in one of the three nun-bearing suffixes; in reduced form the suffix appears without its nun; a masculine-plural reduced form is followed by a silent alif
fields.tutor_destination: very strong — conversion drills, membership sorting, and the feminine-plural exclusion are all clean discriminating items

fields.advanced_explanation: the word is a noun or adjective; the word does not carry the definite article; the three final graphemes that block the supporting alif
fields.beginner_explanation: Introduces nunation: the three doubled-vowel endings that add a nasal to a noun, the writing rule that the a-form normally needs a silent supporting alif, the three graphemic environments that exempt it, and the claim that nunation marks a noun as indefinite and cannot co-occur with the definite article.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: writing the a-form of nunation without its supporting alif on a word that requires one; pronouncing the supporting alif as a vowel
fields.contrast_or_transfer: a nunated form against the same noun with the definite article; nunation against gemination, which look superficially similar as descriptions but do different work
fields.intermediate_explanation: identify the doubled mark, read its base vowel, then append the nasal; when writing the a-form, add the supporting alif unless the word ends in one of the three exempt graphemes; never write nunation together with the definite article on the same word
fields.prerequisite_statement: the three short-vowel marks; the tied taa and the variant final a-spelling as graphemes; the definite article as a written prefix
fields.recognition_cue: a doubled vowel mark on the final letter of a nominal; a final alif carrying a doubled a-mark, where the alif is not pronounced; a doubled mark placed directly on the tied taa with no added alif
fields.tutor_destination: high - ending substitution over a fixed stem and the support-spelling decision are both closed-set

fields.advanced_explanation: the register claims are stated for classical usage; the emphasis suffix is described for imperfect verbs; binding force is attributed only to oaths on the divine name
fields.beginner_explanation: Presents the sworn-statement construction as a three-slot frame and fixes which prefixed particle may head it, what case it imposes on the element sworn by, and which emphatic or negative markers the sworn content must carry.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: omitting the emphasis suffix from affirmative sworn content about the future; attaching the emphasis suffix to negative sworn content
fields.contrast_or_transfer: oath particle versus coordinator of the same shape; affirmative versus negative sworn content
fields.intermediate_explanation: locate the particle and confirm genitive marking on the element sworn by; classify the sworn content as affirmative or negative; for affirmative content select the emphatic pattern by tense or clause type
fields.prerequisite_statement: genitive government by prepositions; imperfect verb inflection; past and future negation particles
fields.recognition_cue: a single prefixed consonant immediately before a genitive divine name; a following clause carrying an emphatic prefix, an emphasis suffix, an aspectual particle, or a negator; absence of any preceding element that the prefixed consonant could coordinate with
fields.tutor_destination: supports production drills that give polarity and tense and require the correct sworn-content shape, and discrimination drills separating the oath particle from the coordinator

fields.advanced_explanation: the letter is not a member of the non-attaching set; the letter to its right is itself capable of attaching leftward; the six non-attaching letters have no initial and no medial variant
fields.beginner_explanation: Teaches that letters are realized by position-conditioned variants inside a word and that a closed set of letters refuses attachment on its left, so that an orthographic word can break into several connected runs. The learner is trained to identify a letter across its variants and to predict where a word will visually split.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: attaching a member of the non-attaching set to the letter that follows it; reading medial bumps of different letters as the same letter
fields.contrast_or_transfer: a word built only from attaching letters, forming one run, against a word containing non-attaching letters, forming several; the standalone against the final variant of the same letter, which differ only by an incoming stroke
fields.intermediate_explanation: mark every member of the non-attaching set in the letter string, then cut the word immediately after each of them to obtain the connected runs; assign each letter its variant by position: nothing before it makes it initial, attachment on both sides makes it medial, nothing after it makes it final, neither makes it standalone; when reading, hold the dot signature constant and let the connecting strokes vary
fields.prerequisite_statement: the grapheme inventory and dot signatures from the preceding lesson; the shape-family grouping
fields.recognition_cue: read a gap inside a word as the trace of a non-attaching letter rather than as a word boundary; identify a variant by which of its sides bears a connecting stroke; use dot signature to resolve medial bumps that share one skeleton
fields.tutor_destination: high - variant identification and run counting are mechanical, closed-set, and auto-gradable

fields.advanced_explanation: class membership is lexically listed and is not derivable from root or template; for the summons word the inflectional treatment follows from the dialectal register adopted; for the exception words the verbal reading requires the accusative and the prepositional reading the genitive
fields.beginner_explanation: Presents the class of verbs whose paradigm is lexically incomplete - locked to one stem, to one person, or to the imperative alone - and works through the individual members, each showing a differently shaped gap. Motivates the gaps by the specialised, non-eventive meanings the members carry and closes with a matrix keyed by which cells are missing.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: generating an imperfect stem for the negative copula; reading the verb of expectation as a past-time report on the model of the ordinary copula
fields.contrast_or_transfer: complete versus defective paradigm; past stem versus past-time reference
fields.intermediate_explanation: identify the lexeme rather than the template, since the gap belongs to the lexeme; consult the per-lexeme list of available cells before attempting any conjugation; for the negative copula, inflect within the past stem for person and number and read time reference from context rather than from the stem
fields.prerequisite_statement: past, imperfect, and imperative stems; person, number, and gender inflection on verbs; the copular family and its case effects
fields.recognition_cue: a verb that never surfaces on an imperfect stem in any attested text; a past-stem form carrying present or future reference; an invariable exclamatory predicate followed by a definite general noun and then a specific nominal
fields.tutor_destination: high - negative drills naming the form that does not exist, and per-lexeme cell-availability drills; a conjugation drill must never request a blocked cell
fields.unresolved_notice: the word class of the praise and blame pair is classically disputed and the lesson asserts one side without attribution

fields.advanced_explanation: the ellipsis classification requires that the omitted element be uniquely recoverable from context; the parenthetical classification requires that removal leave the clause grammatical; register claims hold only relative to the speaker's role and the occasion
fields.beginner_explanation: Introduces the length axis of expression: saying less than expected, saying more than expected, and the neutral midpoint, each with named subtypes. The syntactically load-bearing parts are the ellipsis type of brevity and the parenthetical-insert type of amplification.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: treating brevity as always the better choice; conflating synonym-piling with exact repetition
fields.contrast_or_transfer: brevity versus parity versus amplification; brevity without omission versus brevity through ellipsis
fields.intermediate_explanation: for a short clause, first test for a recoverable omitted element, then classify it as the elliptical or the complete brevity type; for an amplified clause, locate the added span, determine its relation to the base, and name the technique; apply the removability test before treating a mid-clause span as a predicate
fields.prerequisite_statement: genitive construct relations and head-dependent structure; nominal sentence with subject and predicate; coordination
fields.recognition_cue: for the ellipsis type: ask whether a constituent must be supplied for the clause to mean what it evidently means; for the deleted-head pattern: a dependent whose semantics do not fit the overt head signals a missing head; for a parenthetical insert: test whether deleting the span leaves a well-formed clause, and check for invocation content set off by dashes or commas
fields.tutor_destination: medium — technique naming is drillable, but the two brevity subtypes require a completeness judgement that beginners will not make reliably

fields.advanced_explanation: only a verb with an available object yields a promoted deputy subject; the text must be vocalized or otherwise disambiguated, since the consonantal skeleton of the two voices is identical for sound stems; the promoted noun must actually carry nominative marking for the transformation to be complete
fields.beginner_explanation: Trains the learner to convert an agent-naming clause into an agentless one by revocalizing the verb stem and promoting the direct object into a nominative deputy-subject slot, and to recognize why procedural and technical prose prefers the agentless form.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: leaving the promoted noun in the accusative it carried as an object; using vowel combinations other than the perfect passive template
fields.contrast_or_transfer: active vocalization against passive vocalization on the same skeleton; deputy subject against ordinary subject, identical in case but different in derivation
fields.intermediate_explanation: locate the agent phrase and delete it; revocalize the verb stem for the tense at hand; recase the former direct object from accusative to nominative
fields.prerequisite_statement: transitivity and object marking; nominative and accusative marking; perfect and imperfect stem shapes
fields.recognition_cue: an u-vowel on the first stem consonant paired with an i-vowel before the final consonant in a perfect verb; an u-vowel on the inflectional prefix paired with an a-vowel before the final consonant in an imperfect verb; a nominative noun immediately following a lexically transitive verb with no agent named anywhere in the clause
fields.tutor_destination: high — transformation is mechanical for sound stems, but weak and geminate stems need separate drill buckets or the drill teaches a false rule

fields.advanced_explanation: the pause classification depends on a prior syntactic and semantic parse, so it cannot be assigned from the surface string alone; the accusative indefinite exception depends on the ending being orthographically supported; the supporting pausal consonant is presented as restricted in current practice to positions where the text marks it
fields.beginner_explanation: Treats pausing and continuous delivery as grammatical rather than merely decorative: it sets out what happens to inflectional endings at a pause, classifies pause sites by how much meaning is complete at them, and shows that pause placement can shift constituent boundaries and reverse a reading.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: pausing on an element that governs or depends on what has not yet been uttered, such as a preposition or the first member of an annexation; treating a breath pause as though it were a complete pause
fields.contrast_or_transfer: continuous delivery versus pausal delivery, and audible versus inaudible inflection; the four pause grades ordered from ideal to prohibited
fields.intermediate_explanation: before reciting, plan pause points at boundaries where the meaning is complete; when forced to pause mid-unit for breath, resume from the start of that unit rather than from the interrupted point; at a chosen pause, apply the ending changes: drop the short vowel, convert two of the indefinite endings to zero, keep the accusative as a long vowel, realise the feminine ending as its pausal consonant
fields.prerequisite_statement: the case and mood system and the ability to state what ending a word should carry; annexation and the indivisibility of its two members; recognition of prepositional and negation particles
fields.recognition_cue: a delivery is pausal when the final vowel is absent and the last consonant is quiescent; a pause site is complete when what follows begins an independent predication; a pause site is sufficient when the preceding meaning is finished but what follows elaborates on it
fields.tutor_destination: high for the mechanical half: ending changes and marker meanings are deterministic. Lower for pause grading, which requires a prior parse and a judgement about semantic completeness and should be presented with the analysis attached rather than as a single scored key
fields.unresolved_notice: the four-way pause grading is analysis-dependent: the boundary between the complete and the sufficient grade turns on whether what follows is judged connected, and readers who parse differently will grade differently

fields.advanced_explanation: scope is limited to roots with no weak letter; the sukun alternation is conditioned by the consonant-initial shape of the ending, not by meaning; dual endings apply only when the referent is exactly two
fields.beginner_explanation: Builds the full person/number/gender ending paradigm of the perfect (الماضي) for strong triliteral verbs and explains the stem alternation that appears before consonant-initial endings. It also fixes the third-person masculine singular as the citation shape a learner looks up.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: treating the first-person singular and second-person masculine singular perfect as interchangeable; applying a dual ending to a subject of three or more
fields.contrast_or_transfer: third-person slots versus first/second-person slots with respect to the vowel on the second radical; dual versus plural reference
fields.intermediate_explanation: take the citation shape of a strong verb; strip to the stem used for endings; choose the person/number/gender slot
fields.prerequisite_statement: Arabic script and short-vowel marks including sukun; triliteral root concept; independent personal pronoun inventory including dual
fields.recognition_cue: a consonant-initial ending beginning with ت or ن signals a first- or second-person form and co-occurs with a vowelless second radical; a vowelled second radical with a light vowel-initial or ت-initial third-person marker signals a third-person form; long-alif endings mark dual, waw-alif marks masculine plural, a nun ending marks feminine plural
fields.tutor_destination: strong slot-to-form and form-to-slot drilling, including the unvocalised-ambiguity case that needs contextual resolution
fields.unresolved_notice: analysis-dependent: the traditional account treats the attached ending itself as the فاعل, which is not the same claim as an optional-pronoun/pro-drop account

fields.advanced_explanation: the directive reading requires an authority differential or facts that carry their own authority; the commitment reading requires the absence of possibility-hedging particles; the supplication reading requires the invocation lexeme set and the absence of past-time anchoring
fields.beginner_explanation: Isolates the case where a grammatically assertive clause performs an act, and gives it named subtypes with recognition cues. The pedagogically load-bearing case is perfective-form invocation, where the tense form must not be read as past reference.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: treating every assertive as a pure report; reading a perfective invocation formula as a statement about the past
fields.contrast_or_transfer: assertive form with enacting function versus overtly enacting form; perfective-as-supplication versus perfective-as-report
fields.intermediate_explanation: state the grammatical form, then state the function, then state the speaker's intent as a separate line; run the indicator checklist for each of the four subtypes before defaulting to plain report; for a perfective clause, test for a past-time adverbial before assigning the supplication reading
fields.prerequisite_statement: perfective and imperfective verb morphology; nominal sentence with predicate nominal; L5.M1.01 assertive/enacting partition
fields.recognition_cue: for supplication: perfective verb from the invocation lexeme set, divine name as subject, no past-time adverbial, and a context of illness, death or blessing; for commitment: first-person subject, future or ongoing aspect, absence of hedging particles; for directive: statement of an obstacle or condition, speaker with standing, addressee action as the expected uptake
fields.tutor_destination: high for the invocation subtype, where the cue set is concrete; low for the directive and status subtypes, which need a supplied situation

fields.advanced_explanation: the base must itself be a plural, otherwise the analysis is simply a first plural; the item must be lexically attested with a second layer; the collection or category reading must be contextually supported for the analysis to hold
fields.beginner_explanation: Introduces second-order pluralisation, where an existing broken plural is itself pluralised, and insists that the second layer is not a quantity increase but a shift to groupings, categories, or kinds. Locates the phenomenon in catalogue-like technical, administrative, and elevated literary writing and warns that it cannot be generated at will.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: reading a second-layer plural as an intensified quantity; generating a second-layer plural from any available broken plural
fields.contrast_or_transfer: first plural versus second-layer plural of the same singular; quantity reading versus grouping reading
fields.intermediate_explanation: identify the singular and its ordinary broken plural; test whether the observed form takes that plural, not the singular, as its base; decide which second-layer strategy is present: feminine suffixation or template replacement
fields.prerequisite_statement: broken plural templates; sound feminine plural suffixation; nunation and defective-noun inflection
fields.recognition_cue: a sound feminine plural ending sitting on a stem that is itself a recognisable broken plural; a broken-plural shape whose base is not the singular but an intermediate plural; a reading of groupings or kinds where a plain plural would already be sufficient
fields.tutor_destination: moderate: recognition drills are safe, production drills must be closed-list because the process is not productive

fields.advanced_explanation: metrical verse only; a genuine metrical or rhyme pressure at that position; the departure must map onto one of the recognised types
fields.beginner_explanation: Introduces the register-bounded notion of licensed deviation in metrical verse and surveys a six-item taxonomy of such deviations, so that a reader parsing verse tests for a sanctioned licence before declaring a form ungrammatical.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: Using a licensed verse form in prose and defending it as licence.; Reversing the direction of the lengthen/shorten pair.
fields.contrast_or_transfer: verse permission vs prose prohibition; each inverse pair set against itself: lengthen vs shorten, grant vs withhold nunation, vowel vs de-vowel
fields.intermediate_explanation: establish register first: verse or prose; scan the position and determine the syllable count and final vowel the meter and rhyme demand; retrieve the form the lexicon predicts for prose and compare it with the attested form
fields.prerequisite_statement: nunation and the three-case system; the blocked vs fully declinable noun distinction; final long-vowel noun classes
fields.recognition_cue: the text is established as metrical verse before any rule is applied; a word-final shape at a line-final or hemistich-final position departs from the lexicon default; nunation appears on a noun whose class blocks it, or is absent from one whose class requires it
fields.tutor_destination: high for a register-gate drill and for direction-of-pair discrimination; low for the attestation examples, which are too hedged to drill on
fields.unresolved_notice: the rhyme-word kasra in the flagship ode admits rival accounts including ordinary rhyme-vowel treatment

fields.advanced_explanation: the word is taken as a full word rather than a fragment; the test is applied to a vowelled written form; borderline items disputed among grammarians, such as verb-like nouns and certain negators, are not raised
fields.beginner_explanation: Establishes that every word falls into exactly one of three classes, defines each class by its own criterion (naming without time, action anchored in time, meaning only in combination), and maps the eight-way English scheme onto that three-way division.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: concluding that a word is not of the naming class because it rejects the article and nunation; classifying a demonstrative outside the naming class because it takes neither the article nor nunation
fields.contrast_or_transfer: naming class versus action class, discriminated by inherent time reference; residual class versus the other two, discriminated by inability to stand alone
fields.intermediate_explanation: for each word in a clause, test for the naming markers, then for conjugation and time, then assign the remainder to the residual class; state the reason for the assignment alongside the label; run the five markers in order and stop at the first that the word accepts
fields.prerequisite_statement: L1.M2.02 threshold for a complete utterance; L1.M2.01 awareness that endings vary; L1.M2.04 three-way class division
fields.recognition_cue: the word accepts the definite article or nunation, which points to the naming class; the word conjugates for person, number and gender and takes the imperfect prefixes, which points to the action class; the word cannot stand alone as an answer and shows neither of the above, which points to the residual class
fields.tutor_destination: strong basis for a label-plus-reason drill over each word of a short clause, with credit withheld when the reason is wrong even if the label is right
fields.unresolved_notice: the no-exceptions claim about exhaustiveness is stated without the disputed borderline items grammarians debate

fields.advanced_explanation: the subject must belong to the admissible inventory; the specified element must be nominative; omission of the specified element requires a recoverable referent
fields.beginner_explanation: Introduces the frozen praise and blame constructions as a three-slot pattern with a restricted subject inventory, and records that the final slot has two competing classical analyses that nevertheless converge on one case outcome.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: placing a bare indefinite in the subject slot without the article; marking the specified element accusative
fields.contrast_or_transfer: praise polarity against blame polarity; frozen items against ordinary inflecting verbs
fields.intermediate_explanation: identify the frozen item and its polarity; identify the subject slot and check it against the admissible inventory; identify the specified element and mark it nominative
fields.prerequisite_statement: nominal sentence structure with subject and predicate; the notion of a frozen verb; definiteness marking
fields.recognition_cue: a clause-initial frozen item of the praise or blame set with no inflectional variation available; a following definite noun naming a category rather than an individual; a nominative noun in final position specifying the individual
fields.tutor_destination: high — the subject inventory converts directly into an admissible against inadmissible sort, and the rival analyses give a good discussion item, but the accusative-indefinite case must be presented consistently or the drill teaches a contradiction
fields.unresolved_notice: whether these items are verbs or nouns is a long-standing dispute between the grammatical schools and the lesson asserts the verb analysis without attribution

fields.advanced_explanation: applies where the comment is a bare word rather than a phrase or clause; the non-human-plural rule applies to plural topics whose referents are not human; agreement exponents assume a fully declinable adjective
fields.beginner_explanation: Narrows the comment slot to its single-word realisation, splits that realisation into a describing type and a classifying type, and sharpens agreement by adding the non-human-plural rule. Defines the single-word comment partly negatively, against clause and phrase comments.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: giving a non-human plural topic a plural comment; leaving a feminine topic with a masculine comment
fields.contrast_or_transfer: describing comment versus classifying comment; single-word comment versus clause comment versus phrase comment
fields.intermediate_explanation: read the topic's gender, number, and humanness; select an adjective if a quality is asserted or a noun if a class membership is asserted; apply feminine singular agreement when the topic is a non-human plural, otherwise match gender and number directly
fields.prerequisite_statement: the two slots of the noun-initial sentence and their nominative case; gender and number exponents on adjectives; the notion of humanness as a lexical property of a referent
fields.recognition_cue: the comment consists of exactly one word; that word is a noun or an adjective, never a verb or a particle; it lacks the definite article in the unmarked case
fields.tutor_destination: high — the non-human-plural override is a clean discriminator with a well-defined error to elicit, and agreement drills are mechanically checkable
fields.unresolved_notice: whether the governed phrase fills the comment slot or attaches to an unexpressed comment is a standing analytic dispute; the lesson asserts one side without attribution and the dispute must be preserved rather than resolved

fields.advanced_explanation: stated for present-time affirmative assertions; topic element identifiable to the hearer; comment element carries new information
fields.beginner_explanation: Introduces predication itself (إسناد) as the relation that converts isolated words into an assertion, and establishes that Arabic forms present-time equative statements by adjacency alone, with no linking verb. Names the two predication roles before the learner is asked to manipulate the slot labels technically.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: scanning the string for a word corresponding to the English copula and treating the sentence as incomplete when none is found; reading a definite nominal followed by a definite adjective as an assertion
fields.contrast_or_transfer: assertion versus attributive noun phrase, distinguished only by the definiteness of the second element; English overt copula versus Arabic structural linking
fields.intermediate_explanation: locate the element being talked about; locate the element that states something about it; test whether the second element merely modifies the first by comparing definiteness
fields.prerequisite_statement: the definite article and nunation as definiteness exponents; the noun versus adjective distinction; gender agreement on adjectives
fields.recognition_cue: two adjacent nominals with no verb and no abrogating particle between them; the first element carries a definiteness exponent that the second lacks; the second element supplies information not already presupposed of the first
fields.tutor_destination: supports drills that require deciding whether an adjacent nominal pair is an assertion or a phrase, and that require supplying the English copula without inventing an Arabic one
fields.unresolved_notice: the lesson does not say what assigns nominative to the two slots; standard grammars dispute this and the dispute must remain attributed rather than resolved; whether copula-free predication is best modelled as a zero copula or as the absence of any copular element is analysis-dependent and untouched here

fields.advanced_explanation: the material sense requires a substance-denoting complement under an artefact-denoting head; the partitive sense requires a mass or plural complement conceived as divisible; the oath sense requires an oath predicate, expressed or understood
fields.beginner_explanation: Moves the learner past one-preposition-one-gloss thinking by presenting each common genitive-assigning preposition as a set of distinguishable semantic functions, and by supplying paraphrase tests that pick one function in a given context. Case government is held constant while the semantics vary.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: Reading a substance-denoting complement as a place of origin.; Rendering the instrumental proclitic with one fixed English preposition in every occurrence.
fields.contrast_or_transfer: origin against material for the same preposition; partitive against explicative for the same preposition
fields.intermediate_explanation: locate the preposition and delimit its complement; classify the complement semantically as place, substance, mass, tool, animate participant, event, or verbal noun; apply the paraphrase test attached to each candidate sense
fields.prerequisite_statement: prepositions assign genitive; kasra and tanwin kasra as genitive exponents; attached versus independent prepositions
fields.recognition_cue: the complement names a place or a starting bound and the predicate expresses motion, indicating the origin sense; a made-of paraphrase preserves the meaning, indicating the material sense; inserting a quantity expression such as part of preserves the meaning, indicating the partitive sense
fields.tutor_destination: high + sense selection with type-matched distractors is directly drillable and the rejected senses supply natural distractors

fields.advanced_explanation: weight assignment depends on the final element of the syllable, not on its onset; normalisation must precede syllabification, otherwise weights are computed over letters that are not spoken; rhyme-position lengthening applies only at the hemistich end
fields.beginner_explanation: Supplies the phonological input layer that metrical analysis presupposes: the two syllable weights and their shapes, the voweled/quiescent consonant distinction that generates them, the rewrite rules converting orthography into a pronounced representation, and a repeated end-to-end application of the four-step scansion method.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: assigning weights from the written form rather than the pronounced form; confusing an open syllable with a closed one
fields.contrast_or_transfer: light versus heavy syllable; voweled versus quiescent consonant
fields.intermediate_explanation: convert the written verse to a pronounced representation using the rewrite rules; walk the pronounced representation consonant by consonant, deciding each syllable's weight from what follows; emit the weight string
fields.prerequisite_statement: the foot and meter vocabulary from the previous lesson; fully vocalised reading including case and mood endings; the assimilation behaviour of the definite article
fields.recognition_cue: a syllable is light if it ends in its short vowel and heavy if it ends in a consonant or a long vowel; a consonant is quiescent when no vowel follows it and voweled when one does; a spelling requires normalisation whenever a written letter is not pronounced or a pronounced sound is not written
fields.tutor_destination: high for the weight-classification and rewrite-rule items, which are deterministic and gradable; low for the full scansion walkthroughs, whose printed segmentations are not reproducible in every case

fields.advanced_explanation: the particle must be adjacent to its verb; the following token must be a verb; the frequency reading requires a generic statement
fields.beginner_explanation: Teaches a verbal particle whose reading is selected locally by the tense class of the verb immediately following it, with a secondary reading noted on each side and an explicit statement that the particle governs nothing.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: Translating the particle the same way regardless of the tense of its verb.; Treating the plain particle and its emphatic variant as one item.
fields.contrast_or_transfer: perfect complement against imperfect complement with the same verb; certainty against possibility
fields.intermediate_explanation: locate the particle; determine the tense class of the token immediately following; assign the primary reading from the tense class
fields.prerequisite_statement: perfect and imperfect verb morphology; the passive perfect; the indicative mood
fields.recognition_cue: a perfect verb immediately after the particle, indicating certainty and completion; an imperfect verb immediately after the particle, indicating possibility; a generic statement about a type of person or a habitual truth, indicating the frequency reading
fields.tutor_destination: high + minimal pairs differing only in the tense of the verb after the particle make near-ideal drill items

fields.advanced_explanation: both complements are accusative only when the verb is used in its mental-state sense; the second complement must predicate of the first; otherwise the structure is not this one; the agent slot is filled independently of the two complements
fields.beginner_explanation: Introduces the third abrogator type: cognition verbs that absorb a whole predication as two accusative complements while retaining their own nominative agent. The lesson's distinctive work is the subdivision of the roster by epistemic strength and the recognition that two of its members govern this way only under one of their senses.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: marking only the first complement accusative and leaving the second nominative; applying the particle family's split assignment to these verbs
fields.contrast_or_transfer: this family against the particle family, where only one element is accusative; this family against the verbal family, where the accusative sits on the predicate alone
fields.intermediate_explanation: identify the verb as a member of this roster; locate the agent and confirm it is nominative and distinct from both complements; assign the first complement to the embedded subject and the second to the embedded predicate
fields.prerequisite_statement: the two earlier abrogator families and their signatures; direct object marking and verbal transitivity; enclitic object pronouns
fields.recognition_cue: a cognition verb followed by two accusative-marked elements neither of which is a circumstantial or adverbial accusative; a separate nominative agent, which is the surface cue that separates this family from the other two; for the sense-conditioned members, a second accusative that predicates something of the first rather than merely naming a further participant
fields.tutor_destination: high — the literal versus judgemental minimal pair for the two sense-conditioned members is a genuinely discriminating drill, unlike a pure case drill

fields.advanced_explanation: the templates apply once the stem is confirmed to have four radicals; the reflexive template requires a corresponding base verb for its transitivity contrast to be meaningful; the participle vowel distinction only carries the active versus passive contrast in the base template
fields.beginner_explanation: Introduces the four-radical verb class, its base and reflexive templates, and their full conjugation, verbal nouns and participles, so that a four-consonant stem is analysed as its own class rather than forced into a triliteral derived form. A secondary aim is stylistic: the class's phonetic weight and its sound-imitating members are presented as a resource for expressive prose.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: Giving the reflexive template's low prefix vowel to the base template's imperfect.; Analysing a four-consonant stem as the triliteral doubling form.
fields.contrast_or_transfer: four-radical base template versus the triliteral doubling form, which also shows a geminate-looking middle but doubles the second radical of a three-consonant root; base versus reflexive four-radical templates in transitivity and in vowel pattern
fields.intermediate_explanation: count the stem consonants after removing any inflectional prefix; decide between the base and the reflexive template by the presence of the initial t; assign the prefix vowel and the pre-final vowel from the chosen template
fields.prerequisite_statement: triliteral conjugation in past and imperfect; the template notation; verbal-noun and participle formation for the derived forms
fields.recognition_cue: a verb stem with four consonants and no recognisable triliteral derived-form augment; a rounded prefix vowel in the imperfect, which the base triliteral form never shows; an initial t before a four-consonant stem, marking the reflexive template
fields.tutor_destination: high — conjugation is fully regular and mechanically gradable, and the base versus reflexive vowel contrast is a clean discriminator; the sound-imitation material is appreciation rather than drill
fields.unresolved_notice: school-dependent: four independent radicals versus reduplication of a two-consonant base for reduplicated stems

fields.advanced_explanation: attributive or predicative adjective position; agreement in gender, number, definiteness and case with the described noun; the restricted-inflection behaviour holds in the indefinite, non-annexed state, a qualification the lesson does not state
fields.beginner_explanation: Introduces the adjective of stable quality as a derivational class distinct from the agent noun, inventories its principal templates, and attaches the morphosyntactic consequences that follow from template membership, notably feminine formation and restricted inflection.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: using the agent-noun template where a stable-quality template is required; adding tanwin to the two restricted templates
fields.contrast_or_transfer: agent noun versus quality adjective on the same root; state-now versus disposition, mapped onto two of the templates
fields.intermediate_explanation: isolate the root; decide whether the intended property is stable or episodic; select the template appropriate to the semantic domain
fields.prerequisite_statement: the bare-triliteral agent-noun template; adjective agreement and the case system; the notion of a root and a template
fields.recognition_cue: the word ascribes a lasting property rather than reporting an event; the shape matches one of the listed templates; absence of tanwin, with the genitive taking fatha, marks the two restricted templates
fields.tutor_destination: strong: masculine-to-feminine drills per template, and class-assignment drills that force a semantic decision rather than a shape match

fields.advanced_explanation: human and rational reference for the inherent-quality class; geminate or weak final radical for the prefixed class; affliction or temporary condition semantics for the shortened-alif class
fields.beginner_explanation: Adds four low-frequency broken-plural templates to the learner's inventory and, more importantly, teaches that the choice among them is licensed by properties of the singular: its template, whether its final radical is geminate or weak, whether its referent is human, and whether the quality it names is inherent or an afflicted condition. Ties the survival of these plurals to technical, legal, devotional, and belletristic registers.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: extending the human-quality plural template to a non-human noun; omitting the prefixed hamza in the geminate or weak-final class
fields.contrast_or_transfer: inherent quality versus afflicted state as the divider between two templates of similar length; geminate final radical versus sound final radical inside the same prefixed class
fields.intermediate_explanation: check whether the singular referent is human and rational; check the singular template and whether it names an inherent quality; inspect the final radical for gemination or weakness
fields.prerequisite_statement: broken versus sound plurals; the فَعيل adjectival template; geminate and weak radical classes
fields.recognition_cue: a plural ending in a long vowel plus hamza with damma-fatha vowelling on the stem, pointing to the human-quality class; the same long ending but with a prefixed hamza and kasra inside, pointing to the geminate or weak-final class; gemination inside a prefixed plural signalling an underlying doubled radical in the singular
fields.tutor_destination: strong for recognition drills; production drills must be restricted to attested items because the lesson itself denies full predictability

fields.advanced_explanation: the procedure presupposes knowledge of the case system, the pattern inventory, and the government of the common particles; it operates over a whole sentence, not over an isolated word; it presupposes that the text is grammatically well formed
fields.beginner_explanation: Assembles previously taught grammar into a reading procedure: recover the unwritten short vowels of unpointed text from syntactic position, word pattern, particle restrictions, and context, applied to the sentence as a whole rather than word by word.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: Vocalising each word before understanding the structure of the sentence.; Ignoring the category restriction imposed by a preceding particle.
fields.contrast_or_transfer: pointed against unpointed text; a word read in isolation against the same word read in a sentence
fields.intermediate_explanation: scan the sentence for particles, for the article, and for likely verbs; classify the sentence as verbal or nominal from its opening element; assign grammatical roles and the cases those roles entail
fields.prerequisite_statement: the three cases and their exponents; verbal and nominal sentence structure; the derived verb forms
fields.recognition_cue: presence of a category-restricting particle immediately before an ambiguous skeleton; presence of the definite article, marking the word as a noun or adjective and blocking tanwin; match between a candidate pattern and the skeleton's letter count and long-vowel positions
fields.tutor_destination: very high + unpointed-to-pointed conversion over graded sentences is directly drillable and self-checking

fields.advanced_explanation: the decision is made on the referent, not on the noun's morphological gender or plural type; the rule targets plurals; singulars and duals are unaffected; the dual, which keeps dedicated exponents
fields.beginner_explanation: Formalises the referent-rationality distinction as the controlling factor in plural concord and shows that a plural of non-rational referents drives feminine singular exponents across adjectives, verbs, resumptive pronouns and demonstratives, irrespective of how that plural was formed.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: giving a masculine plural adjective to a non-rational plural; giving a feminine plural adjective to a non-rational plural whose own form is a feminine plural
fields.contrast_or_transfer: rational plural concord against non-rational plural concord, target by target; feminine singular against feminine plural exponents, which the lesson treats as a live confusion
fields.intermediate_explanation: classify the referent as rational or non-rational before selecting any concord exponent; for non-rational plurals, select the feminine singular exponent on every concord target in the clause; for rational plurals, select plural exponents matched for gender
fields.prerequisite_statement: all three number values; both suffixal plurals and restructured plurals; adjective, verb, pronoun and demonstrative concord
fields.recognition_cue: a plural head noun with a feminine singular adjective is a strong cue that its referent is non-rational; a feminine singular verb exponent with a plural subject indicates the same; a feminine singular resumptive pronoun referring back to a plural antecedent
fields.tutor_destination: high + the rationality decision plus four target selections give a compact drill matrix, but generation drills must accept the alternate feminine plural agreement

fields.advanced_explanation: feature bundles identify a register only in aggregate; single features recur across registers; register judgements presuppose a known communicative situation; the spectrum ordering is a teaching device, not a metric
fields.beginner_explanation: Builds a taxonomy of Arabic registers and gives each one a bundle of observable linguistic features: sentence completeness, voice, connector type, rhythm, presence of rhymed prose, vocabulary weight, tone, and communicative goal. Closes on the principle that correctness is a function of situation rather than a property of a single prestige variety.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: using administrative phrasing in an everyday transactional exchange; using transactional fragments in a document that must be precise
fields.contrast_or_transfer: transactional fragments versus oratorical complete sentences; administrative agent suppression versus narrative agent-bearing past tense
fields.intermediate_explanation: inventory the observable features of a text: sentence completeness, voice, connectors, rhyme, tone; match the feature bundle against the register profiles; check the communicative goal implied by the situation
fields.prerequisite_statement: passive voice formation; verbal nouns and annexation chains; past-tense narration
fields.recognition_cue: clustering of agent-suppressed verbs with long annexation chains, pointing to the administrative variety; past-tense predicates chained by sequential connectors, pointing to the narrative variety; phrase-final rhyme with matched clause structure, pointing to the oratorical variety
fields.tutor_destination: moderate: text-to-register classification drills are feasible, but they need real specimens rather than the lesson's composed ones

fields.advanced_explanation: the fallback to constituent order is licensed only where case exponents are genuinely unrealised; the energetic is licensed by an oath particle, by an emphatic command, or by elevated register; particle-based case prediction is reliable only in a text that maintains the older rigour
fields.beginner_explanation: Separates two registers of the standard written language and enumerates the grammatical features that distinguish them, so that a reader knows which cue - case exponent or constituent order - carries the functional load in a given text. It frames the difference as register and period variation rather than as correctness, and closes with a feature-by-feature comparison of a chronicle passage against a modern retelling of the same events.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: treating the later register as a corrupted form of the older one; confusing dual exponents with plural exponents because the letters overlap
fields.contrast_or_transfer: dual nominative exponent versus dual oblique exponent versus sound plural exponents; heavy versus light emphatic nun
fields.intermediate_explanation: form the energetic by taking the jussive stem and suffixing the heavy or the light nun, respecting the paradigm gaps; before assigning function, decide whether the text realises case at all; if it does not, fall back on order and context; compare a passage and its retelling feature by feature and record each substitution
fields.prerequisite_statement: the three cases and their exponents in singular, dual, and plural; jussive formation; the emphatic particle family and their case effects
fields.recognition_cue: dual exponents co-occurring on a noun, a relative, a verb, and an attached pronoun within one clause mark the older register; a doubled or single nun suffixed to a jussive-shaped stem marks the energetic; sukun on every phrase-final word, with no case vowels realised, marks pausal delivery rather than absent grammar
fields.tutor_destination: strong for dual-versus-plural exponent drills and energetic formation drills; register-identification drills need real passages, and the lesson's constructed contrast sentences must not be used as drill targets because several contain agreement mismatches

fields.advanced_explanation: the referents of the original participants must be recoverable before any pronoun can be shifted; the deictic shift is licensed only where the reporting context is actually displaced from the original; the complementizer must be selected to match the reporting verb
fields.beginner_explanation: Teaches the conversion of quoted speech into reported speech, treating the operation as a coordinated re-anchoring of person, place and time deixis under a reporting frame rather than as the insertion of a single particle.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: leaving first person forms unshifted inside reported content; leaving proximal demonstratives unshifted when the reporting context is displaced
fields.contrast_or_transfer: quoted against reported framing of the same content; first person in the original against third person in the report
fields.intermediate_explanation: identify the original speaker, the addressee and the reporter; shift every first and second person form to the perspective of the reporter; shift proximal deictics where the reporting context is displaced
fields.prerequisite_statement: detached and attached pronoun inventories; demonstrative series near and far; the subordinating particles and their case effects
fields.recognition_cue: a reporting verb followed by a complementizer marks the boundary of reported content; a third-person pronoun immediately after the complementizer is a candidate for the original speaker rather than for a new referent; a distal demonstrative inside reported content may correspond to a proximal one in the original utterance
fields.tutor_destination: high — conversion drills are well defined for declaratives, but items must state the reporting context explicitly or the deictic shift has no determinate answer

fields.advanced_explanation: the restriction reading depends on the fronted element being an argument of the verb rather than a loose adverbial; a prepositional unit counts as a comment only through an understood host; an estimate for an unexpressed element must be recoverable from the context of use, otherwise the parse is unconstrained
fields.beginner_explanation: Opens the module by running full word-by-word parsing over short fixed scriptural formulas and by arguing that the parse is a precondition for interpretation rather than an ornament. Three worked segments (cited only: Q 1:1, Q 1:2, Q 1:5, with a reading pair at Q 1:4) carry three distinct payloads - estimation of an unexpressed host, object fronting for restriction, and a prepositional unit filling the comment slot.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: assuming a fixed prepositional formula is syntactically complete as it stands; reading a fronted object as stylistic rearrangement with no semantic effect
fields.contrast_or_transfer: verb with enclitic object versus fronted detached pronoun followed by the verb; restriction by fronting versus by the compound restrictive particle versus by negation plus exception
fields.intermediate_explanation: tabulate every word with form class, case or indeclinability, function label, and governor; when a slot is empty, name the missing element and state the estimate explicitly instead of leaving the parse open; restate the segment in unmarked order, then state precisely what the marked order adds
fields.prerequisite_statement: the three cases and their exponents; verbless clause structure with topic and comment; prepositions assigning genitive
fields.recognition_cue: a clause opening with preposition plus genitive that contains no verb and no participle signals an unexpressed attachment host; a detached accusative pronoun standing before a finite verb, where an enclitic object was available, signals the restriction reading as a candidate; a definite nominative noun followed only by preposition plus genitive, with no verb anywhere, signals a verbless clause with a prepositional comment
fields.tutor_destination: strong for governor-identification and unmarked-versus-marked-order drills; any drill touching a specific aya must be citation-only and must not auto-score against a single estimate for the unexpressed host
fields.unresolved_notice: school-dependent: the estimate for the unexpressed host of the opening formula is unsettled and the lesson lists rivals without adjudicating; rival analyses: topic-with-prepositional-comment versus fronted-comment-with-unexpressed-topic for the praise formula

fields.advanced_explanation: restriction should be applied only where exclusion of alternatives is actually intended; device selection is conditioned on the communicative setting, not on the proposition; the order adjustment is required whenever the default order would focus the wrong element
fields.beginner_explanation: Turns the two restriction devices from objects of analysis into instruments of composition: converting general propositions into restricted ones, choosing between the devices by register, and analysing official prose for restriction scope. Runs the module's analytic content in the production direction.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: applying restriction where only assertion was meant; choosing the device that mismatches the setting
fields.contrast_or_transfer: general versus restricted proposition; the implicit device versus the explicit device, compared on register and force
fields.intermediate_explanation: identify the two predication roles, decide which is to be confined to the other, then apply the chosen device with the order that puts the target in the focused slot; select the device by register: implicit for calm assertion and wisdom, explicit for argument, rebuttal and legal text; analyse a document in three steps: locate the marker, identify what is restricted to what, state the implicit negation
fields.prerequisite_statement: L5.M1.06 restriction with the single particle, including its case consequence; L5.M1.07 negation-plus-exception and its case branches; predication-role terminology
fields.recognition_cue: scan for a clause-initial restrictive particle or for a negator paired with an exception particle inside a clause; identify what precedes the marker and what occupies the focused position; state the excluded set to make the commitment explicit
fields.tutor_destination: high — transformation exercises with a fixed target element are objectively scorable, and the three-step document analysis is a reusable rubric
fields.unresolved_notice: the claim that both devices are truth-conditionally equivalent inherits the unresolved dispute flagged at L5.M1.06 about whether exclusion is encoded or inferred

fields.advanced_explanation: the substitution diagnostic applies only where the resulting phrase remains sensible, which excludes source and origin readings; the partitive reading changes the semantic relation but leaves the case assignment untouched; a claim may be attributed to a commentator only when the layer it comes from is known
fields.beginner_explanation: Teaches the classical commentary as a genre with its own readable syntax: a recurring three-move block of lemma marker, gloss marker, and justification marker, applied recursively across a base text and stacked in layers of base text, commentary, and marginal super-commentary. The grammatical payload is preposition-sense assignment, worked through the partitive reading and its substitution test.
fields.contrast_or_transfer: lemma versus gloss versus justification as three distinct moves with distinct markers; partitive versus source or origin reading of the same preposition
fields.intermediate_explanation: segment a commentary page into blocks by locating each lemma marker; for each block, separate the quoted lemma from the gloss and from the evidence before extracting any claim; apply the substitution diagnostic to decide whether a preposition is partitive
fields.prerequisite_statement: the grammatical label set taught in the preceding lesson; prepositions and the genitive they assign; passive formation and agent deletion
fields.recognition_cue: a lemma marker followed by a short quoted string identifies the segment under discussion and separates base text from commentary; a gloss marker introduces a paraphrase, a definition, or a syntactic analysis rather than more base text; a justification marker introduces evidence, and the evidence type can be classified as lexical contrast, parallel passage, grammatical rule, or logical inference
fields.tutor_destination: strong for marker-to-move identification and for the substitution diagnostic, both of which work on independently chosen standard examples; drills must accept a disjunction as a correct answer where the sense is genuinely open

fields.advanced_explanation: the text is vocalized; the consonant actually bears a mark; a consonant may legitimately bear no vowel at all, marked separately
fields.beginner_explanation: Introduces the three short-vowel diacritics as marks attached to consonants rather than as letters, fixes their shapes and above/below placement, and explains that ordinary written Arabic omits them so that readers must recover vowels from context, from word patterns, and from grammatical endings.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: exchanging the a-mark and the i-mark; pronouncing the u-mark as a long back vowel
fields.contrast_or_transfer: the above-placed against the below-placed oblique stroke; short vowel against its lengthened counterpart
fields.intermediate_explanation: work through the word from right to left, reading each consonant together with the mark written on it; when transliterating, emit the consonant then the vowel of its mark; when a consonant carries no mark, do not supply a vowel by guesswork
fields.prerequisite_statement: the consonant inventory; positional letter forms
fields.recognition_cue: a short oblique stroke above a consonant versus the same stroke below it; a small hook resembling a miniature wow-letter above the consonant; absence of any mark, which signals either vowellessness, an unvocalized text, or a carrier configuration rather than a default vowel
fields.tutor_destination: high - mark identification, placement, and CV transliteration are mechanical and closed-set

fields.advanced_explanation: template choice for Form I depends on the present stem, not on the past stem; the derived-form rule presupposes correct passive-participle formation; the abstract-noun suffix requires a nominal or adjectival base
fields.beginner_explanation: Presents two verbal-noun strategies that dominate technical and formal writing: the mim-initial verbal noun, whose Form I shape is set by the present-stem vowel and whose derived-form shape coincides with the passive participle, and the suffix-built abstract noun that turns a noun or adjective into a quality term. Trains the learner to feel the concreteness contrast between a mim-initial form and the ordinary verbal noun of the same root.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: reading an ambiguous mim form as a place noun when the context calls for an action noun; choosing the mim template from the past stem rather than the present stem
fields.contrast_or_transfer: mim-initial verbal noun versus ordinary verbal noun of the same root; mim-initial verbal noun versus place or time noun of identical shape
fields.intermediate_explanation: identify the root and strip the mim prefix; for Form I, read the present-stem middle vowel and select the matching template; for derived forms, build the passive participle and use that shape
fields.prerequisite_statement: ordinary verbal-noun families; present-stem vowelling of Form I; passive participle formation across Forms II to X
fields.recognition_cue: a noun with a prefixed mim whose remaining consonants are the root and whose vowels match one of the two Form I templates; for derived forms, a mim-prefixed noun with the passive-participle vowelling used where an action noun is expected; a noun ending in the doubled-glide plus feminine sequence built transparently on a free-standing noun or adjective
fields.tutor_destination: strong: present-stem-to-template drills are deterministic and suffixation drills are mechanical; function disambiguation needs context-bearing items

fields.advanced_explanation: the root must be trilateral; the verb must inflect rather than be frozen; the quality must admit degrees
fields.beginner_explanation: Teaches the two fixed exclamatory templates, the conditions a verb must satisfy before either template can be built on it, and the workaround construction that routes a disqualified verb through a helper template plus its verbal noun.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: leaving the exclaimed element nominative in the first template; building the first template directly on an augmented stem
fields.contrast_or_transfer: plain predication against exclamation of the same quality; accusative marking in the first template against prepositional marking in the second
fields.intermediate_explanation: identify the root and check it against the six conditions; if licensed, build the elative shape and place the exclaimed element in the accusative for the first template; or build the imperative-shaped form and attach the element with the fixed preposition for the second template
fields.prerequisite_statement: root extraction and trilateral against augmented stems; the elative pattern; verbal noun formation
fields.recognition_cue: a clause-initial ما followed immediately by a fixed elative-shaped word and an accusative noun; an imperative-shaped word of the elative pattern followed by a prepositional phrase with no addressee in context; a helper exclamatory form followed by a verbal noun, signalling the indirect route
