fields.tutor_destination: high — the condition set converts cleanly into a licensed against unlicensed sorting drill with a repair step, which is a stronger exercise than form recall alone
fields.unresolved_notice: the analysis of the initial element as a dedicated particle is one school position, and a competing tradition analyses it as a nominal head, which the lesson does not attribute

fields.advanced_explanation: the matrix verb must be one that would otherwise take two accusative complements; the suspending particle must stand between the verb and the material it would otherwise govern; the following material must form a complete clause
fields.beginner_explanation: Teaches that an interrogative or negative particle standing between a mental-state verb and its expected complement blocks that verb from assigning case across it, so the following clause keeps its own internal case pattern.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: Classifying the complementiser meaning that among the suspending particles.; Forcing accusative endings onto the clause that follows a suspending particle.
fields.contrast_or_transfer: a mental-state verb with its plain double-accusative frame against the same verb followed by a suspending particle; a suspending interrogative against the non-suspending complementiser
fields.intermediate_explanation: classify the matrix verb as a mental-state verb or not; check whether an interrogative or a negative particle immediately follows it; if such a particle is present, do not assign the verb's accusative frame to the following material
fields.prerequisite_statement: double-accusative verbs and their complement frame; nominative topic and predicate in nominal sentences; interrogative particles and their meanings
fields.recognition_cue: the matrix verb belongs to the knowing, supposing or perceiving class; an interrogative or negative particle immediately follows that verb; the material after the particle is a complete clause with its own subject and predicate
fields.tutor_destination: high - drills can contrast the same matrix verb with a suspending particle and with the complementiser, requiring different case output

fields.advanced_explanation: the specifier must be indefinite; the specifier must be accusative; the specifier must follow, not precede, the specified element
fields.beginner_explanation: Teaches the accusative specification noun that resolves vagueness in a preceding element, and splits it into a stated-quantity type and an implied type. Fixes the three formal requirements on the specifier and supplies discriminators separating it from three other accusative or genitive roles.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: making the specifier definite; putting the specifier in the genitive after an elative
fields.contrast_or_transfer: stated-quantity subtype versus implied subtype; specification versus the circumstantial accusative: respect versus state
fields.intermediate_explanation: locate the vague element; decide whether that element is overtly stated or only implied; supply the noun naming the domain of the vagueness
fields.prerequisite_statement: the accusative case and its licensing roles; elative formation; numeral bands and their complement rules
fields.recognition_cue: an indefinite accusative noun immediately after an elative; an indefinite accusative noun after a numeral, measure or container word; an indefinite accusative noun after a verb of filling, overflowing, increasing or becoming pleasant
fields.tutor_destination: strong: role-discrimination items and form-selection items both generate cleanly once trigger inventories exist

fields.advanced_explanation: there must be two or more governors preceding the shared noun; the shared noun must be a plausible argument of each governor; the resolving pronoun must be selected by the features of the shared noun, not of either subject
fields.beginner_explanation: Teaches the configuration in which two coordinated verbs both stand before a single noun that each of them could take as an argument, and presents the two classical schools' opposing rules for deciding which verb governs it and which is left with a pronoun.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: Treating one of the two school analyses as ungrammatical.; Choosing a resolving pronoun whose gender or number does not match the shared noun.
fields.contrast_or_transfer: contention against ordinary coordination in which each verb has its own distinct argument; contention against the preoccupation construction: two governors and one noun versus one governor and a displaced noun
fields.intermediate_explanation: confirm that both verbs precede the disputed noun; confirm that each verb could take that noun in the relevant role; choose an analysis: nearer verb governs, or earlier verb governs
fields.prerequisite_statement: transitivity and direct objects; coordination with the conjunction; attached object pronouns
fields.recognition_cue: two or more finite verbs stand before a single noun; the verbs are typically joined by the coordinating conjunction; each verb is independently capable of taking that noun in the same role
fields.tutor_destination: high - drills can require the learner to resolve the same string twice, once under each school, and to justify the pronoun's features
fields.unresolved_notice: school-dependent: the governor of the shared noun is not determinable from the surface string alone and any projection must carry the school attribution; rival analyses: the traditional treatments also differ over whether an unexpressed pronoun is deletion or non-insertion, which the lesson does not address

fields.advanced_explanation: a contextually salient target must exist and be present or otherwise relevant; the situation must make the intended mapping recoverable to that target; the generic statement must be independently true, which is what preserves deniability
fields.beginner_explanation: Moves indirection from the level of word meaning to the level of who is being addressed: a grammatically general or third-person utterance aimed at one specific hearer present in the situation. Catalogues the syntactic frames that carry this and the social reasons a speaker chooses it over direct address.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: treating every general statement as this device; assuming the device is always hostile
fields.contrast_or_transfer: direct naming of the addressee versus generic or third-person framing; indirection of the addressee versus indirection of the meaning
fields.intermediate_explanation: ask whether the surface is generic or third-person; ask whether one specific present participant satisfies the description; ask whether the situation makes the mapping unambiguous
fields.prerequisite_statement: generic relative clauses and their heads; conditional sentence structure; imperative formation, needed to see what is being avoided
fields.recognition_cue: a generic relative clause whose description is satisfied by exactly one person present in the situation; a conditional or generic frame occupying the discourse slot where a command was expected; an impersonal reporting frame introducing a normative claim
fields.tutor_destination: medium — direct-to-indirect rewriting drills are mechanically checkable, but recognition drills need an authored situation because the string alone underdetermines the reading
fields.unresolved_notice: school-dependent: classical treatments vary on whether this is an independent device or a species of the metonymy device, and the clean addressee-versus-meaning split is the lesson's own framing

fields.advanced_explanation: both poles must be recoverable for the comparison classification to hold at all; the exponent must be overt for the exponent-present label; the shared quality must be verbalised for the detailed label
fields.beginner_explanation: Establishes comparison (التشبيه) as an analysable object with a fixed inventory of named slots, so that a learner decomposes a comparison into labelled parts instead of only registering its effect. Adds a naming scheme that classifies any comparison by which of the two optional slots have been left out.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: swapping the two poles, treating the vivid or familiar term as the thing being described; calling the doubly-omitted type a metaphor because no exponent appears
fields.contrast_or_transfer: exponent present versus exponent omitted; shared quality stated versus left to inference
fields.intermediate_explanation: identify the two poles by asking what is being described and what it is set against; test for an exponent and assign the exponent-presence label; test whether the shared quality is verbalised and assign the explicitness label
fields.prerequisite_statement: genitive marking after a preposition or prefixed particle; annexation and the genitive of its second term; the إنّ family and accusative assignment to its first term
fields.recognition_cue: a one-letter prefixed comparison particle standing before a genitive noun; an independent comparison noun heading an annexation; the كأنّ frame introducing a clause with an accusative first term
fields.tutor_destination: high for slot-labelling and type-classification drills on short supplied comparisons; items must be authored because the classification turns on semantics rather than surface form
fields.unresolved_notice: analysis-dependent: whether exponent omission asserts identity or merely compresses

fields.advanced_explanation: exact form identity is required, not near identity or a synonym; the repeating token follows immediately; clause repetition requires the whole clause
fields.beginner_explanation: Presents the repetition variety of the emphasis follower: reinforcement obtained by repeating a token identically, extended beyond nominals to verbs, particles, and whole clauses, and set explicitly against the meaning-word variety taught in the preceding lesson.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: repeating a verb in a different tense or a different form; repeating a nominal with a different case ending
fields.contrast_or_transfer: repetition emphasis versus meaning-word emphasis; repetition versus coordination of two identical items
fields.intermediate_explanation: confirm token identity including vowelling; confirm inflectional identity across case for nominals and across tense, person, and number for verbs; assign the emphasized and emphasizer roles by linear order
fields.prerequisite_statement: semantic emphasis from L4.M2.02; verb tense, person, and number morphology; case inflection
fields.recognition_cue: two adjacent tokens identical in segmental form and in inflection; no coordinator and no pause particle standing between them; the second token introduces no new argument and fills no independent syntactic slot
fields.tutor_destination: medium - identity checks drill cleanly, but the rhetorical effect items are interpretive and are not safely auto-gradable

fields.advanced_explanation: the emphasizer follows the reinforced noun and does not precede it; a clitic is obligatory whenever the emphasizer follows an overt noun; the gendered choice between the two dual emphasizers is fixed by referent gender
fields.beginner_explanation: Develops the emphasis follower in its meaning-word variety: a small closed set of nominals placed after a noun to reinforce identity or totality, each obligatorily carrying a clitic pronoun coindexed with the reinforced noun and copying its case, with a separate gendered pair reserved for duals.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: leaving the emphasizer bare with no clitic; attaching a clitic whose gender does not match the reinforced noun
fields.contrast_or_transfer: identity emphasis versus totality emphasis; wholeness-focused totality versus collective-inclusion totality
fields.intermediate_explanation: identify the reinforced noun and read its case and phi-features; select the emphasizer by the intended force, identity or totality; attach the clitic matching person, gender, and number
fields.prerequisite_statement: the clitic pronoun paradigm; three-case inflection; dual inflection and its two shapes
fields.recognition_cue: a post-nominal member of a small closed nominal set; an attached clitic pronoun coindexed with the immediately preceding noun; a case marker identical to that of the preceding noun
fields.tutor_destination: high - clitic selection and case copying are deterministic once the head features are known

fields.advanced_explanation: only the listed causative informing and showing verbs take three complements; the ordering with the person first is fixed; all three complements require accusative marking
fields.beginner_explanation: Teaches the small class of verbs that take three accusative complements, presenting them as causatives derived from the two-complement mental-state verbs and assigning each complement a distinct role.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: Placing the content complement before the person complement.; Omitting the third complement while still intending the full three-complement reading.
fields.contrast_or_transfer: one-complement transitives against two-complement mental-state verbs against three-complement causatives; the non-causative base verb against its causative counterpart
fields.intermediate_explanation: identify the verb and confirm class membership; assign the first complement to the person informed or shown; assign the second complement to the content
fields.prerequisite_statement: transitivity and accusative objects; two-complement mental-state verbs and their topic-predicate origin; causative derivation by the augmenting prefix
fields.recognition_cue: the verb belongs to the listed informing or showing class; three accusative-marked constituents follow it, or two follow a clitic that counts as the first; the first constituent denotes an animate recipient of knowledge
fields.tutor_destination: high - drills can require converting a two-complement clause into its causative counterpart and labelling the three positions

fields.advanced_explanation: all three requirements must hold simultaneously; the string is taken in isolation, without contextual completion; imperatives and other forms whose subject is implicit, treated by classical analysis as complete through an estimated pronoun, are not reconciled with the stated two-word minimum
fields.beginner_explanation: Draws the technical line between a single lexical unit and a string that counts as speech in the grammarians' sense, and states three conditions that must hold jointly for the stronger label to apply. The purpose is to fix a metalinguistic threshold before any sentence analysis begins.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: treating any meaningful word as an instance of technical speech; accepting a multi-word string as speech because it contains more than one word
fields.contrast_or_transfer: word versus utterance; multi-word fragment versus complete assertion
fields.intermediate_explanation: apply the three conditions in fixed order and reject on the first failure; when rejecting, name which condition failed rather than judging by feel
fields.prerequisite_statement: reading vowelled Arabic; the notion that individual words carry meaning
fields.recognition_cue: count the independent words in the string; test whether a hearer is left waiting for a completion; test whether the arrangement follows the language's conventions rather than being arbitrary sound
fields.tutor_destination: good source for a classify-the-string drill in which the learner must name the failing condition rather than answer yes or no

fields.advanced_explanation: verse register for the licensed reading; the verb's default frame must be established independently before any deviation is claimed; for object withholding, the absence of a recoverable antecedent is what makes the reading rhetorical rather than ordinary
fields.beginner_explanation: Treats verse-level manipulation of verbal valency, both supplying a direct object to a verb whose default frame excludes one and withholding the object of a verb whose frame requires one, and attaches the two grammatical schools' rival accounts of whether valency is inherent or contextual.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: Confusing a valency shift with a derived causative form.; Treating every omitted object as a poetic device.
fields.contrast_or_transfer: supplying an object vs withholding one; bare accusative object vs prepositional complement
fields.intermediate_explanation: identify the verb and its default valency from the lexicon; check the context for an unexpected accusative object, or for an unexpected absence of one; classify the device by which of the two configurations is found
fields.prerequisite_statement: verb and object identification and accusative marking; prepositional complementation; the derived causative pattern and its effect on valency
fields.recognition_cue: an accusative noun governed directly by a verb whose lexical frame does not license one, with no preposition mediating; an object-taking verb with no object present where the frame requires one; the missing object is not recoverable from the immediate context, so the gap is doing rhetorical work
fields.tutor_destination: high + valency discrimination and device classification are cleanly drillable and the closing classification grid is a genuine drill, though the phrases used are constructed rather than cited
fields.unresolved_notice: the classification of the personifying example under intellectual metaphor competes with a reading as implicit simile, and the schools' positions are reported without primary citation

fields.advanced_explanation: genitive marking applies to whatever nominal directly follows the particle; the source-to-goal reading requires the paired particles to occur together in one clause; the bound members require orthographic attachment to the following word
fields.beginner_explanation: Presents a working set of governing particles that place their complement in the genitive, and shows that each one carries a spread of relational senses beyond its primary meaning. It also introduces verb-specific particle selection.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: leaving the complement of a particle in a non-genitive form; substituting the source particle for the topic particle or the reverse
fields.contrast_or_transfer: source particle versus topic particle, which the lesson treats as a primary confusion pair; spatial sense versus abstract sense of the same particle
fields.intermediate_explanation: identify the particle; identify the nominal it governs; mark that nominal genitive
fields.prerequisite_statement: the three case labels and their markers; the definite article and how it merges with bound prefixes; basic noun and verb vocabulary
fields.recognition_cue: a closed-class function word immediately preceding a nominal; the following nominal shows a genitive marker, or would if it were fully vowelled; two members appear as a bound prefix on the following word rather than as separate tokens
fields.tutor_destination: high — case assignment is mechanical; sense selection and verb pairing need contextual items rather than isolated forms
fields.unresolved_notice: classification of location words as particles versus adverbials is analysis-dependent

fields.advanced_explanation: the input is fully vocalized, since every step of the routine reads a mark; the token has been segmented from any attached clitic before analysis; the a-form of nunation is written without its support after the tied grapheme
fields.beginner_explanation: A capstone that applies every orthographic device of the module jointly to whole words and short sentences. It supplies a letter-by-letter analysis routine for reading fully vocalized text and an ordered production routine for writing it, and it labels the nunation endings with case names for the first time.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: reading past the gemination mark and pronouncing a single consonant; reading a nunation ending as a plain short vowel
fields.contrast_or_transfer: short against long vowels in near-identical consonant frames; assimilating against non-assimilating article environments in worked examples
fields.intermediate_explanation: tabulate the word letter by letter, recording each letter with the mark it carries; assign a value or a function to every mark before pronouncing anything; decide the article's behaviour from the class of the following letter
fields.prerequisite_statement: every preceding lesson of the module
fields.recognition_cue: a gemination mark on the letter after the article, indicating assimilation rather than lexical doubling; a doubled vowel mark at the word edge, indicating an indefinite ending rather than a plain vowel; a long vowel identified as a short-vowel mark plus an unmarked matching carrier
fields.tutor_destination: high - the analysis routine and the writing order convert directly into staged, auto-gradable drill templates with per-stage checkpoints

fields.advanced_explanation: the melodies are stated for past and imperfect; the derived-form melodies are stated for three forms explicitly; the medial-weak melody replaces the ordinary melody, it does not combine with it
fields.beginner_explanation: Introduces voice as a vowel melody imposed on an existing stem in both tenses, and shows that the derived forms keep their identifying consonants while their internal vowels are overwritten. Adds the distinct melody used by medial-weak stems and opens the syntactic consequence that the next lesson develops.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: leaving the active vowel melody in place while treating the sentence as passive; keeping the active prefix vowel in the imperfect passive
fields.contrast_or_transfer: active against passive melody in each tense; past passive melody against imperfect passive melody
fields.intermediate_explanation: identify the form number and the stem class first; overwrite the internal vowels with the melody for the tense in question; leave every template consonant in place
fields.prerequisite_statement: the derived-form series and their templates; sound-verb paradigms in both tenses; medial-weak stem behaviour, which this lesson assumes rather than teaches
fields.recognition_cue: damma on the first radical with kasra on the second in a past-shaped word; damma on the person prefix of an imperfect-shaped word; fatha on the middle radical where the active would carry a lexically fixed vowel
fields.tutor_destination: strong active-to-passive conversion drills stratified by form number and stem class; drills should include medial-weak stems so the class-specific melody is not treated as an afterthought

fields.advanced_explanation: a verb or verbal equivalent must precede; the nominal must be accusative; the accompaniment sense must be intended rather than coordination
fields.beginner_explanation: Introduces the accusative accompaniment object and the discrimination between the accompaniment sense of the connective and its coordinating sense, presenting four licensing conditions and a semantic test for choosing between the two readings.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: putting the nominal after the accompaniment connective in the nominative; reading coordination as accompaniment when both nominals can perform the event
fields.contrast_or_transfer: accompaniment connective versus coordinating connective; accompaniment object versus direct object
fields.intermediate_explanation: confirm a verb precedes the connective; read the case of the following nominal; apply the participation test to the following nominal
fields.prerequisite_statement: coordination and case agreement between coordinated nominals; accusative exponents by noun class including dual and sound plurals; verb-subject structure
fields.recognition_cue: a connective followed by an accusative nominal in a clause whose subject role is already filled; the following nominal is inanimate or otherwise incapable of performing the event; no second verb is present that could license the nominal as its own subject
fields.tutor_destination: high for case-selection drills; medium for reading drills, since the participation test yields contested answers on the animate cases the lesson itself admits
fields.unresolved_notice: how freely the accompaniment reading is available with animate, capable nominals is disputed and treated differently by the schools; the lesson asserts availability without attribution; the participation test is semantic, but the schools ground the distinction in case marking, so the two can diverge

fields.advanced_explanation: first-radical deletion applies in the imperfect stem, not in the past; final-radical deletion applies under the jussive; the prosthetic hamza is licensed only when the stem would otherwise open with a vowelless consonant
fields.beginner_explanation: Puts two weak radicals into one root and teaches how the rules already learned for first-position and final-position weakness apply to the same stem. Divides the class by whether the two weak radicals are adjacent or held apart by a sound consonant, and uses the resulting extreme shortening to show that surface length is not a guide to root length.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: restoring the first weak radical into the imperfect of the separated subtype; keeping the final weak radical under a jussive operator
fields.contrast_or_transfer: separated subtype against adjacent subtype across a full form-by-form comparison; this class against the simple first-weak class of L4.M1.01
fields.intermediate_explanation: count the weak radicals and locate them before choosing a subtype; for the separated subtype, apply first-radical deletion to build the imperfect stem, then apply final-radical behaviour on top of it; for the adjacent subtype, keep the middle weak consonant and apply only final-radical behaviour
fields.prerequisite_statement: L4.M1.01 first-radical deletion in the imperfect; L4.M1.02 final-radical realisation, restoration and jussive deletion; participle templates for sound verbs
fields.recognition_cue: a citation form whose first and third letters are both weak, with a sound consonant between them; a citation form whose last two letters are both weak; an imperfect exposing only one root consonant plus a long vowel, which points to the separated subtype
fields.tutor_destination: high value as a synthesis drill: supply a root and a target cell, require the learner to apply both rules in order; also a good discrimination drill between the two subtypes given only a citation form

fields.advanced_explanation: stated for the closed inventory the lesson lists; the annexation behaviour presupposes the annexation rules from the preceding lesson; the prepositional paraphrase is offered for the free-standing time items
fields.beginner_explanation: Introduces the adverbial of time and place as an accusative complement, explaining the containment metaphor behind its classical name and grounding its case in an implicit locative preposition. It supplies a working inventory of items in both classes and connects the ones that require a dependent to the annexation construction taught immediately before.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: marking the noun that follows an adverbial as accusative because the adverbial itself is accusative; labelling any accusative noun as a direct object
fields.contrast_or_transfer: time adverbials against place adverbials, discriminated by the question each answers; direct object against adverbial: what the action is done to against what it is done in
fields.intermediate_explanation: ask whether the noun answers the when question or the where question; decide whether the item stands alone or requires a dependent; if it stands alone, expect an accusative tanwin
fields.prerequisite_statement: the case system and its exponents; accusative marking on direct objects; the annexation construction and its invariant genitive
fields.recognition_cue: a noun answering when or where rather than naming a participant; accusative marking, either an accusative tanwin on a free-standing item or a bare fatha on an item that heads a dependent; membership in a small closed inventory of frequent items
fields.tutor_destination: high — the item inventory, the two-case phrase pattern and the class-split diagnostic all yield deterministic items; the built items must be excluded from any drill that asserts the blanket accusative rule

fields.advanced_explanation: the word is a noun or adjective; the word does not carry the definite article; the three final graphemes that block the supporting alif
fields.beginner_explanation: Introduces nunation: the three doubled-vowel endings that add a nasal to a noun, the writing rule that the a-form normally needs a silent supporting alif, the three graphemic environments that exempt it, and the claim that nunation marks a noun as indefinite and cannot co-occur with the definite article.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: writing the a-form of nunation without its supporting alif on a word that requires one; pronouncing the supporting alif as a vowel
fields.contrast_or_transfer: a nunated form against the same noun with the definite article; nunation against gemination, which look superficially similar as descriptions but do different work
fields.intermediate_explanation: identify the doubled mark, read its base vowel, then append the nasal; when writing the a-form, add the supporting alif unless the word ends in one of the three exempt graphemes; never write nunation together with the definite article on the same word
fields.prerequisite_statement: the three short-vowel marks; the tied taa and the variant final a-spelling as graphemes; the definite article as a written prefix
fields.recognition_cue: a doubled vowel mark on the final letter of a nominal; a final alif carrying a doubled a-mark, where the alif is not pronounced; a doubled mark placed directly on the tied taa with no added alif
fields.tutor_destination: high - ending substitution over a fixed stem and the support-spelling decision are both closed-set
fields.unresolved_notice: the lesson does not say what assigns nominative to the two slots; standard grammars dispute this and the dispute must remain attributed rather than resolved; whether copula-free predication is best modelled as a zero copula or as the absence of any copular element is analysis-dependent and untouched here

fields.advanced_explanation: the possessed item stays nominative because it is the subject, not a complement; an indefinite subject is acceptable here only because the predicate has been fronted; the person suffix must be the attached series, since these hosts do not take free pronouns
fields.beginner_explanation: Shows that Arabic expresses possession without any verb corresponding to 'have', using a fronted adverbial or particle phrase as the predicate with the possessed item as a delayed subject, and distinguishes the available exponents by nuance and register.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: treating the availability and ownership exponents as interchangeable; combining these hosts with a free pronoun instead of an attached one
fields.contrast_or_transfer: availability exponent versus ownership exponent; neutral register versus formal or literary alternant
fields.intermediate_explanation: choose the exponent by whether availability, ownership, accompaniment or formal register is intended; attach the appropriate person suffix to that exponent; place the resulting phrase first
fields.prerequisite_statement: verbless sentence structure with topic and comment; attached pronoun series and host selection; the genitive-governing particles
fields.recognition_cue: there is no verb in the clause, yet a possession relation is asserted; a location or benefactive phrase carrying a person suffix stands first; the item said to be possessed follows and is nominative, commonly indefinite
fields.tutor_destination: high for the frame and its case marking; the nuance contrast needs contextual items rather than isolated sentences, since the split is defeasible
fields.unresolved_notice: classification of the location hosts as particles versus adverbials is analysis-dependent and affects their case treatment; school-dependent: the behaviour of one negating operator over a verbless sentence

fields.advanced_explanation: applies where the comment is a governed phrase rather than a bare word; the head must be a preposition or a locative adverb, not a verb; the locative adverbs listed take a following nominal
fields.beginner_explanation: Introduces the comment realised as a phrase rather than a word, splits it into a preposition-headed type and a locative-adverb type, and lists the prepositions and locative adverbs that commonly head it. Contrasts this realisation with the single-word comment and shows its use for location and possession.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: giving the nominal after a preposition or locative adverb a nominative or accusative ending; vowelling a locative adverb as if it were itself the nominative comment
fields.contrast_or_transfer: single-word comment (describes a quality, nominative) versus phrase comment (locates or attributes, internally genitive); preposition-headed phrase versus locative adverb phrase
fields.intermediate_explanation: select a topic and mark it nominative; choose a preposition or locative adverb according to the spatial or possessive relation intended; place the following nominal in the genitive
fields.prerequisite_statement: the two slots of the noun-initial sentence; the single-word comment and its nominative case; the genitive case name and its exponents
fields.recognition_cue: the material after the topic begins with a preposition or a locative adverb; the nominal after that head carries a genitive exponent; the comment span contains at least two words and no finite verb
fields.tutor_destination: high — the genitive-after-head rule and the realisation label are both mechanically checkable, and the adverb-ending item type elicits a well-defined error
fields.unresolved_notice: whether the governed phrase fills the comment slot or attaches to an unexpressed comment is a standing analytic dispute; the lesson asserts one side without attribution and the dispute must be preserved rather than resolved; analysis-dependent: whether an attached object pronoun is itself the object or occupies an accusative position is stated differently in traditional and modern descriptions

fields.advanced_explanation: the number-agreement suppression holds only while the verb precedes its agent; the taught patterns use past-tense verbs with overt nominal agents; the object rule assumes a transitive verb with an expressed object
fields.beginner_explanation: Introduces the verb-initial sentence as the second sentence type, names its verb and agent constituents, fixes the default constituent order, assigns nominative to the agent and accusative to the object, and states the order-conditioned agreement behaviour of the verb. Ends by contrasting the two sentence types as alternative framings of one situation.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: using a plural verb form before a plural agent in verb-initial order; omitting the feminine exponent on a verb whose agent is feminine
fields.contrast_or_transfer: verb-initial versus noun-initial sentence type; agent (nominative doer) versus object (accusative undergoer)
fields.intermediate_explanation: place the verb first; read the agent's gender and select the verb's gender exponent accordingly; keep the verb singular irrespective of the agent's number while the verb precedes
fields.prerequisite_statement: the noun-initial sentence and its two slots; the case names and their exponents; past-tense verb forms as vocabulary
fields.recognition_cue: the first element is a finite verb; the immediately following nominal is nominative and is the doer; the verb is singular even where the following agent is plural
fields.tutor_destination: very high — the order-conditioned agreement asymmetry is a compact rule with a single high-frequency error, and both correct and incorrect forms are generable mechanically
fields.unresolved_notice: analysis-dependent: whether an attached object pronoun is itself the object or occupies an accusative position is stated differently in traditional and modern descriptions; school-dependent: an accusative noun after a motion or entry verb is analysed by different authorities as a true object, as an adverbial of place, or as an accusative after a dropped preposition, and this lesson does not attribute the choice it makes

fields.advanced_explanation: the antecedent must be definite; the following clause must be complete; agreement is computed on the antecedent, never on anything inside the clause
fields.beginner_explanation: Introduces the relative pronoun series as an agreement and licensing problem: which form matches the antecedent in gender and number, which forms alternate for case, and under what condition a relative pronoun may appear at all. The returning pronoun is named here and developed in the following lesson.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: attaching a relative pronoun to an indefinite antecedent; dropping the returning pronoun on the English model
fields.contrast_or_transfer: definite antecedent with a relative pronoun versus indefinite antecedent with a bare clause; human plural versus non-human plural agreement
fields.intermediate_explanation: read the antecedent's gender, number and, for plurals, humanness; select the matching form from the series; for a dual antecedent, select the shape by case
fields.prerequisite_statement: gender and number marking on nouns; definiteness and its exponents, including definiteness through إضافة; the dual's case alternation in ordinary nouns
fields.recognition_cue: a definite noun immediately followed by a member of the series; the selected form agreeing with that noun in gender and number; a complete predication following the form rather than a bare word or phrase
fields.tutor_destination: high: form selection is deterministic once gender, number and humanness are given, and the definiteness gate makes a clean yes-or-no drill with a productive error to catch
fields.unresolved_notice: whether the dual members are genuinely inflected or built with two shapes is disputed; the hidden pronoun is an analytic posit rather than a surface fact, and rival analyses exist

fields.advanced_explanation: the licensor must be identified before any mood is reported for a deletion-exponed form; the conditional reading requires both a condition verb and an answer verb; cluster resolution applies only where a following word begins with a connecting alif
fields.beginner_explanation: Consolidates the three moods into a single verb-class by mood matrix and extends the licensors of the third mood beyond negation to conditional structures. Makes explicit that for one inflectional class two moods are surface-identical, so the mood can only be recovered from the licensor.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: putting the subjunctive vowel where the silent ending belongs; keeping the weak final letter under the third mood
fields.contrast_or_transfer: the three moods set side by side with their licensors and exponents; identical surfaces under different licensors within the nun-bearing class
fields.intermediate_explanation: identify the verb class; identify the licensor and the mood it imposes; read the exponent expected for that class in that mood off the matrix
fields.prerequisite_statement: all three mood licensor inventories from the three preceding lessons; the exponent for each class in the first two moods; identification of weak final radicals
fields.recognition_cue: the ending is silent, or an expected nun is missing, or an expected weak letter is missing; a conditional particle or a conditional noun introduces a clause containing two verbs; a nun-less form of the nun-bearing class occurs with a licensor that must be inspected to fix the mood
fields.tutor_destination: supports discrimination drills built on the syncretic pair where the licensor is the only cue, and repair drills where a cluster-resolved kasra must not be relabelled as a different mood
fields.unresolved_notice: the categorial and positional analysis of the three non-particle condition words is analysis-dependent; the mood status of the imperative is a standing school dispute and the lesson asserts one side

fields.advanced_explanation: the residual assignment is licensed only after both positive class tests have failed; the state-copying rule for coordination assumes the two conjuncts occupy the same position; content interrogatives look like function words but are excluded from the class
fields.beginner_explanation: Completes the three-way division by defining the residual class negatively, giving a rejection-based test in place of positive markers, and subdividing the class into four functional groups with their governing effects.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: classifying content interrogatives as particles because they are short function-like words; leaving the noun after a preposition in a non-genitive state
fields.contrast_or_transfer: residual class against the other two across the article, nunation and conjugation tests; content interrogative of the naming class versus yes-no particle of the residual class
fields.intermediate_explanation: run the three rejections; if all three fail to attach, assign the residual class; then place the word in its functional group by what it does to its neighbours; for the multifunction coordinator, decide the function from the clause context rather than from the word alone
fields.prerequisite_statement: L1.M2.05 naming-class markers; L1.M2.06 action-class markers; L1.M2.04 class inventory
fields.recognition_cue: the word rejects the article; the word rejects nunation; the word cannot be conjugated and takes no verbal marker
fields.tutor_destination: strong for a group-assignment drill and for a disambiguate-the-coordinator drill; the negator table supports a select-the-right-negator-for-the-time-frame drill
fields.unresolved_notice: classification of location words as particles versus adverbials is analysis-dependent; government by an unwritten أن versus government by the lam itself is a school dispute that the lesson presents without attribution

fields.advanced_explanation: the possessed item stays nominative because it is the subject, not a complement; an indefinite subject is acceptable here only because the predicate has been fronted; the person suffix must be the attached series, since these hosts do not take free pronouns
fields.beginner_explanation: Shows that Arabic expresses possession without any verb corresponding to 'have', using a fronted adverbial or particle phrase as the predicate with the possessed item as a delayed subject, and distinguishes the available exponents by nuance and register.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: treating the availability and ownership exponents as interchangeable; combining these hosts with a free pronoun instead of an attached one
fields.contrast_or_transfer: availability exponent versus ownership exponent; neutral register versus formal or literary alternant
fields.intermediate_explanation: choose the exponent by whether availability, ownership, accompaniment or formal register is intended; attach the appropriate person suffix to that exponent; place the resulting phrase first
fields.prerequisite_statement: verbless sentence structure with topic and comment; attached pronoun series and host selection; the genitive-governing particles
fields.recognition_cue: there is no verb in the clause, yet a possession relation is asserted; a location or benefactive phrase carrying a person suffix stands first; the item said to be possessed follows and is nominative, commonly indefinite
fields.tutor_destination: high for the frame and its case marking; the nuance contrast needs contextual items rather than isolated sentences, since the split is defeasible
fields.unresolved_notice: classification of the location hosts as particles versus adverbials is analysis-dependent and affects their case treatment; school-dependent: the behaviour of one negating operator over a verbless sentence

fields.advanced_explanation: the categorisation is stated at class level, so membership must be established before the ending is interpreted; visible vowelling is needed for the variable type to display anything; fixed words still occupy positions that would otherwise carry a case, which the lesson names in passing without developing positional case
fields.beginner_explanation: Introduces the split between words whose ending varies with grammatical function and words whose ending is fixed, and supplies class-level inventories on each side so that a fixed ending is not misread as evidence of a syntactic role.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: placing a free pronoun in a slot that only accepts a suffixed one, for instance directly after a transitive verb; ignoring the vowel that separates the two second-person singular forms
fields.contrast_or_transfer: variable-ending word versus fixed-ending word; perfect stem against imperfect stem on the inflection question
fields.intermediate_explanation: before reading a final vowel as evidence of a role, check whether the word belongs to a fixed category; for an inflected word, read the ending and connect it to its position; for a fixed word, record the shape and treat its role as positional rather than marked
fields.prerequisite_statement: L1.M2.01 case labels and vowels; L1.M2.04 class inventory; L1.M2.05 to L1.M2.07 class membership tests
fields.recognition_cue: the same word appearing with different final vowels across positions, which indicates the variable type; membership in one of the listed fixed categories; a word whose ending stays constant across subject, object and prepositional positions
fields.tutor_destination: strong for a classify-by-type drill and for a should-you-read-this-ending-as-a-case drill; the misstated example about the complement of a verb of asking must not be reused in drill copy
fields.unresolved_notice: rival analyses: post-verbal free pronoun as emphatic subject versus reinforcing appositive; school-dependent: whether the dual demonstratives are genuinely declinable or invariant with substituted endings

fields.advanced_explanation: the override applies when the plural head denotes non-humans; definiteness matching is the axis that determines whether the string is a phrase at all; case agreement holds regardless of which governor assigned the case
fields.beginner_explanation: Sets out attributive modification (النعت والمنعوت) as agreement on four simultaneous axes, and shows that mismatching one of them either produces ungrammaticality or reanalyses the string as a predication rather than a phrase.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: modifying a non-human plural head with a plural adjective; treating a definite noun followed by an indefinite adjective as a noun phrase
fields.contrast_or_transfer: definite head with definite adjective versus definite head with indefinite adjective; human plural agreement versus non-human plural agreement
fields.intermediate_explanation: fix the head noun's case from its role in the clause; read the head's gender, number and definiteness; build the adjective on the same four values
fields.prerequisite_statement: the three cases and their exponents; definiteness marking; gender and number marking on nouns
fields.recognition_cue: a noun immediately followed by a descriptive word carrying the same case exponent, the same definiteness marking and matching gender/number; a definite noun followed by an indefinite descriptive word, which signals predication rather than modification; a non-human plural head followed by a feminine singular descriptive word, which is modification and not a mismatch
fields.tutor_destination: drills should vary one axis at a time and include the non-human plural override plus at least one definiteness-mismatch item
fields.unresolved_notice: analysis-dependent: describing the adjective as copying the head's case is one formulation; the follower relation is described differently in traditional terms; school-dependent: whether the dual demonstratives are genuinely declinable or invariant with substituted endings

fields.advanced_explanation: the prosthetic alif is added only when the residue would otherwise be unpronounceable at the start of an utterance; the vowel computation reads the stem vowel of the imperfect, not the vowel of the perfect; the derivation is defined for addressee persons
fields.beginner_explanation: Derives the command form from the third-mood stem by removing the person prefix and, where the residue would begin with a vowelless consonant, supplying a prosthetic connecting alif whose vowel is computed from the stem. Separates positive commands from negative ones, which are built on a governed imperfect rather than on the command form.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: putting the wrong vowel on the prosthetic alif; prefixing a prosthetic alif to a fourth-pattern command
fields.contrast_or_transfer: a command form against the governed imperfect it was derived from, differing by the presence of the prefix; a prosthetic connecting alif against a pattern hamza that belongs to the word
fields.intermediate_explanation: put the verb into the third mood; remove the person prefix; test whether the residue begins with a vowelless consonant
fields.prerequisite_statement: the third mood and its exponents; the prohibitive negator and its construction; identification of derived verb patterns, in particular the fourth
fields.recognition_cue: a verb form with no person prefix opening with a plain alif that carries a vowel; the same stem shape as the governed imperfect once the prefix is stripped; a derived-form command opening with a written hamza rather than a plain alif
fields.tutor_destination: supports staged derivation drills where each intermediate step is checked, prosthetic-vowel drills, and polarity drills where the negative form must switch construction rather than shape
fields.unresolved_notice: the inflectional status of the command form is a standing school dispute and is stated here as settled; school-dependent: the negative-clause alternation is presented as a free choice, whereas the tradition records a preference between the two readings that this lesson does not attribute

fields.advanced_explanation: the subjunctive requires the causal reading and a preceding pure request or negation; the apodosis connective is required only when the apodosis cannot stand as an apocopated verb clause; the coordinating reading requires two coordinated elements of the same syntactic type
fields.beginner_explanation: Presents a single-letter connective proclitic as a five-way ambiguous element, contrasts it with the neutral connective that carries no ordering, and ties one of its readings to a mood change on the verb that follows.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: Leaving the following verb in the indicative after the causal reading.; Treating this connective as interchangeable with the neutral coordinating particle.
fields.contrast_or_transfer: this connective against the neutral coordinating particle; the causal reading with subjunctive against the coordinating reading whose mood is inherited from context
fields.intermediate_explanation: identify what precedes the connective: a clause, a request, a negation, a conditional protasis, or nothing; inspect the mood exponent on any following imperfect verb; if a conditional protasis precedes, test whether the apodosis is of a type that forces the connective
fields.prerequisite_statement: coordination; the three moods of the imperfect and their exponents; conditional particles and apocopated verbs
fields.recognition_cue: two eventive predicates in narrative succession with no gap between them, indicating the coordinating reading; a request-type or negative clause before the connective together with a subjunctive exponent on the following imperfect verb, indicating the causal reading; a conditional protasis before the connective and an apodosis that cannot itself be an apocopated verb clause, indicating the apodosis connective
fields.tutor_destination: high with care + function identification and mood selection drill well, but several of the lesson's own token labels would need correction before use as answer keys
fields.unresolved_notice: accompaniment versus coordination is disputed per occurrence and depends on whether the verb can take the noun as an argument; the syntactic category of the surprise element is a classical dispute among grammarians (adverb of place, adverb of time, or particle); the lesson does not raise it

fields.advanced_explanation: the preceding consonant carries the matching short vowel; the carrier itself carries no mark; the text is vocalized, since the whole test is stated over marks
fields.beginner_explanation: Teaches that each short vowel has a long counterpart formed by a matching carrier letter, that length is contrastive, and that two of the three carriers are graphemically identical with consonants, so the learner must be able to tell a carrier from a consonantal radical. It also introduces the word-final variant spelling of long a.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: reading every wow-letter or yaa as a vowel, or conversely as a consonant, without checking marks; pronouncing the word-final variant spelling of long a as long i because it looks like a yaa
fields.contrast_or_transfer: short against long vowel in otherwise identical consonant frames; a carrier wow-letter or yaa against a consonantal one
fields.intermediate_explanation: on meeting one of the three carrier graphemes, look one letter to its right: if that consonant carries the matching short vowel and the carrier itself carries no mark, read a long vowel; if the candidate carrier carries its own vowel mark, read it as a consonant instead; hold a long vowel roughly twice the duration of its short counterpart
fields.prerequisite_statement: the three short-vowel marks and their placement; the vowellessness mark; the consonant inventory and positional forms
fields.recognition_cue: an unmarked alif immediately after a consonant carrying the a-mark; an unmarked wow-letter immediately after a consonant carrying the u-mark; an unmarked yaa immediately after a consonant carrying the i-mark
fields.tutor_destination: high - the carrier test and minimal-pair discrimination are closed-set and auto-gradable
fields.unresolved_notice: the inflectional status of the command form is a standing school dispute and is stated here as settled; the membership of the masculine-with-tied-taa set is lexical and disputed at the margins

fields.advanced_explanation: the test presupposes that the intended sense of the verb is fixed first; the transitivising effect of the augmented pattern is described as frequent, not automatic; alternating verbs must be checked against usage rather than class membership
fields.beginner_explanation: Separates verbs that license a direct object from those that do not, gives a test for deciding which a verb is, and shows that an augmented pattern can turn a non-licensing verb into a licensing one.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: placing a bare accusative noun after a verb that selects a preposition; treating the goal noun of a motion verb as its direct object
fields.contrast_or_transfer: object in the accusative versus prepositional complement in the genitive; base pattern versus causative augmented pattern of the same root
fields.intermediate_explanation: take the verb; attempt an accusative noun as its complement; if that fails, look for the preposition the verb selects
fields.prerequisite_statement: direct object and the accusative from the previous lesson; prepositions and the genitive; the notion of derived verb patterns
fields.recognition_cue: an accusative noun following the verb with the agent separately expressed indicates object-licensing; a preposition immediately after the verb, with a genitive noun, indicates a prepositional complement rather than an object; an augmented causative pattern on a normally non-licensing root predicts an object
fields.tutor_destination: drills should present the same root in base and causative patterns and require the learner to supply or withhold an object accordingly
fields.unresolved_notice: school-dependent: an accusative noun after a motion or entry verb is analysed by different authorities as a true object, as an adverbial of place, or as an accusative after a dropped preposition, and this lesson does not attribute the choice it makes; the inflectional status of the command form is a standing school dispute and is stated here as settled

fields.advanced_explanation: a core recoverable from the surface; the template must be one of the inventoried patterns; the generated word must be checked against attestation rather than assumed
fields.beginner_explanation: Develops the core-and-template mechanism introduced earlier into a general word-building system, presenting the placeholder notation, a template inventory keyed to function classes, and the use of the system to predict the meaning of unseen words.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: counting a template's augment among the core consonants; assuming every word rests on a three-consonant core
fields.contrast_or_transfer: core letters versus template letters in the same surface word; two words sharing a core but differing in template and therefore in function
fields.intermediate_explanation: identify the core by removing letters that a matched template accounts for; read the function class off the template rather than off the meaning; to generate, choose a core, choose a template, fill the slots in order
fields.prerequisite_statement: L1.M2.03 first exposure to core and template; ability to read vowelled derived forms; triliteral root extraction
fields.recognition_cue: the same consonants recurring in order across several words with different vowel patterns; a surface form matching a listed template slot mapping; an initial م or a long vowel in a position the template assigns to an augment
fields.tutor_destination: strong for a fill-the-template drill and for a which-letters-are-core drill; the generation exercise needs an attestation check attached or it teaches invention
fields.unresolved_notice: school-dependent: several of the cited scriptural accusatives are analysed variously as state, as reinforcing verbal noun, or as specification, and the lesson presents one reading without attribution; school-dependent: the conventional listing of the addition inventory and whether hamza and long alif count as two members

fields.advanced_explanation: the causative reading presupposes an identifiable base predicate for the same root; the valency-increase reading presupposes that the base predicate is intransitive; the masdar default assumes a sound triliteral root
fields.beginner_explanation: Introduces the first augmented pattern, whose only formal augment is gemination of the second radical, and licenses three semantic effects for it. It also fixes the pattern's imperfect prefix vowel and its default masdar family.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: Writing the imperfect with a on the subject prefix.; Overlooking the gemination and reading the stem as the unaugmented baseline.
fields.contrast_or_transfer: geminated-middle pattern against the unaugmented baseline; causative reading against intensive reading for the same stem
fields.intermediate_explanation: locate the geminated consonant and count it as a single radical when extracting the root; choose among the licensed readings by inspecting the object and the base sense; build the masdar by prefixing تَـ and lengthening the position before the final radical
fields.prerequisite_statement: the unaugmented triliteral baseline and its vowel classes; root extraction; reading of shadda and full diacritics
fields.recognition_cue: a shadda sits on the second radical and on no other position of the stem; the imperfect shows u on the subject prefix together with i before the final radical; three distinct radicals remain recoverable once the geminate is counted as one consonant
fields.tutor_destination: strong for prefix-vowel drills and for verb-to-masdar drills; weaker for reading selection, which the lesson leaves to context without a decision procedure
fields.unresolved_notice: analysis-dependent: whether fixed accusative interjections are genuinely this construction with a deleted governor, or lexicalized adverbials, is a choice among analyses; analysis-dependent: reconstructed pre-alternation forms are posited, not attested

fields.advanced_explanation: a triliteral core recoverable from the surface; a known template inventory to match against; place versus time reading inside the same م-template is not decided by the template alone and the lesson does not raise the distinction
fields.beginner_explanation: Introduces the word-form discipline by contrast with the sentence discipline, then demonstrates the consonantal-core-plus-template mechanism through one root's word family, including the template that commonly yields a noun of place.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: answering a word-build question with a sentence-function analysis, or the reverse; counting a template's initial م among the core consonants
fields.contrast_or_transfer: a build question versus a sentence-function question; core letters versus template letters, specifically the initial م
fields.intermediate_explanation: remove template material and read off the consonantal core; fit the core into a named template and predict the function class from the template; when a question is about build, answer with the word-form discipline; when it is about the ending in a sentence, answer with the sentence discipline
fields.prerequisite_statement: the discipline split introduced in L1.M2.01; ability to read vowelled derived forms; L1.M2.03 first exposure to core and template
fields.recognition_cue: a set of words whose consonants recur in the same order under different vowel patterns; an initial م standing before three surviving consonants that fill the template's slots; a residual letter that has no slot in the core once the template is matched
fields.tutor_destination: supports a build-from-core drill and a which-letters-are-core drill, with the caution that the transfer item invites shape-based guessing

fields.advanced_explanation: the text is vocalized, since both marks are routinely omitted in ordinary prose; the geminated consonant is not word-initial, so that its first half has a syllable to close; gemination introduced by the definite article belongs to the clitic boundary, not to the noun's stem
fields.beginner_explanation: Introduces the two marks that are not vowels: the mark of vowellessness, which closes a syllable, and the gemination mark, which doubles a consonant. The learner is taught to keep the two apart visually and to understand gemination as two consonant slots rather than one heavier letter.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: mistaking one mark for the other because both are small superscript signs; pronouncing a geminated consonant once
fields.contrast_or_transfer: the hollow circle against the w-shaped mark; single against doubled consonant in otherwise identical words
fields.intermediate_explanation: on meeting the circle, pronounce the consonant and move straight to the next sound without inserting any vowel; on meeting the gemination mark, expand it into two consonant slots and attach the accompanying vowel to the second slot; before treating gemination as part of the stem, check whether it stands right after the definite article and is therefore assimilatory
fields.prerequisite_statement: the three short-vowel marks; the consonant inventory and positional forms; the three short-vowel marks and their placement
fields.recognition_cue: a hollow circle above a consonant, versus a small w-shaped mark; a short-vowel mark stacked above or below the gemination mark; a gemination mark on the first consonant of a noun standing immediately after the definite article, which signals assimilation rather than lexical doubling
fields.tutor_destination: high - mark identification, gemination expansion, and transliteration are all mechanical and auto-gradable
fields.unresolved_notice: the inflectional status of the command form is a standing school dispute and is stated here as settled; the categorial and positional analysis of the three non-particle condition words is analysis-dependent

fields.advanced_explanation: the categorial tests must be applied in order because later tests presuppose earlier exclusions; elision applies only when a word precedes within the same utterance; the vowel rule for the connecting alif is stated for commands of triliteral verbs
fields.beginner_explanation: Splits word-initial alif into two categories according to whether its glottal onset survives inside connected speech, and supplies a category-based decision procedure keyed to word class, verb length and a memorised closed noun list. Closes with a note that in unpointed writing the two categories are not distinguishable from the orthography alone.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: pronouncing a connecting hamza in the middle of an utterance; assigning the same hamza type to commands of triliteral and of derived verbs
fields.contrast_or_transfer: a triliteral command against a fourth-pattern command, differing in hamza type; a member of the closed noun list against an ordinary noun
fields.intermediate_explanation: ask whether the word is the definite article; ask whether it belongs to the closed noun list; for a perfect verb, count the letters of the pattern
fields.prerequisite_statement: command derivation and the prosthetic alif from the preceding lesson; derived verb patterns and their letter counts; the definite article as a prefixed element
fields.recognition_cue: in pointed text, the presence or absence of the hamza mark on the initial alif; membership of the word in one of the listed categories, applied in order; the letter count and derived pattern of a perfect verb
fields.tutor_destination: supports sorting drills over mixed word lists, connected-reading drills where the elision must actually be performed, and closed-list recall drills
fields.unresolved_notice: analysis-dependent: reconstructed pre-alternation forms are posited, not attested; rival analyses: shortened suffixed past as relocation plus deletion versus long-vowel shortening

fields.advanced_explanation: the tied grapheme is licensed only in word-final position; the t realization requires either a pronounced case ending or a following annexed word; masculine nouns carrying the tied grapheme
fields.beginner_explanation: Separates the two word-final spellings of the same consonant: the tied grapheme, restricted to word-final position and normally marking feminine gender, and the open grapheme, used where the consonant is a root letter, a subject suffix, or part of a plural pattern. It also teaches the context-dependent realization of the tied grapheme and both classes of exception to the gender inference.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: writing the tied grapheme without its dots, producing a different letter; writing the tied grapheme in the middle of a word
fields.contrast_or_transfer: tied against open grapheme; the tied grapheme against the undotted laryngeal letter it resembles
fields.intermediate_explanation: decide the grapheme by asking whether the final consonant belongs to the stem or is an added gender marker; for pronunciation, check whether the word stands in pause or is followed by an ending or an annexed noun; derive the feminine of an adjective by suffixing the tied grapheme to the masculine
fields.prerequisite_statement: the letter inventory and dot signatures; positional letter forms; the short-vowel marks and nunation
fields.recognition_cue: a laryngeal-shaped grapheme carrying two dots and standing only at the end of a word; two dots over a normally-connecting taa skeleton anywhere in the word; an audible t before an annexed noun or before a pronounced case ending
fields.tutor_destination: high - grapheme choice, gender labelling and feminine derivation are all closed-set and auto-gradable
fields.unresolved_notice: what licenses nominative on the two slots is disputed among grammarians and is not addressed; analysis-dependent: the traditional account treats the attached ending itself as the فاعل, which is not the same claim as an optional-pronoun/pro-drop account

fields.advanced_explanation: the marker-based test assumes a fully declinable common noun; the enumeration is presented as covering the whole definiteness space; the topic/comment default is stated for the unmarked construction
fields.beginner_explanation: Treats definiteness as a system in its own right: it separates definite from indefinite nominals, enumerates the sources from which definiteness comes, names the surface markers, and connects the distinction back to the default definiteness of the two slots of the noun-initial sentence.
fields.common_error_warning: watch out: reading any nunated nominal as indefinite; reading any nominal without the article as indefinite
fields.contrast_or_transfer: specific versus non-specific reference for the same lexeme; article-marked definiteness versus inherited definiteness through annexation
fields.intermediate_explanation: check the nominal against each definiteness source in turn; if none applies, classify the nominal as indefinite; when constructing a noun-initial sentence, select a definite topic and an indefinite comment
fields.prerequisite_statement: the article and nunation as surface elements; pronominal suffixes and their attachment; the two slots of the noun-initial sentence
fields.recognition_cue: presence of the definite article on the nominal; nunation on the ending, in the absence of any other definiteness source; membership in a closed class (pronoun, demonstrative, relative noun)
fields.tutor_destination: high — source attribution is a clean, checkable task, and the nunated proper name is an ideal item for eliciting the lesson's own weakest generalisation
fields.unresolved_notice: analysis-dependent: the traditional account treats the attached ending itself as the فاعل, which is not the same claim as an optional-pronoun/pro-drop account; analysis-dependent: whether an attached object pronoun is itself the object or occupies an accusative position is stated differently in traditional and modern descriptions
